President Trump made a brief appearance on Tuesday at the finals of the Patriot Games, the three-day teen athletics tournament his administration helped organize as part of America’s 250th anniversary celebrations.

The administration was likely hoping for a better turnout than its Great American State Fair, which suffered widespread mockery online and poor attendance.

The Republican arrived Tuesday evening on a rainy day in Cleveland to take in the competition, which was being held at the SPIRE Academy sports boarding school, where organizers reportedly again struggled to fill seats.

He entered the arena in a shower of sparklers alongside ESPN’s Pat McAfee, leading a group of competitors who had battled against delegations representing all 50 states and various U.S. territories and tribal nations to make it to the final.

For a Donald Trump production, the president was relatively muted, giving a brief interview with ESPN’s Laura Rutledge about how he was “very proud” of the athletes and parents in the room while praising their “love for our country.” Naturally, he also did his signature shimmy dance move as confetti fell on the winners.

open image in gallery President Trump does his signature dance move at the Tuesday-night finals of the Patriot Games ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Competitors hailed from all 50 states, plus U.S. territories and tribal nations ( Reuters )

open image in gallery As with other Trump-inspired America’s 250th anniversary events, the Patriot Games reportedly struggled to draw large crowds ( Reuters )

open image in gallery The president has often mixed sports and politics, throwing his own events such as the White House UFC fight and attending high-profile finals in the World Cup and NBA ( Reuters )

The upbeat atmosphere masked some of the questions that have swirled around the event.

Student athletes, who won entrance to the games based on patriotic video submissions rather than qualifying competition, told The Washington Post they were unnerved to see those chosen to compete were almost entirely white, despite the country’s wide diversity.

“It’s a little startling,” one player said. “This is supposed to be the best high school athletes. … It just feels a little concerning not to see very many different types of people.”

Other critics noted multiple states had non-residents representing them.

open image in gallery Competitors were chosen after submitting video essays, rather than competing athletically to qualify ( Getty )

open image in gallery The president takes in the festivities with ESPN’s Pat McAfee (left) and Senator Bernie Moreno (R-OH) (right) ( Getty )

open image in gallery Winners of the Patriot Games shared a $250,000 prize pool of scholarship funds ( Getty )

open image in gallery The president traveled to Ohio as another Trump trip dominated the headlines: a July flight out of Turkey where the president allegedly swapped planes in secret on his way home ( Getty )

Though the president didn’t appear to comment on it at the games, another key thread was gender and athletics.

The White House has cracked down on federally supported schools that allow transgender people to compete in leagues matching their gender identity, and the president pledged last year that “there will be no men playing in women’s sports” at the games.

For their part, many of the student competitors seemed to be enjoying themselves, chanting “USA!” and cheering the president during the finals.

Two Democratic senators are demanding answers from a pair of Belgian firms regarding an 18-carat gold ring set with 321 diamonds that was presented to President Donald Trump just weeks prior to the U.S. granting Europe's diamond industry an exemption from newly imposed tariffs.

In an August 10 letter addressed to the Antwerp World Diamond Centre and David Gotlib Luxury Cufflinks, Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut cautioned that the gift creates significant legal concerns under U.S. federal bribery statutes and could subject the businesses to potential criminal penalties.

"At best, your (gift to) ... President Trump amidst high-stakes tariff decisions creates the glaring appearance of impropriety. At worst, it reinforces that foreign corporate special interests can … buy lucrative tariff exemptions simply by showering President Trump with shiny gifts," they wrote in the letter.

According to the senators, the ring—handcrafted by David Gotlib—was presented to the U.S. ambassador in Belgium on June 28 by the president of the Antwerp World Diamond Centre as a gift for Trump to honor the 250th anniversary of the U.S.

Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut cautioned that the gift creates significant legal concerns ( Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images )

On July 24, the Trump administration officially exempted natural European diamonds from new Section 301 tariffs, reinstating the Belgian diamond industry's prior zero-percent tariff access.

The senators directed the firms to answer a list of inquiries by August 24, including the precise financial value of the ring, the entity that paid for it, and any discussions about tariffs held with the Trump administration prior to the exemption announcement. News reports have placed the ring's value at $25,000 to $35,000.

While Republicans currently maintain control over both houses of Congress, Democrats are developing a comprehensive investigative strategy targeting corporations and financial institutions surrounding Trump if they return to power following the congressional elections in November.

The White House denied granting any favors to special interest groups. A spokesman said the choice to exempt the diamond sector merely upheld the Trump administration's prior agreement to extend preferential treatment for diamonds under the U.S.-European Union trade agreement concluded in Scotland last July.

An administration official noted that the diamond ring remains federal property, adding that if the president intends to retain it, he must pay the government the full market price for the item.

Donald Trump is blocking two federal health insurance programs that serve low-income Americans from funding gender-affirming healthcare for transgender youth, the administration’s latest effort to deny affirming care to young trans people as part of a government-wide campaign against trans Americans.

The new rule prohibits Medicaid funds from being used to provide care to trans youth under 18, despite recommendations from their own physicians. It also blocks Children’s Health Insurance Program funds from covering care for trans youth under 19.

The rule, which is expected to face legal challenges, specifically bars those programs from supporting pharmaceutical intervention, including hormone treatments, and affirming surgeries, which are exceedingly rare and only under extraordinarily limited circumstances. Medicaid and the Children’s Health Insurance Program benefits will still be available to support mental health services for trans youth.

“The federal government is putting up barriers between parents and their ability to make the best medical decisions for their children,” according to Josh Rovenger, legal director of GLBTQ Legal Advocates & Defenders. “That should be chilling to every American.”

With the new rule, the administration is “once again holding vital healthcare funding hostage — pressuring states and providers to fall in line with its political agenda, not sound medicine,” Rovenger said.

open image in gallery In a move supported by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Medicaid chief Mehmet Oz, Donald Trump’s administration is blocking two federal health insurance programs that serve low-income Americans from funding gender-affirming healthcare for transgender youth ( AFP/Getty )

After a public comment period that received more than 35,000 responses, the president announced the rule change on Truth Social to declare that Medicaid “will NO LONGER fund gender transition surgeries and hormones for minors.”

“We are not going to pay for our innocent children to undergo these barbaric surgeries and practices, which result in unthinkable and irreversible harm to their young bodies,” Trump wrote Tuesday. “Just think about all of the young, innocent, and perhaps confused children who will be spared!”

He then baselessly accused the “Dumocrat Party” of encouraging children to “chop off their reproductive organs before they are old enough to vote.”

In a statement, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said the government is “ending federal taxpayer funding for sex-rejecting procedures on children.”

“Children deserve our protection, not experimental interventions that pose serious risks and convey no proven benefits,” added Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services

“By cutting off federal funds for these sex-rejecting procedures, we’re following the science, saving taxpayer dollars, and, most importantly, protecting children from potentially irreversible harm so they can truly flourish,” he added.

Major medical organizations including the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American Medical Association, the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and the American Counseling Association, among others, agree that affirming care is clinically appropriate for trans youth experiencing gender dysphoria.

“This rule is a dangerous restriction on doctor-prescribed health care,” said Rodrigo Heng-Lehtinen, senior vice president of public engagement campaigns at The Trevor Project.

“Personal medical decisions should be made by individual patients, their doctors, and their families — not by a one-size-fits-all mandate from the federal government,” he said.

open image in gallery The Trump administration has implemented a government-wide effort targeting trans Americans, from limiting access to affirming healthcare coverage to seeking to remove them from the military ( AFP/Getty )

The organization’s 2022 peer-reviewed study determined that gender-affirming hormone therapy was significantly related to lower rates of depression, suicidal thoughts, and suicide attempts among trans and nonbinary young people.

One week after his inauguration, Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to rescind policies that support or acknowledge gender-affirming healthcare for trans Americans.

He also issued an executive order effectively ending federal recognition of trans people across the government, forming the basis for several other orders focused exclusively on trans people, their healthcare and whether they can serve in the U.S. military or play on women’s sports teams.

Earlier this year, the Federal Trade Commission sued the World Professional Association for Transgender Health, alleging the group made deceptive claims about gender-affirming care for minors and that its members profited off them.

“The Trump administration is terrorizing trans youth and their families with these kinds of actions, and it has to stop,” said Kelley Robinson, president of the Human Rights Campaign, the nation’s largest LGBTQ+ civil rights group.

Under the new rule, current Medicaid and CHIP patients receiving hormone therapy can continue to receive coverage for up to six more months. The rule appears to be effective immediately for coverage for puberty blockers and surgeries.

Police are investigating the death of a woman who was found dead in her tent at a popular techno festival in Norfolk over the weekend.

The woman, who has not been publicly identified, was found unconscious in a tent on a campsite on the last day of Houghton festival at Houghton Hall in north Norfolk.

The hall is home to David Cholmondeley, the 7th Marquess of Cholmondeley, and his wife Rose Hanbury, friends of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

The woman was pronounced dead at the scene on Sunday, despite efforts by an on-site medical team to save her.

Police are treating her death as unexplained while they await the results of a post-mortem examination, but they say they do not believe there were any suspicious circumstances.

A spokesman for the festival said: “We are deeply saddened to confirm that a person has passed away at Houghton 2026.

“Our thoughts are entirely with their family and loved ones at this difficult time.

“We are grateful to our onsite medical team, event response team and to Norfolk Constabulary, who all responded immediately.

“We continue to work closely with the relevant authorities to support in any way we can with their investigations.”

open image in gallery The festival was at Houghton Hall, owned by Rose Hanbury and David Cholmondeley, friends of Prince William and Kate ( Getty )

A police spokeswoman said they were investigating and that the woman’s next of kin had been informed.

Houghton festival, which draws 10,000-strong crowds, is known for its house and techno music, played around the clock in the 1,000-acre grounds.

The festival, which has been running at the estate every year since 2017, is the UK’s only 24-hour music festival. Tickets cost between £280 and £330.

Houghton Hall, built in the 1720s for Britain’s first prime minister, Sir Robert Walpole, is set in extensive parkland near William and Kate’s country retreat at Sandringham.

In 2023 the Princess of Wales attended the festival, accompanied by security guards and a group of friends.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register or login to an existing telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football launched on August 10, 2026. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.

How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games. Last season Mark Flekken came out on top with 153 saves for Brentford, so it will be interesting to see how Caoimhin Kelleher gets on this season.



What counts as a Save?



A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

For an exhaustive list of how to score Telegraph Fantasy Football points, take a look at our Game Guidelines.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: Jets' Stiggers in hospital after collapsing during practice
Sports.content:
New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers collapsed during a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Stiggers regained consciousness and was talking on the field before being taken to hospital; Jets head coach Aaron Glenn later gave a positive update on Stiggers' condition

New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers was taken to a hospital by ambulance after he briefly lost consciousness during a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Tuesday.

Jets coach Aaron Glenn said the 24-year-old was conscious and talking on the field before being put on a stretcher and taken for further examination. There was no immediate word on Stiggers' condition, but Glenn indicated the cornerback was doing okay.

"He was able to talk and I want to make sure I go and see him after this, just to make sure I'm good with everything," Glenn said. "But for the most part, he was good."

The Jets and Buccaneers were in the middle of special-teams drills when Glenn said Stiggers came to the sideline.

"He actually fell out," Glenn said. "The good thing is, he was conscious. Our guys did a hell of a job, just like most medical staffs around this league do in situations like that, and they took the necessary steps just to make sure that we do everything we can to be on board when it comes to those situations."

It was a somewhat scary scene, though, as several Jets team-mates took a knee near the sideline and some formed a prayer circle.

After several minutes, Stiggers was placed on a stretcher with what appeared to be an IV and loaded into the ambulance as fans seated near the area clapped in support.

"It was very sad, very emotional," Jets running back Breece Hall said. "You get on your knee and say a prayer for him and hope he's okay."

Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips added: "What's been shared to us is things are on the up and up."

Practice resumed after being halted for more than 10 minutes while Stiggers was being attended to.

Stiggers was earlier involved in one of the handful of chippy moments during the practice when he had his helmet flung down the field by a Buccaneers player after players on both teams scuffled.

Stiggers is entering his third season with the Jets after being a fifth-round draft pick in 2024. He was one of that draft's feelgood stories because he had no college football experience and was the first player drafted directly from the CFL, where he played for the Toronto Argonauts, since Miami took Jermaine Haley in 1999.

In 29 games, including five starts, with New York, Stiggers has 35 tackles, two fumble recoveries and three passes defended. He is also one of the Jets' top special teams players.

Sports.title: Super Giants rout SunRisers to move to cusp of Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Manchester Super Giants routed SunRisers Leeds to all but seal their place in The Hundred men's eliminator and leave their opponents at risk of being knocked out.

The Super Giants restricted SunRisers to 127 all out from their 100 balls as England's Gus Atkinson (3-30) and Sonny Baker (2-22) led the way, before opening batters Tim Seifert (80no from 40) and Paul Walter (44no from 28) knocked off the target with 33 balls to spare.

The huge margin of victory saw the Super Giants move above SunRisers into second place in the group table, with both sides on 20 points but Manchester having edged ahead on net run-rate. The result also confirmed Trent Rockets' place in Sunday's final as table-toppers.

Super Giants and SunRisers occupy the positions that would see them meet in Friday's eliminator for a place in the final, but can still technically be caught by fourth-placed MI London and fifth-placed Welsh Fire, who go into their final group-stage matches on Wednesday on 16 points, meaning wins would take them to 20 points.

While Welsh Fire's negative net run-rate of -1.001 makes it almost impossible they could catch either Super Giants or SunRisers when they face London Spirit, a big win for MI London away to Birmingham Phoenix could feasibly lift them into second or third.

Welsh Fire's clash with London Spirit is live on Sky Sports from 3pm, with MI London's trip to Edgbaston following at 6.30pm.

Asked whether he knew the net run-rate permutations ahead of the chase, Seifert, the Match Hero, said: "I had no idea, to be honest. A message got run out when we needed about 50 runs and that's when we looked to put the pedal down.

"We've got a great side and it's a great environment to play in. It's my first time playing in The Hundred and it's a great tournament to be involved in. It's great to be playing in front of good crowds in amazing stadiums."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Seifert hammered three sixes in a row!

Seifert bludgeoned his third fifty in as many knocks and struck seven sixes, while Walter thumped three maximums of his own as the SunRisers' attack was put to the sword.

The Super Giants' opening pair were electric but the foundations for a stunning win were laid by their bowlers, who clawed things back after Ryan Rickelton and Mitchell Marsh had made a rapid start for the visitors, posting 42 from 22 balls before Rickelton became the first of Atkinson's three victims.

Marsh (32 from 23), the tournament's leading run-scorer, continued his fine form, but when he was snaffled at extra cover off Noor Ahmad, the visitors lost their way.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A spectator was caught knitting at The Hundred!

Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence and Matthew Revis all fell cheaply and when Zak Crawley's stuttering innings of 31 from 28 was ended by Baker, the wheels came off.

SunRisers could only muster 14 runs from the final 14 balls of the innings, for the loss of four wickets. Expensive earlier in the piece, Atkinson was exceptional, taking two wickets and conceding just three runs from the final five.

Sports.title: SunRisers beat Super Giants to reach Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Reigning champions SunRisers Leeds snatched a spot in the women's Hundred eliminator by beating Manchester Super Giants by 41 runs in a winner-takes-all game at Old Trafford.

In a shoot-out for the final place in the top three, Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off 36 balls helped Leeds leapfrog their opponents and set up an eliminator clash against Southern Brave.

The Australian all-rounder hit nine boundaries, including three sixes, as the visitors posted 166-4 after being put in to bat.

Visiting spinner Jess Jonassen took 3-21, while Deepti Sharma and Sutherland claimed two wickets apiece, as Manchester were restricted to 125-8 in reply and exited the competition after slipping to fourth place in the standings.

Second-placed Leeds will continue their title defence against Southern Brave on Friday at The Oval, with table-topping Trent Rockets awaiting the winner in Sunday's final at Lord's.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UNBELIEVABLE athletic fielding from SunRisers' Phoebe Litchfield to prevent a six

Sutherland, the Match Hero, said: "It's the beauty of being an all-rounder, you're in the game all the time, and I love competing, especially in a match we were calling a final. We had to win and it was nice to do a job for the team."

Phoebe Litchfield made her intentions clear after SunRisers were asked to bat, the Aussie opener racing to 27 from 12 deliveries to leapfrog Sophia Dunkley at the top of the competition's run-scoring chart.

An electrifying innings was brought to a halt after Litchfield miscued a drag down from Mady Villiers but Bryony Smith (17 off 16) and Lauren Winfield-Hill (20 off 15) kept the scoreboard ticking.

Sports.title: Levy goes up against Spurs owners to buy London's NBA Europe team
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy is vying with a consortium including current Spurs' owners, the Lewis family, to buy NBA Europe's London-based team.

Sky News has revealed that the Lewises are part of a consortium, led by the Checketts family, which has submitted an offer as part of the ongoing auction.

The Checketts have owned or invested in professional sports franchises including Major League Soccer team Real Salt Lake and the NHL's St Louis Blues.

The third leg of the consortium is the Eccles family, who own shares in Burnley FC and Spanish side Espanyol along with the Checketts.

Sky News has previously reported Levy's involvement in a consortium including Liberty Global and MSP Sports Capital, a former backer of McLaren Racing, which is also among the contenders for the NBA London team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol examines where Daniel Levy was 'pushed' out of his role as Spurs chairman

London has rapidly become most highly prized of the 12 new NBA Europe outfits, with other teams based in cities such as Berlin, Manchester, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome.

The NBA wants to generate billions of dollars by selling the rights to the teams, with the first transactions expected in the coming weeks.

Wealthy US families and investors are increasingly buying stakes in sports teams in the UK, especially in football.

Levy left his role as Spurs executive chairman in September 2025 after nearly 25 years in the job.

While the official communication from Spurs and Levy was that he had "stepped down" from the role, it was widely understood that the decision was taken out of his hands.

Sports.title: Floodlights to be on throughout Hundred matches for solar eclipse
Sports.content:
Floodlights will be turned on throughout games in The Hundred on Wednesday due to the solar eclipse.

Up to 90 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon during the eclipse, which will occur between 6.17pm and 8.06pm, peaking shortly after 7pm.

It will be the first partial solar eclipse for 27 years and will be visible across Europe, with some places experiencing a total eclipse, where the sun, moon and earth all line up in space.

The light will dim, the temperature will drop and the wind may change direction as the sun disappears behind the moon. After a few minutes the sun will reappear and daylight will return.

There are four games in The Hundred taking place on Wednesday, all of them live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Seifert & Walter hit 10 HUGE sixes in Super Giants win

Welsh Fire women face London Spirit women at 11.30am in Cardiff, followed by the men's game at 3pm. Birmingham Phoenix women host MI London at Edgbaston from 3pm before the men's teams play each other at 6.30pm.

In anticipation for the solar eclipse, organisers will keep floodlights on throughout all four matches and additional messaging will be issued to fans.

Experts have warned that only special solar eclipse glasses that are certified for the safest eye protection should be used to view the eclipse.

Floodlights will be on 'plenty early' at Kempton

Kempton is all set to stage racing on Wednesday during the solar eclipse.

While the twilight meeting at Ffos Las will begin and end earlier than originally scheduled to ensure all six races take place in daylight, there are no such issues at Kempton due to the floodlights that are in place at the Sunbury circuit.

Image: The floodlights will also be turned on at Kempton race course

The eclipse is expected to occur between 7.02pm and 7.16pm and Kempton has races scheduled to take place at 7pm and 7.30pm.

Kempton's clerk of the course Barney Clifford said: "The last one was nearly 30 years ago so I wasn't quite at Kempton then. I remember it but there were no floodlights in those days!

"I'm going to put the floodlights on early doors. I know they have predicted a time for it but you don't quite know how much of the sun is going to be covered and for what race so we'll have the lights on plenty early enough."

Sports.title: Inter Milan in talks over Spurs and England defender Spence
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Inter Milan over the sale of Djed Spence.

Inter believe a total package of £30m could be enough to get a deal done and Spurs are understood to be willing to sell if they receive an acceptable offer.

Spence's opportunities could be limited at Spurs this season with Destiny Udogie and Andy Robertson also competing for the left-back position and the ever-present Pedro Porro the clear first choice on the right.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Spence's brilliant cameo off the bench against Norway, England fans Ben Cipolla and Dan Lucas came up with a new song for the full-back titled 'Total Eclipse of Djed Spence'

Inter want to bring in a new player who can operate as a wing-back.

Spence has been high on their list all summer and Inter are now turning their attention to the Spurs man after struggling to strike a deal for Al Ittihad's Moussa Diaby.

De Zerbi: Spurs aren't done in the transfer window

Roberto de Zerbi maintains Tottenham are "not finished yet" in the transfer market as they look to build a competitive Premier League squad again.

Having only avoided relegation on the final day of last season, Spurs have spent already spent around £237m - with the club's transfer record broken twice in deals for Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tottenham Hotspur head coach Roberto De Zerbi tells the Men in Blazers Network that he expects to make more signings this summer (Pictures: Men in Blazers Network)

Dutch defender Jan Paul van Hecke also arrived from Brighton for £52m, while Martin Dubravka, Robertson and Marcos Senesi signed on as free agents.

With Micky van de Ven having also committed his long-term future to the club, there is genuine hope Spurs will soon be challenging at the other end of the table.

"In the transfer market, we have not finished yet [with] the players who will arrive," De Zerbi said, speaking to the Men in Blazers Network.

"We are looking forward to start another season with, I don't know [different] ambitions, but with different results."

De Zerbi continued: "The club has been great because they closed [deals for] very, very important players. I think we have not finished yet.

"Okay, we spent money, but the other clubs made the same or more in the past. To compete in the Premier League, you need first [the] level of the players.

"The ambition of the owner of the club, of the board, of the people who decide behind me are very important and very high, so we have to find the condition to build a strong team, a stronger team than the last seasons, to compete again for the top of the table."

Sports.title: Unbeaten star Bow Echo in shock retirement after setback
Sports.content:
Bow Echo has been retired from racing after the shock news that George Boughey's unbeaten star has suffered a setback in training.

Having won the 2000 Guineas, the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Sussex Stakes this season, Bow Echo was being lined up for Sunday's Prix Jacques le Marois.

Announcing the surprise news on his X account, Boughey said: "It is with great disappointment that we have to announce that Bow Echo has had a setback and will be retired from racing.

"It has been the honour of a lifetime to train a horse like Bow Echo. He has given us some extraordinary days and taken everyone involved on a journey we will never forget.

"To retire unbeaten, having won the 2000 Guineas, St James's Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes says everything about what an exceptional racehorse he has been.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bow Echo and Gstaad served up a thriller in the St James's Palace Stakes on day one of Royal Ascot

"Bow Echo's remarkable story began with his owner-breeder, the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid and it is a great sadness that he was not here to see what a lifetime of breeding was able to produce.

"Bow Echo's unbelievable constitution and extraordinary ability have set him apart. We will all miss seeing him at home and on the racecourse but we are incredibly excited for his next chapter and in time, to see a new generation of his progeny on the racecourse."

This is amid a market of high prices for central-midfield players this summer, although he can play both positions.

Last season, Arsenal kept their squad together despite a big spend. They want to be ambitious again this summer - but there is an acceptance there will have to be sales.

Players like Ethan Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly would represent pure profit.

Analysis: Would Arsenal be right to sell Lewis-Skelly?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

"Pure profit" wrote Myles Lewis-Skelly on his Instagram page as Arsenal celebrated the Premier League title. Reading between the lines, it was message over his future.

Despite posing with the Premier League title in May, Lewis-Skelly had a very difficult campaign. Fully fit the whole season, he made just one Premier League start before Christmas - by the start of May he had only managed three.

Many fans felt it was right for Arsenal to move Lewis-Skelly on as the sale of an academy graduate would bring a 'pure profit' funds into the club - hence the message on Instagram.

But everything changed in May, Mikel Arteta put Lewis-Skelly in a previously unused midfield role for a crucial title run-in game against Fulham, and Arsenal got some life back into their team.

With Martin Zubimendi fading in terms of fitness and form - and Arsenal struggling against the Man City title race momentum - Lewis-Skelly was Man of the Match in the 3-0 win that put them back on track for the title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Monday Night Football, Thierry Henry analysed Myles Lewis Skelly's outstanding midfield performance against Fulham.

Lewis-Skelly did not leave the midfield for the rest of the run-in - including the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

From third choice left-back to playing in Arsenal's biggest game in 20 years, Lewis-Skelly had kick-started his Arsenal career again. But now the question marks have returned.

The £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes has threatened his role in the Arsenal midfield. The Gunners' two most expensive players are now the Brazilian and Declan Rice.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes come face-to-face for the first time after the Brazilian made his move from Newcastle to the Premier League champions.

For two midfield positions, Arsenal have Rice, Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Five does not go into two, so does something - or someone in this instance - have to give?

Ever since his breakthrough last year, Lewis-Skelly has become a fan favourite at Arsenal. He has showed his ability in both midfield and left-back - it is worth remembering he played 180 minutes in defence as Arsenal beat Real Madrid in the Champions League in 2025.

There are valid reasons for Arsenal keeping a hold on Lewis-Skelly, particularly given the amount of minutes key midfielder Rice has played over the past year.

The 27-year-old played in all but two of the Premier League, Champions League and Carabao Cup games between January 1 and the end of the season.

Image: Minutes played by Arsenal players in midfield

By the time Rice got to the World Cup, England manager Thomas Tuchel admitted the midfielder was in "a lot of pain". Rice was substituted regularly during the World Cup - something that very rarely happens in an Arsenal shirt.

The sheer amount of minutes he has played means Arsenal cannot rely on the midfielder to just carry on running through the barriers. If Rice is to be rotated more often, then that opens the door for Lewis-Skelly to continue playing.

But on the flip side, Arsenal have Zubimendi and Merino as options for Rice rotation. And with Arsenal needing to address others areas and showing a need to sell better - their record transfer sale is still Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's £35m move to Liverpool in 2017 - then Lewis-Skelly's future opens up a conundrum.

Arteta said important decisions will need to be made this summer to take the team to another level. But a popular academy graduate ends up at a Premier League rival, then that is not just an important decision - it's a controversial one.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 5: Brighton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 9th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 8th

Prospects

Last season’s final day in May featured Brighton fans and players united in celebrating qualification for the Europa Conference League despite losing 3-0 to Manchester United. Considering West Ham and Crystal Palace have won the competition since its inception, lifting that trophy becomes a target to aim for.

How realistic is that? Beyond the Thursday-Sunday schedule playing in the Conference League demands, it has been a summer of change within the ranks. James Milner did not celebrate as Europe was reached. By then he had decided he would retire. Danny Welbeck was last season’s outstanding forward for Brighton, one of the best in England, and has followed the now traditional trade route to Chelsea. Him turning 36 in November adds a note of curiosity to that transfer. Thus, the veteran class, each older than their head coach, Fabian Hürzeler, still just 33, is reduced to Pascal Gross, Lewis Dunk and the reserve goalkeeper Jason Steele. Solly March not being offered a new contract was another break from the past, a surprise to a long-serving and popular player whose injury problems counted against him.

Jan Paul van Hecke, last season’s best defender, has been sold to Tottenham for £52m, with the teenager Luka Vuskovic coming in the opposite direction. If Brighton supporters are wondering about their club’s slew of new signings then their Premier League peers will be watching as closely, such is the industry’s respect for the club’s recruitment. The Jamestown Analytics company owned by Tony Bloom, Brighton’s financier, is a football Rosetta Stone, admired and coveted. It is not, though, completely infallible; there have been a number of busts.

Fans hugely enjoyed being in the Europa League three seasons ago, reaching the last 16, but it had a deleterious effect at home, stretching resources and relations with the then manager, Roberto De Zerbi. Brighton finished a disappointing 11th. Better is hoped for this time around.

Off-field picture

Safe standing is being expanded in the South Stand of the Amex, as part of a £40m modernisation project. The work will take place during September’s extended international break and is a drive towards enhancing the atmosphere. The ownership is among the most mindful of the matchday experience in English football. For Albion fans seeking a middle ground between the posh seats and pre-match drinks in the concourse, there’s the opening of the 1901 Pub, a “hybrid traditional pub and premium matchday lounge designed for a more relaxed fan experience”. With a capacity of 660, membership starts at £173 a month.

Owner-fan relationship

There can be no doubt that Brighton’s continued success relies on the patronage and funds of Bloom. The club’s supporters are more than aware of this. Last season, Bloom’s involvement with Hearts’ chase for the Scottish title demonstrated he has wider horizons, though his key priority will always be the hometown, boyhood club. In January, “the Lizard”, as he is known in the gambling circles he made his fortune, increased his Brighton investment with a £107m loan, making for an overall loan amount of £400m. Without Bloom’s financing and his continued enthusiasm, Brighton would not be the established, model Premier League force they remain.

The manager

Hürzeler has done much growing up in public. There have been points during his two seasons when doubts circled. In the boardroom, though, Bloom and his influential chief executive, Paul Barber, have kept faith in the still youthful Bavarian. As a new, three-year contract was announced in May, Bloom referred to a “clear playing identity”. Hürzeler can be fiery. His touchline behaviour does not always meet the approval of officials and opposing coaches but he enters the season as the fifth longest-serving manager in the Premier League and will be showing off a severe hair remodelling unveiled in pre-season. Success in European football can burnish a growing reputation.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen New arrival Luka Vuskovic’s playmaking abilities from the back are highly regarded. Photograph: Matt Impey/Shutterstock

Will Tottenham rue never drawing on Vuskovic’s potential? Brighton hope so. He never played a match for Spurs but impressed on loan at Hamburg, where his reading of the game, positioning and maturity drew rave reviews. The signing of the experienced centre-back Pascal Struijk from Leeds means Vuskovic can be allowed time to develop but the Croatian’s playmaking abilities from the back may make him a long-term successor for the captain, Dunk. His fee, reported at £46m when Spurs paid £12m for him, suggests the demand for his talents. The hope and expectation is that the deal becomes regarded as a bargain.

Stat attack

The two Manchester clubs were the only sides who scored more Premier League goals than Brighton in regular play last season. The Seagulls dropped down the standings a little once counterattacks were included but they had an identical rate for open play expected goals per game as Arsenal in 2025-26. There should be no shortage of chances for whoever picks up the goalscoring baton after Danny Welbeck’s departure.

Set for a breakthrough

Patience with new arrivals is part of the Brighton doctrines, players are given latitude and opportunity to bed in. A season’s grace is often granted, and Charalampos Kostoulas showed a few flashes of his talent during the 2025-26 campaign. With Welbeck departed, there is a vacancy to lead the line. The Greece international scored a brilliant overhead kick against Bournemouth in January, and at 19, last summer’s signing from Olympiakos should receive more airtime than the two league starts he received last season. His Greek compatriot Stefanos Tzimas, back in training after an ACL rupture, can provide either competition or a partnership.

World Cup impact

When Jordan Henderson played master of ceremonies as England celebrated third place at the World Cup, he made sure Steele was given a medal for his acclaimed, appreciated work as training goalkeeper. It was an otherwise mixed summer for Albion players, with Maxim De Cuyper going furthest to the quarter-finals with Belgium. Diego Gómez was suspended for Paraguay’s historic defeat of Germany though featured in his country’s bruising exit at the hands of France. Yasin Ayari became the first Brighton player to score two World Cup goals in a game as Sweden beat Tunisia 5-1. Michael Svoboda, the summer defensive signing from Venezia, did not play a single minute for Austria.

Sports.title: Infantino’s opponents developing new framework for running world football
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s opponents are working together to produce a new framework for running world football to replace what they regard as a system of patronage that Fifa has adopted since he replaced Sepp Blatter as president 10 years ago.

Repeated calls from Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation for an independent review of Fifa’s governance have been ignored by Infantino since his plan to sell off 21% of the World Cup was made public a fortnight ago, and the rebels are now understood to have taken matters into their own hands.

A source with knowledge of the discussions told the Guardian that the three confederations are working on producing a policy document to demonstrate how the world governing body could evolve in the future.

Those involved have been empowered to ask existential questions such as what Fifa’s precise role should be, how it should be structured and what governance model should be adopted. Financial distribution among member associations is also a key consideration, particularly with an eye on how best to deploy funds from Fifa’s estimated $5bn (£3.7bn) reserves.

If Infantino refuses to engage then the new framework is likely to be adopted by a challenger at the presidential election next year, or could even serve as a template for a breakaway organisation.

After releasing a joint statement on Monday, which called for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”, Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC let it be known that they have begun preliminary discussions about organising new competitions if the standoff with Fifa’s leadership persists.

View image in fullscreen Uefa officials are meeting in Salzburg where the Super Cup takes place on Wednesday between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa. Photograph: Gintare Karpaviciute/Reuters

At present the Under-20 Women’s World Cup next month could take place without European teams, as Uefa is maintaining that its members will boycott the tournament, unless Fifa moves quickly to set up an independent review of the World Cup sell‑off debacle and provide legally binding assurances that such a move will not be repeated.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is seen as the most likely presidential challenger to Infantino at this stage – although, as he told the Guardian in June, his current focus is on being reelected as president of the North and Central American confederation next year.

It seemed significant, however, that the joint statement released on Monday contained strong echoes of a speech given by Montagliani at the Fifa congress this year in Vancouver, where he said: “Let me be frank, leadership is not about power.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Senior figures from European football are gathering in person for the first time since the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal broke, with a number of meetings expected in Salzburg – where the Uefa Super Cup final will be held on Wednesday – over the next two days.

The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, will hold talks with Nasser al-Khelaifi, the chair of European Football Clubs, aimed at reinforcing the continent’s unity in demanding a change at the top of Fifa.

Uefa continues to hold firm in its pledge to boycott Fifa competitions, having not received its desired assurances that there will be no recurrence of the issues that caused the current crisis.

Sports.title: Emery positive about Aston Villa’s outlook despite summer exits as PSG await
Sports.content:
One thing was almost instantly detectable as Unai Emery walked into a stuffy room inside the Red Bull Arena on the eve of Wednesday’s Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain. After a summer of change, Aston Villa’s manager appeared uber-relaxed, confident his team will absorb a series of headline departures. He cracked a joke about his English improving and poked fun at John McGinn, impersonating his captain while next to him on the auditorium’s top table.

Emery was in a jovial mood, then. But he was also switched on, alert to the frequency, the tone of the wave of questions at the beginning of his fourth full season in the job. “You ask about the changes of coaches and players, but McGinn is intelligent and his answer was fantastic,” Emery said with a smile. “When he arrived here [in 2018] they were in the Championship and every year since there have been changes and still the club has moved forward.

“If we compare ourselves to other clubs like Man City, Chelsea, Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool, we are competing with them. We don’t have their power … yet.”

Emery spoke with an enthusiasm that will be music to the ears of Villa supporters fretting about the size of the task on his hands. Villa have sold Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, the latter returning to PSG, for whom he could make his second debut against his former club. Villa would be tested again if Arsenal make a serious play for Ezri Konsa, who, together with Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martínez, remains on holiday after World Cup duty. Three key coaching staff have also left, including the set-piece coach, Austin MacPhee. But Emery, the beating heart of the operation, as McGinn said, is still in the building.

McGinn’s response was punchy when asked where expectations should be for the forthcoming campaign. “Similar to where it has been in the past few seasons,” he said. “I think we have consistently competed with the best in England, the best in Europe, no matter what the competition is. We will have our challenges. There is a lot of change, but when you look at other clubs around England there is a lot of change there as well: a lot of coaches changing, a lot of players changing.

“But what we still have is our main core, same manager, same methods, same desire to achieve more. A lot of people thought we had reached our ceiling a couple of seasons ago, and we proved them wrong. We have still got the same hunger and desire to go and achieve more. Our job is just to integrate the new players and try and make them believe, in the same way the players in the last few seasons have believed. I’m really excited by the sort of ‘new Aston Villa’.”

View image in fullscreen Players and staff of Aston Villa on the pitch at Stadion Salzburg. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Villa, of course, did not want to lose Rogers. Chelsea paid £117m to sign the England midfielder, two and a half years after Emery asked Villa to pay £8m to take him from Middlesbrough. The same goes for Tielemans, who after a slow start established himself as one of Emery’s undroppables. Villa signed Tielemans on a free but sold the 29‑year‑old for £35m. Digne was an equally reliable performer, taking back the left-back spot from £38m buy Ian Maatsen.

Emery knows the business but it was particularly interesting to hear him talk about the importance of the leverage Villa have gained off the back of the ride they have been on over the past few years. One of the most memorable nights was their pulsating quarter-final against PSG 16 months ago, a 3-2 second‑leg victory at Villa Park, when Gianluigi Donnarumma pulled off three superb saves to prevent Villa taking the game to extra time. Emery ended up on all fours after Willian Pacho blocked Maatsen’s goal-bound volley with 28 seconds to play.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The Premier League is the best league in the world and Aston Villa can now have better brands in the way we are,” Emery said. “I am so, so, so happy how the club is committed together with us. [I am so happy] with how we are getting better, keeping our consistency in the Premier League … the club is making a huge effort to try to be in the same direction as me. They are trying to extend Villa Park to achieve 50,000 supporters next season. We are increasing our budget through good results on the pitch, by sometimes selling some players and being consistent like we are, and as well expecting a high level, like we are more or less keeping.”

Emery, who spent two years in charge of PSG, knows how these things work. PSG are no longer just a football team but a brand: see their megastore on London’s Oxford Street. PSG’s chief executive, Victoriano Melero, has talked of PSG competing with the likes of Real Madrid on the pitch but labels like the LA Lakers and Ferrari off it.

Salzburg is the latest destination on Villa’s quest for success, with 6,000 Villa fans in tow. The stadium facade is plastered with images of McGinn and co celebrating their Europa League win in Istanbul in May. “I am feeling comfortable, happy, very demanding, even more than the last years,” Emery said. “We want more. We are not stopping here.”

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Manchester United as left-back solution
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Manchester United as a potential left-back option, with Arsenal wishing to recoup some of the £75m paid to Newcastle for Bruno Guimarães.

Chelsea, it is understood, have also been made aware of the 19-year-old’s availability. Lewis-Skelly won the Premier League under Mikel Arteta last term, but whether the west London club will make a move for him is unclear.

Lewis-Skelly, who made only five league starts and 36 appearances in all competitions in 2025-26, signed a five-year contract last summer. His prospective price is thought to be in the region of £45m.

This is within the range of finance United have spent so far this summer, after Youri Tielemans’s £35m move from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos’s arrival for £48m plus £2m of add-ons from Chelsea. United are now weighing up a move for the teenager.

Newcastle’s Lewis Hall remains of prime interest for United but, after losing Guimarães, Sandro Tonali to Tottenham, and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, the new Newcastle manager, Matthias Jaissle, is intent the 21-year-old England international does not also depart

RB Leipzig’s 28-year-old left-back David Raum is another in the position United may assess.

Chelsea have already had a busy summer in the market, having spent over £300m on a raft of new signings. Maxence Lacroix and Marco Palestra have been brought in to bolster the centre and right of the defence respectively, while Morgan Rogers became the club’s record signing at a cost of £117m.

But Xabi Alonso’s side have a hole on the left of their defence after Marc Cucurella’s £52m move to Real Madrid. The 20-year-old Jorrel Hato, who featured for the Netherlands at the World Cup, was Cucurella’s deputy at left-back.

Mason Mount missed training on Monday and Tuesday at United’s County Kildare summer training camp owing to a knock he received on a foot in Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg.
