The the 27-year-old midfielder being stood down is a precautionary measure, it is understood, and he is also set to sit out Wednesday’s penultimate pre-season friendly against Leeds at Croke Park. The game at the 81,300 capacity venue is a sell-out.

United’s final friendly before Michael Carrick’s team start the season on Saturday week at Hull is against Milan in Wroclaw on Saturday.

Sports.title: Djed Spence nears Tottenham exit with Inter in talks over £25.6m move
Sports.content:
Tottenham are prepared to allow Djed Spence to join Inter, with the England defender expected to cost around €30m (£25.6m).

Spence – who started four games at the World Cup, including the semi-final against Argentina – has fallen further down the pecking order at Spurs after the arrival of Andy Robertson from Liverpool. He signed a new four‑year contract in north London at the start of last season but is believed to be keen on joining the Italian champions, with Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro expected to be Roberto De Zerbi’s preferred full‑backs this season.

Talks are ongoing over a fee for the 26-year-old as Inter search for a replacement for Denzel Dumfries, who joined Real Madrid this summer. But personal terms are not believed to be an issue and an agreement is likely to be reached that will see Inter pay only slightly more than the £20m fee Spurs paid to sign Spence from Middlesbrough in 2022.

Inter also held talks with Tottenham over a potential move for Cristian Romero but the Argentina defender looks poised to join Atlético Madrid for a fee of €40m. They have yet to agree a fee but Romero is expected to move to La Liga despite interest from elsewhere, including the Premier League champions Arsenal.

On Monday, Spurs – who have spent almost £240m this summer on new players, including Sandro Tonali for a club‑record £92.5m, confirmed that Micky van de Ven has signed a new five-year contract. “It’s clear the direction the club wants to go in and I want to be a part of it. I’m excited about what’s to come,” the Netherlands defender said.

Crystal Palace, meanwhile, are in talks to re-sign Evann Guessand on a season-long loan from Aston Villa. The Côte d’Ivoire forward spent the second half of last season at Selhurst Park and was part of the side that won the Conference League in May, although Palace decided not to take up an option to sign him earlier in the summer. The south London club are also expected to complete deals for Anan Khalaili from Union Saint‑Gilloise for £21m and Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake for £11m.

Sports.title: ‘I am quite optimistic’: Newcastle’s Jaissle on leading club after turbulent summer
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle has been described as “fire” and a “rockstar”, but his formal “unveiling” as Newcastle’s manager revealed a rather more considered and conservative character than advertised.

At the precise moment the clock struck 3pm on Tuesday the 38‑year‑old German walked into a packed media suite at St James’ Park. Before taking his seat on the stage Jaissle, wearing a smartly understated open-necked suit complete with a silk pocket square, took a deep breath and jumped down into audience, making a point of shaking everyone’s hand. It was a courteous and classy gesture.

Once back on that podium, his evident excitement at exchanging Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli for the Premier League was tempered by the sort of realism inevitable at a club that, in Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, has just sold its three best players.

“This is now a vacuum as you call it,” Eddie Howe’s successor said in his excellent English. “They were great characters, great players, ­experienced players. Obviously we are in that transition phase. My job is to make the best out of it all. I am quite optimistic. We are ambitious, that’s the most important thing and why I decided to come here. But it will not happen overnight. I’m pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now.”

Regular chats with the England head coach, Thomas Tuchel, promise to help minimise any culture shock. “It’s been a long connection,” he said. “Thomas was my youth coach when I was a youth player at Stuttgart. He was amazing, I really admire him.

“He’s a really special coach and I’m looking forward to staying in touch with him, and getting insights on the league. That’s something I want to use for sure. But it’s also important to build your own opinions because every coach is their own human being and has their opinions and, ­sometimes players get stuck in a box. It’s ­important for me to be neutral about players.”

Allied to a willingness to chall­enge assumptions, such refusal to take labels at face value hinted at the qualities that prompted David ­Hopkinson, Newcastle’s Canadian chief executive, to dub Jaissle “fire” and “a rock star”.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle beat Valencia 2-1 in Jaissle’s first pre-season game in charge. Photograph: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images

If the one-time RB Salzburg manager’s brand of football – “front foot, intense, aggressive, vertical and, of course, also successful” – fits the latter tag, Newcastle fans have greeted him with an adaptation of a late 1970s Euro-disco hit.

Where the Spanish female pop duo Baccara soared to No 1 with Yes, Sir I Can Boogie, travelling supporters attending the friendly win in Valencia last Saturday chorused: “Oh Jaissle I can boogie/You try me once, you’ll beg for more.”

Jaissle said: “All my staff members already said they’re looking forward to sitting after a match in the bar and listening to the song. So let’s see about that! I heard it once and I was smiling. I’m really happy the fans already appreciate me a lot. The welcome from the fans was unbelievable when I was having a walk yesterday in the city. It was really giving me a nice feeling.”

There were more “big smiles” when he recalled a phone call last month asking him if he would be interested in replacing Howe but, little more than 48 hours after arriving in Newcastle for the first time following a training camp at La Manga in southern Spain, Jaissle is under no illusions as to the scale of the challenge ahead.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With the need to comply with football’s spending rules having seen the club pivot to buying young players with high resale potential – four of their five summer signings so far are aged 20 or younger – the immediate future remains opaque.

“I’m long enough in the industry now that you cannot promise anything,” Jaissle said when asked what he aimed to achieve this season. “It makes no sense to promise you things now because I don’t know how things will look in one year. But it doesn’t make sense to see the negative. There will be more adjustments to the squad this summer. We still have time. I would say keep the optimism.”

His cautiously upbeat mood will be bolstered further should Newcastle’s ongoing talks with Benfica about potentially signing their 23‑year‑old full-back Amar Dedic, who played for Jaissle at Salzburg and can operate on both the right and the left, conclude successfully.

“I had a tour of St James’ Park two days ago,” Jaissle said. “When I entered the pitch here with my assistant coaches for the first time, we were looking at each other with smiles and goosebumps. It’s really special, an amazing stadium. I can’t wait to see it full.

“When I received the call at the end of July and it was clearly most likely Eddie would quit there were no doubts or question marks. I had a big smile.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Liverpool, Jeff Bezos and mission creep off the field at Anfield
Sports.content:
THIS MEANS MORE (MONEY)

Far be it for Football Daily to make cheap gags [wait, what? – Football Daily Ed] relating to the involvement of Amazon founder and master of the universe Jeff Bezos in a consortium buying around 30% of Liverpool FC. Will new signings arrive via prompt delivery but end up next door at Everton? How will fans rate the packaging? Etc, etc. There’s also the involvement of Eduardo Saverin, the Facebook co-founder poking his head in. Though long ago unfriended by Mark Zuckerberg, Saverin still ranked No 56 on Forbes’s billionaires list. These are seriously rich men, and among the planet’s chino class, to quote Vladimir Putin, “soccer is popular”. The Geopolitics World Cup posh seats were full of those eyeing up deals on a frontier hardly new to investors from the USA USA USA, but where there may be much more gold to strike. See Gianni Infantino’s misreading of the art of the deal as an, ahem, prime example.

Bezos is no football man, barely known as a sports fan. Links with buying the Seattle Seahawks, his local NFL franchise, were speculative. He is, though, the third richest man in the world, according to appendage-measuring listicles. Amazon’s market value is higher than Brazil’s annual GDP. For certain people, that triggers arousal at the thought of their team being able to buy the biggest and best players in the world. Just imagine if their club was to spend, say, £446m in a single summer. How good would that be?

For others, there is a regrettable mission creep towards a civic institution – one that, despite global fame, cleaves to its local community – being tossed around by venture capitalists. Though that process has been in train since Tom Hicks and George Gillett arrived on Merseyside, full of huckster charm, almost two decades ago. The socialism and collectivism Bill Shankly envisaged for the club he made famous disappeared in the sepia-tinged rearview mirror. Football was a business even back in Shanks’ day but now attracts the richest suits of all; if Bezos is chancing his arm in football, what price Elon Musk or Google tycoon Larry Page are seen wearing the scarf of their chosen club? Oh joy.

Current overlords Fenway Sports Group, who picked up the pieces from impending disaster in 2010, are, yes, a consortium of American venture capitalists. Their existential aim is to make as much loot as possible from an asset purchased for a knockdown price of £300m. It’s gone well. This mooted deal includes Bezos, Saverin and Amit Bhatia, a frontman you may recognise from when QPR fans celebrated their owners being richer than Roman Abramovich. That did not go well. The latest deal would value the club at £4.4bn. High-fives all round, though the doubles and trebles may take time. Liverpool enter the season with an imbalanced squad, unsuited to a manager whose arrival was generally seen as a Good Thing. If football is all about money, even the biggest money cannot solve every problem.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“After careful consideration, we don’t feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place, but we will remain in conversation with the club and see what is possible in the future” – one wealthy benefactor not entering the game – yet – is Turki Alalshikh, whose bid to buy a controlling interest in Derby will no longer proceed, with the club now off the market.

RECOMMENDED LOOKING

Here’s David Squires on … the masochistic life of a Football League fan.

View image in fullscreen Illustration: David Squires/The Guardian

double quotation mark Having also boycotted the GWC and also being very concerned about the season to come, I sympathise with Ken Muir (yesterday’s Football Daily letters). But at least Hearts know who their manager is. Due to the absurd, months-long FA ‘investigation’ into the manager who’s clearly admitted culpability for the undisputed facts of Spygate, my club, Southampton, is in a horrid limbo. Surely it could have been done and dusted in a couple of weeks and Saints could have planned accordingly. But perhaps the FA blazers were too busy writing their letter of support to Gianni Infantino to worry about destabilising my football club” – Bob Cushion.

double quotation mark ‘It’s 15 years of frustration here at this club,’ says Rangers boss Derek McInnes (yesterday’s Quote of the Day.) Steven Gerrard and the sole object in his managerial trophy cabinet would like a word, Derek” – David Maddock.

double quotation mark Given the surfeit of the recent GWC machinations, the blatherings and canvassing for Gianni to do one (or not) and the less-than-sportsmanlike attitude from members of the Argentina team, can we please have a reprise of the Football Daily’s erstwhile, eventually abortive, attempt to ‘STOP FOOTBALL’? It has to be worth a thought, before VAR, PGMOL and Arsenal’s Dark Arts Department™ get to work on the 2026-27 Premier League shenanigans, surely?” – Budgie Wright.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s letter o’ the day winner is … Bob Cushion, who gets some Football Weekly merch. Terms and conditions for our competitions can be viewed here.

Sports.title: Chelsea face Real Sociedad in WCL third qualifying round with riches at stake
Sports.content:
Chelsea will face Real Sociedad in the Women’s Champions League third qualifying round, needing a win over two legs to secure a place in the main league phase of the competition.

The 2021 runners-up and six-time European semi-finalists are taking part in the qualifying stage by virtue of their disappointing third-placed finish in the Women’s Super League last season – their lowest league ­finish since 2019 – and they will be the favourites against the Spanish side.

Chelsea could have faced Ajax, Inter, Eintracht Frankfurt or the ­Austrian side St Pölten. They were unable to meet the big-name sides such as Real Madrid, Wolfsburg, Juventus or Paris Saint-Germain at this stage because of seedings. Sonia Bompastor’s team will hope to join Arsenal and Manchester City in the main phase of the competition.

The potential financial implications of missing out on ­qualification are significant. All 18 clubs that take part in the league phase will receive a guaranteed minimum of €505,000 (£431,500), plus a further €60,000 for every league‑phase fixture they win and €20,000 for every draw, as well as prize money ranging from €10,000 to €180,000 depending on where they finish in the table, rising by €10,000 per position.

Additionally, the eventual champions will receive €1,050,000 in prize money across the course of the knockout phase – including €500,000 specifically for winning the final – as there are six-figure sums on offer for each knockout-phase fixture.

Chelsea will be at home for the first leg, which is scheduled to be played on 26 August, with the second leg in Spain scheduled for 2 September, three days before Chelsea’s WSL season opener, which is at home against Aston Villa on 5 September.

League path

Ajax v Real Madrid Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Chelsea have been strong contenders for the European title in recent years, reaching the semi-finals in three of the past four campaigns, but they lost to their rivals Arsenal in a dramatic quarter-final last term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Real Sociedad, based in San Sebastián, finished third in Spain’s top division last season behind Real Madrid and Barcelona. The ­qualifying draw was split into two sections, with a “champions path” for winners of their domestic divisions drawn ­separately to the “league path” which contained domestic runners-up and third-placed sides such as Chelsea.

Køge, who eliminated the Scottish champions Hearts earlier in the ­qualification process, were pitted against PSV, while in the most eye-catching tie of the round Ajax will take on Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez are married! Portugal star ties the knot with influencer in an 'intimate and private' civil ceremony attended by their five children
Sports.content:
Have YOU got a story? Email tips@dailymail.co.uk

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have married in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal.

The couple tied the knot in an 'intimate and private' ceremony on Tuesday with their five children present, a year after they first got engaged.

Ronaldo shared that he and Georgina had tied the knot after ten years together by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram.

He captioned the post: 'C❤️G.'

A representative for Ronaldo also confirmed news of the union, saying: 'Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.

'The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.'

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have married in an 'intimate and private' ceremony in Cascais, Portugal attended by their five children

The Portugal star announced that he and Georgina had tied the knot by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram

The wedding news comes just days after it was thought the couple were set to marry in Funchal Cathedral, leading to thousands of fans gathering outside the church.

However, it was then revealed that the couple were not getting married there at all, and the ceremony turned out to be for an entirely unconnected Portuguese couple from Madeira called Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira.

Georgina was working at a Gucci store in Madrid, earning £10 an hour, when she and Ronaldo met in 2016.

Recalling their meeting, Georgina said: 'I was finally able to leave the shop to go home three hours later than I should have and as I was getting ready to leave Cristiano came in with his eldest son and some friends.

'Let's just say it was butterflies in my stomach.'

Cristiano would then pick Georgina up from work in his £1.5million Bugatti – after she had arrived at the shop on the bus.

'Many times he'd come after work', she said in her Netflix series I Am Georgina.

'He would come, I remember once, once in a Bugatti. My coworkers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it.'

By December, she quit her job shortly after fans began crowding outside the store.

The following month, the pair made their first public appearance at The Best FIFA Football Awards, confirming speculation that they were a couple.

Cristiano and Georgina made their Instagram debut as a couple in March 2017 when the footballer posted a sweet snap of them cuddling on a couch.

In June of that year, the footballer welcomed twins Mateo and Eva via surrogacy and then five months later, Georgina gave birth to their daughter, Alana Martina.

Then the next month, they announced they were expecting, giving birth to their daughter Alana Martina in November.

The following month, Georgina posed for photos with her newborn daughter Alana for the cover of HOLA!

Join the discussion Do you think celebrity weddings should be private family affairs or public celebrations shared with fans?

The pair have two biological children, though she helps raise all five of his kids. Cristiano Jr. (pictured left) hugs his baby sister Eva while Georgina cradles Mateo on her lap, Cristiano (pictured right) holds his two daughters baby Bella and Alana Martina

Ronaldo proposed to Georgina last year with a huge diamond engagement, having previously said he 'waited' before popping the question

Georgina joked that the soccer star popping the question with an 'enormous' diamond ring was 'the least he could offer' after waiting for so long to propose

Revealing how they came up with the name for their daughter, she said: 'We both chose the name. Cristiano chose Alana and I chose Martina.

'We decided to give her both names that each of us chose. We thought it was even more special.'

In 2022, the couple welcomed twins; however, their baby boy tragically died during childbirth, while his sister, Bella Esmeralda, survived.

Opening up about how he and Georgina coped with the heartache of losing a baby, the footballer told Piers Morgan at the time: 'I feel that we always support each other. Sometimes it's like in a relationship you have good moments, bad moments it is part of the journey.

'But probably in that period, we consolidated it more, the relationship, but even in the worst moments you have to meet, you have to make the thing smooth.

'I learned so many things. I saw the other perspective of the life. My daughter, now who is three years old, she is the queen of the family, who made the house happy.

'Everything happens for a reason. I believe in that. So, we are a blessed family. I am proud of that.'

After nearly a decade together, fans were then desperate to know when Georgina and Cristiano would marry, with their family now complete.

However, in an interview with Marca last year, the Portuguese admitted he hadn't yet married Georgina because he hadn't felt the 'click'.

He said: 'I always tell her, "when we get that click". Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about.

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'

In August, the footballer finally popped the question with a giant diamond ring.

Fans speculated the pair got engaged the month before after the model shared pictures of a bridal-themed dinner, complete with 'C heart G' pillows, a six-piece band and stunning white flower arrangements.

She also wore a giant sparkler on her wedding ring finger, hinting at the pair's secret engagement.

Georgina gleefully shared the news on Instagram with a photo of her glitzy engagement ring. 'Yes I do. In this and in all my lives,' she wrote in a heartfelt caption.

Cristiano then revealed that two of his children inspired him to give Georgina a 'not-so romantic' and off-the-cuff proposal.

He revealed that he didn't plan to propose to the 'woman of his life' the night they got engaged, but it felt like the 'right time'.

'It was like 1am. My daughters were in bed sleeping,' the 41-year-old told Piers Morgan in part one of their new interview.

He said: 'One of my friends gave me the ring to offer Gio (Georgina) and as I was giving her the ring, my two kids come in and say "Daddy, you're going to give the ring to mum and you're going to ask her to get married."

'I said, "Wow, this is the right moment to say yes." It was the time. I knew that I was going to do it one day but I hadn't planned to do it then.

Cristiano met Georgina in 2016 after he saw her in the Gucci store where she was working

'Because my daughters said that and my friends were filming, it was what I wanted and I offered (the ring). I didn't (get on one knee) because I wasn't prepared but it was a beautiful moment. I made a speech.

'It was simple, I'm not a very romantic guy. Well, I am, but I'm not very romantic, not the kind of guy who brings flowers every week to the home. But I'm romantic in my way. It was beautiful and I knew that it's the woman of my life so I did that and I hope that I did it well.'

Asked about when they plan to tie the knot, the footballer joked: 'Not yet. We plan to do it after the World Cup with the trophy! But she is not the person that likes big parties. She doesn't like it. She likes private things. So I will respect these decisions.

'One thing that I love, she didn't care about the ring. She asked me if I was honest and I said, "I want you and I want to marry you." I didn't cry but I had tears on my eyes.'

Experts estimated that Cristiano splashed out an astonishing £1.5million on Georgina's engagement ring.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba 'set to have Monaco contract ripped up after suffering injury' in latest blow to troubled ex-Man United star
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba 'set to have Monaco contract ripped up after suffering injury' in latest blow to troubled ex-Man United star

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Paul Pogba's Monaco contract is 'set to be terminated' after the 33-year-old suffered a fresh injury.

The French World Cup winner and former Manchester United star had been trying to revive his career following a doping ban.

But his time at Monaco in Ligue 1 has been disastrous and pre-season this summer was seen by the club as crucial in determining whether he could contribute.

He played 45 minutes in one game before a recurrence of a knee injury last season kept him out of four matches.

And now he has collapsed in severe pain in his leg during a training session, accelerating Monaco's decision to terminate his contract, according to L'Equipe and Nicemartin.com.

Pogba only returned to training last week but sustained the thigh injury in a small-sided game and was scheduled for an MRI this week.

Paul Pogba is set to have his contract at Monaco terminated after suffering an injury

The club will now try and reach an agreement with Pogba and his representatives over paying out his deal, which expires next summer.

Daily Mail Sport understands he was offered to MLS clubs in America on Tuesday.

Pogba - who earned £290,000-per-week in his second spell at Man United - is reportedly earning below £44,000-per-week at Monaco.

Pogba was allowed back into football in March 2025 after his doping ban was reduced on appeal.

He had already left Juventus after having that contract terminated by mutual consent in December 2024.

Monaco was his route back into the game but he only managed to play in six matches last term due to persistent injury problems.

It remains to be seen whether Pogba will try to find a new club or decide the time is right to hang up his boots.

Pogba was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance after what he called 'a time of darkness'.

The midfielder told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

Sports.title: Football's swap shop: The best - and WORST - player trades after Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson switched places... including a Sir Alex Ferguson masterstroke and a rare Pep Guardiola mistake
Sports.content:
Football's swap shop: The best - and WORST - player trades after Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson switched places... including a Sir Alex Ferguson masterstroke and a rare Pep Guardiola mistake

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The lesser-spotted swap deal, always great fun isn't it?

The straight trade is a move that's touted far more than it's actually executed but Brennan Johnson's switch with Dwight McNeil has now been completed between Crystal Palace and Everton.

Both players have signed four-year contracts at their new clubs and while rare, their swap is by no means one of a kind.

The Johnson/McNeil swap joins an illustrious list, with some incredibly high profile players such as Samuel Eto'o, Alexis Sanchez and Fabio Cannavaro involved in similar transactions down the years.

Here, we take a look at football's swap shop, shining a light on 10 of the most high-profile examples.

Samuel Eto'o to Inter Milan - Zlatan Ibrahimovic to Barcelona (2009)

In 2009 the two giants struck a deal to swap two of the world's best strikers.

Inter had the better end of the deal in every possible measure. Barcelona paid £46 million to Inter AND gave them Eto’o who, the season before, had scored in the Champions League final win against Manchester United.

To exacerbate the Catalan side's loss, Eto’o went on to win the Champions League again under Jose Mourinho, while Ibrahimovic only lasted one season, struggling to adapt tactically with Lionel Messi and falling out with Pep Guardiola.

He still managed to score 22 goals and help the team to a LaLiga title but moved to AC Milan on loan the following season.

Samuel Eto'o embraces Zlatan Ibrahimovic ahead of a 2009 Champions League clash

Alexis Sanchez to Manchester United - Henrikh Mkhitaryan to Arsenal (2018)

In January of 2018 after a long, drawn-out contractual dispute between Arsenal’s then talisman Sanchez and the board, the Chilean left for Man United.

Arsenal allowed Sanchez to run down his contract and pick his next club. He originally wanted to go to Manchester City, but they were unwilling to pay him the £400,000-a-week salary that United offered.

Even though he only had six months left on his deal, Arsenal still received a makeweight in the form of Mkhitaryan.

Ultimately, the move wasn't nearly as painful for the Gunners as it could have been. Most fans were despairing the prospect of losing Sanchez to a rival but he never truly delivered at Old Trafford.

Ashley Cole to Chelsea - William Gallas to Arsenal (2006)

Possibly the most infamous swap in history. After Arsenal’s 2006 Champions League final loss, Ashley Cole, who was regarded as the best left back in the world, was swayed by Jose Mourinho to swap north London for west.

They met in a hotel and Mourinho offered to double Cole’s salary, whereas Arsenal’s offer was so low he allegedly ‘nearly crashed his car’ when his agent told him the terms.

Cole only had a year left on his Arsenal deal, so Chelsea paid just £5m, but to sweeten the deal handed over their own left-back, William Gallas, who had the best years of his career behind him.

Cole went onto to win everything with Chelsea, while Gallas endured a rocky time at Arsenal, given the captaincy and then stripped of it, eventually ending up at fierce rivals Spurs.

Ashley Cole and William Gallas traded places in one of the more infamous swap deals

Arthur Melo to Juventus - Miralem Pjanic to Barcelona (2020)

In 2020, after lockdown, both clubs were in serious financial trouble but realised there was a mutually beneficial trade to be had.

Both paid over the odds for each other’s players, which was helpful in being able to present a better balance sheet to the respective governing bodies.

Arthur Melo was a young Brazilian talent who couldn’t get in the team and Pjanic was a Serie A legend who was slowing down with age.

Juventus paid a whopping £72m for Melo, who was arguably worth half of that and Barcelona splashed out £60m for a Pjanic who was hampered by injuries at this point.

Neither set of fans were particularly pleased with the deals and there wasn't a clear winner here.

Jermaine Defoe to Tottenham - Bobby Zamora to West Ham (2004)

In the summer of 2004, Defoe who was part of the golden age of West Ham’s academy, was outgrowing the Hammers. Martin Jol joined Spurs that summer and saw him as the perfect man to be his No 9.

He helped orchestrate a deal that saw Spurs pay £7m to West Ham and hand over their own young striker Bobby Zamora, who despite being an exciting prospect at Brighton, never really tore up trees at White Hart Lane.

Defoe would go on to score more than 100 goals for Spurs. Zamora wasn't as much of a hit at West Ham but did score 36 goals in 151 appearances and famously fired them back to the Premier League in the 2005 Championship play-off final.

Jermaine Defoe was a huge hit for Tottenham, scoring more than 100 goals for the club

Michy Batshuayi to Dortmund - Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang to Arsenal - Olivier Giroud to Chelsea (2018)

If a swap deal is unusual, a triple-swap remains a real anomaly.

But that's what happened in January 2018. Arsenal needed a new star with Sanchez gone, Batshuayi wasn’t getting enough game time at Chelsea and Giroud had looked ready to leave Arsenal for some time.

All three teams would say they were happy with the deals. Despite only playing 10 games for BVB Batshuayi managed seven goals and cost the Germans virtually nothing, Aubameyang was electric for Arsenal and even won the golden boot in the 18/19 season and Giroud won the Europa League, FA cup and the Champions League with Chelsea.

Deco to Barcelona - Ricardo Quaresma to Porto (2004)

After winning player of the tournament in the 2004 Champions League Deco was one of the hottest prospects going, Mourinho tried to convince him to come to Chelsea alongside Porto teammates Ricardo Carvalho and Paulo Ferreria, but the midfielder was drawn to Barca in the end.

Barcelona threw in the young Ricardo Quaresma to get Porto to agree to the deal.

Both Deco and Quaresma flourished at each club with Deco winning the Champions League and Quaresma enjoying some spell-binding seasons in his home country. They both ended up at Chelsea together years later.

Fabio Cannavaro to Juventus - Fabio Carini to Inter Milan (2004)

This one is a bit more niche but interesting. Fabio Carini was a lesser-known Uruguayan goalkeeper who was highly touted but hardly a world beater. Every football fan knows about Cannavaro.

But at the time in 2004, Inter had keeper issues and so thought it would be worth trading their young prospect. This could not have been a worse decision.

Fast-forward just two years and Cannavaro had captained Italy to their fourth world cup and had won the Ballon d’Or. Meanwhile Carini made just 4 appearances in his entire Inter career. It has to go down as the worst swap in history.

Fabio Cannavaro (right), pictured with Monica Bellucci, after winning the Ballon d'Or

Andy Cole to Manchester United - Keith Gillespie to Newcastle (1995)

In 1995 after failed attempts to win the Premier League under Kevin Keegan, Newcastle were slowly falling backwards and one of their most notable departures of this period was English striker Andy Cole.

Sir Alex Ferguson brought him to Old Trafford and in exchange gave Newcastle £6m plus winger, Keith Gillespie.

Cole went onto to win everything at United, Gillespie just the opposite on Tyneside.

Joao Cancelo to Manchester City - Danilo to Juventus (2019)

Finishing with a Premier League one and a deal that is one of the more underrated swaps in recent memory. Cancelo at the time had just completed an excellent first season at Juventus and Danilo after winning the title with City in 2018 and 2019 was slowing down.

Guardiola, knowing he had to replace him went for Cancelo who was excellent for City, winning everything in his time there, where he played both right-back and left-back getting into the FIFA Team of The Year in 2022.

Danilo was a success at Juventus too, winning the Scudetto in his first year there and playing 156 games over six years.

Sports.title: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery sends warning to Europe's elite ahead of UEFA Super Cup showdown against PSG
Sports.content:
Unai Emery has warned Europe’s wealthy elite that Aston Villa believe they will be one of the continent’s giants once again

Villa face Paris Saint-Germain for the UEFA Super Cup on Wednesday looking to add a second trophy in less than three months, after claiming the Europa League at the end of May.

Villa have undergone significant change this summer, with Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne sold for about £150million combined as the club sought to stay in line with UEFA financial rules. But Emery sees no reason to change their ambitions.

He said: ‘If we compare ourselves to other clubs like Man City, Chelsea, Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool, we are competing with them. We don’t have their power… yet.

‘The effort the club are making is huge. We are trying to extend Villa Park to 50,000 supporters. This is one step forward.

‘We are increasing our budget through results on the pitch, sometimes selling some players, being consistent, expecting a high level and more or less keeping it. Every year the club has moved forward.’

Unai Emery's Aston Villa will take on PSG in the UEFA Super Cup on Wednesday night

Villa will be without England pair Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins, as well as Argentina goalkeeper Emi Martinez.

The trio were given four weeks off after the World Cup but are expected to return to training next week.

Skipper John McGinn has been at Villa since they were in the Championship in 2018 and despite the high-profile departures, he is confident they will continue to challenge, both in the Champions League and Premier League this term.

He said: ‘We are really excited by the new Aston Villa. Our expectation is similar to where it has been in the past few seasons, competing with the best in England and Europe.

‘A lot is changing but we have the same manager, the same methods and a desire to achieve more. A lot of people thought we’d reached our ceiling but we’ve proved them wrong.’

Sports.title: Roy Keane's son-in-law could be heading to Portugal, Nottingham Forest complete £36m move for Ousmane Diomande - and Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Roy Keane's son-in-law of Portuguese interest

Benfica are weighing up a move for Southampton centre back Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Portuguese side sold Antonio Silva to Bournemouth at the start of the month and Benfica coach Marco Silva is looking to bolster his defensive options.

Harwood-Bellis, 24, started out at Manchester City and has been capped once by England, scoring in a 5-0 win over the Republic of Ireland.

He was also part of the England squad that won the 2023 UEFA European U21 Championship.

Harwood-Bellis made 48 appearances and scored seven goals in all competitions last season, and married the daughter of former Manchester United captain and Sky Sports pundit Roy Keane in June.

Roy Keane's son-in-law Taylor Harwood-Bellis is of interest to Benfica in Portugal

Hull move back in for Leeds star Gelhardt

Hull City have stepped back in for Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt after Wrexham made an approach to sign him.

The 24-year-old was on loan at Hull last season and scored 14 goals on their way to promotion.

Wrexham were willing to sign him in a £4.5m deal but the chance to play in the Premier League is understood to have swayed the player's decision.

Palace youngster heads out on loan

Bristol City have signed highly rated Crystal Palace wing-back Rio Cardines on a season-long loan.

Cardines, 20, made his Palace debut in their UEFA Conference League win over Dynamo Kyiv last season and went on to make two further appearances for the Eagles while consistently being around the first-team squad.

From Trinidad and Tobago, Cardines has 11 senior international caps to his name and will now look to add Championship experience to his CV.

Palace see Cardines as part of their long-term plans, although he is only contracted until 2028.

The Robins' announcement video featured Cardines drinking a can of Rio in a Caribbean shop while Duran Duran’s ‘Rio’ played.

BOBBY MANZI

Palace consider ex-Brighton man

Solly March has spent time at the Crystal Palace training ground ahead of a potential free transfer.

Brighton released March at the end of last season, with the 32-year-old having played limited minutes over the last three campaigns due to injury problems.

March made 194 Premier League appearances for Brighton, scoring 14 goals and providing 20 assists. He can play on both wings and at wing-back.

A move for March could provoke hostility from Palace supporters, given the Englishman spent 13 years with rivals Brighton. He has scored twice in 11 appearances against Palace.

BOBBY MANZI

Benfica right-back on Toon radar

Newcastle are exploring a move for Benfica right-back Amar Dedic.

The 23-year-old is valued around £25million and has also had interest from Everton.

Born in Austria, Dedic has over 30 caps for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

He started out at Red Bull Salzburg and also had a spell playing for FC Liefering when Matthias Jaissle, Newcastle's new boss, was coaching there.

City's Alleyne is the toast of Clarets

Manchester City defender Max Alleyne is joining Burnley on a season loan.

The 21-year-old who had a spell on loan at Watford last season is expected to undergo a medical in the next 48 hours and could be in the squad to face West Ham on Sunday.

Palace teen on Portuguese radar

Portuguese top-flight club Alverca - who are owned by Vinicius Jr - are in talks to sign Mofe Jemide on a permanent deal from Crystal Palace.

The imposing centre-back, who signed his first professional contract at Palace in 2023, has represented England at U20 level and had significant loan and permanent interest across Europe.

The 19-year-old trained with Pierre Sage’s first team squad in pre-season and was given minutes during friendlies against Swindon, Bromley, Famalicao and Al Ula.

He has yet to make his competitive senior debut, though, turning out 44 times for Palace’s U21s.

EXCLUSIVE BY BOBBY MANZI

Another loan for Kalvin Phillips

Midfielder Kalvin Phillips has agreed to join Sheffield United from Manchester City on another loan, as Daily Mail Sport reported in June.

Midfielder Kalvin Phillips has agreed to join Sheffield United from Manchester City on another loan

Chris Wilder was keen to re-sign the 30-year-old, who has two years left on his contract, despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Forest target twins

Nottingham Forest are closing in the signing of former Reading twins Joseph Ntege and Jubilee Ntege.

The twins were born on a Stockholm council estate in Sweden and moved to London with their mother and grandmother. They have already represented the country at U15 and U16 level.

Reading spotted them playing grassroots football and beat off competition from Arsenal, Crystal Palace and Fulham to sign them.

The 16-year-olds have attracted interest from a number of clubs following their departure from Reading this summer with Forest, German side Augsburg, Norwich City and Belgian club Genk all in the mix for their signature.

Left winger Joseph has also attracted attention from Manchester United and Newcastle United.

Last season, Joseph registered 35 goals and assists, including 12 goal involvements for the U18s, while Jubilee registered 33 goals and assists, including 10 goal involvements for the U18s

World Cup star joins Forest

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon.

The 22-year-old centre-back has signed a four-year deal with an option for another year.

Diomande said: 'It is a historic club, and it motivates me to join such a club. I believe we can achieve very good things this season and I am looking forward to meeting the players and head coach.

'I will give my best and all I can to help the team. I cannot wait to meet the supporters at the City Ground and together we can have a good season.'

Forest still want to add a right-back, midfielder and striker.

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon

Patterson completes Wrexham medical

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson has completed a medical ahead of his £8m move to Wrexham.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed yesterday, the 26-year-old has agreed terms on a four-year deal with the Championship club.

Patterson is finalising the paperwork on his contract.

Wrexham are also in talks to sign Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt in a £4.5m deal.

Baggies strengthen midfield

West Bromwich Albion have fended off competition from Swansea City to sign Rabby Nzingoula from Ligue 1 side Strasbourg for an undisclosed fee.

The 20-year-old midfielder has agreed a three-year contract and becomes the club's seventh signing of the summer.

Nzingoula made 15 first-team appearances for Strasbourg, including in the Europa Conference League, and has also had loan spells with Montpellier and Nuremberg.

'From the games I have seen, it's clear to see it's a very good, physical and demanding division,' he told West Brom's website.

Ex-Everton star back on Merseyside

Former Everton midfielder Tom Davies has been back training with the club.

The 28-year-old is a free agent and looking for a new club after leaving Sheffield United and has been welcomed back at Everton's Finch Farm training ground where he has been working with the club's U21s to maintain his fitness.

Hull get their Nobel prize

Hull City have finally agreed their protracted negotiations for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

The centre back is heading over for his medical after the clubs settled on a £21million fee plus 12.5per cent sell-on clause, while his former club Real Betis receive 20 percent as part of their sell-on.

The 21-year-old Senegal international can play at centre back and left-back.

Fulham snap up Southampton's Charles

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons.

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year contract, tying him to Craven Cottage until June 2031, with a club option to extend by a further 12 months. Southampton also retain a 20 percent sell-on.

Speaking to FFCtv, Charles, who will wear the number 19 shirt, said: 'It’s a great club, with a really good vision – the manager explained that to me. To be here is a massive privilege.

'I hope to really kickstart my Premier League career. At such a good club as well, it’s perfect for me, and hopefully perfect for the fans as well.

'I’m buzzing to finally get it over the line. The club has got a really good foundation, from the bottom to the top really.'

Palace and Everton complete rare swap deal

Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil have completed their respective swaps to Everton and Crystal Palace and signed four year contracts.

Johnson, who only joined Palace from Tottenham in January for £35m, told evertontv: ‘I'm so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it's a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

Brennan Johnson has completed a move to Everton from Crystal Palace in a rare swap deal

As part of the transfer, Dwight McNeil has moved the other way to link up with the Eagles after his transfer to the club on Deadline Day in the winter window collapsed at the last moment

'There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

He becomes the fifth summer signing for David Moyes’ squad after Merlin Rohl’s loan obligation was activated along with the additions of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Christian Norgaard.

Meanwhile, McNeil has signed his four-year contract with Palace and said: 'The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.'

Lukaku agrees Turkey move

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli.

The Belgium international has agreed a two year contract worth around £8.6m a season and has already passed his medical.

The deal includes further add ons based on performances.

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli

Chelsea are understood to have inserted a 40percent sell-on clause when they sold Lukaku for a knockdown £26m to Napoli two years ago.

He scored 14 goals in his first season but injury and the arrival of Rasmus Hojlund from Manchester United restricted him to just seven games last year.

Liverpool starlet wanted in Portugal

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move.

The 18-year-old who has joined the club from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal has stood out for the first team in pre-season friendlies.

But despite the promise he has shown, and Liverpool's dearth of defensive cover, post-Brexit rules mean Austria youth international Ndukwe doesn't have enough points to obtain a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) to obtain a work visa.

He will start against Como in their last friendly but is unable to play a competitive match for the Anfield club.

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move

Now clubs from Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have been calling to take the 6ft 6ins centre back on loan but there is a sense Portugal may be his preferred destination.

After playing alongside him, captain Virgil van Dijk said: 'Big talent, big guy and he wants to learn. I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him, it is just progressing. I know he has to go on loan I think so let's see where he ends up.'

Napoli still in the hunt for Badiashile

Napoli have offered a £2m loan fee for Chelsea's £30million-rated centre-back Benoit Badiashile with obligation to buy.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs and the player's representatives to try and find a full agreement.

Chelsea have sold Trevoh Chalobah to Como and are also looking to sell Axel Disasi who has had interest from Crystal Palace and West Ham.

Napoli are continuing talks to sign Chelsea's £30m-rated centre-back Beniot Badiashile (right)

Mamadou Sarr, who suffered an injury at the weekend, is likely to go on loan to a Premier League side.

Keeper Filip Jorgensen has completed his move to Strasbourg on loan.

Wigan Athletic are closing in on their loan move for Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh while Portsmouth want 17-year-old Chelsea winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen on loan.

Napoli remain keen on Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus also as talks continue. Arsenal want £20m for the Brazilian.

Villa defender wanted in Belgium

Aston Villa right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic is a target for Rangers along with Hugo Siquet of Bruges.

Nedeljkovic has had interest from a number of clubs including Osasuna but Rangers are exploring a £4million deal with initial loan for the Serbia international.

The 20-year-old had a spell with RB Leipzig last season.

Burnley after new keeper

Burnley are showing interest in OH Leuven goalkeeper Tobe Leysen.

The 24-year-old former Belgium U21 international has one year left on contract so Leuven are willing to listen to offers.

Nottingham Forest are closing in on the signing of former Reading twins Joseph and Jubilee Ntege.

The twins were born on a Stockholm council estate in Sweden and moved to London with their mother and grandmother.

They have already represented the country at Under-15 and U16 level.

Reading spotted them playing grassroots football and beat off competition from Arsenal, Crystal Palace and Fulham to sign them.

The 16-year-olds have attracted interest from a number of clubs following their departure from Reading this summer with Forest, German side Augsburg, Norwich City and Belgian club Genk all in the mix for their signature.

Left winger Joseph has also attracted attention from Manchester United and Newcastle United.

Nottingham Forest are closing in the signing of former Reading twins Joseph and Jubilee Ntege

Sports.title: Venomous snake uncovered in football player's helmet after he practiced for an hour with it next to his head
Sports.content:
A high school football player in Arkansas spent an hour practicing with a venomous snake in his helmet.

Coaches at Maumelle High School eventually made the shocking discovery of the creature wriggling after the player noticed unusual movement inside his helmet. He flagged the problem to his defensive coach, who alerted Athletic Director Kirk Horton.

The snake, eventually determined to be a cottonmouth, was hiding underneath the helmet's padding, making it difficult to remove as it was roughly two-foot-long.

'It really was just shock and disbelief,' Horton told KARK. 'I've got a better shot at winning the lottery than seeing this in my ten years.'

After using a tote bag to secure the helmet and snake, Animal Services were called to the high school.

Animal Services Director Chris Davis claimed the young player was fortunate not to be bitten by the venomous creature, that was eventually removed from the helmet and relocated to a forested area far away from the school.

The player felt movement inside his helmet with a snake hiding inside the padding

The venomous snake was roughly two-foot-long

The snake had to be washed out of the helmet and was then safely removed

'When the officers got there and stuff, they examined the helmet, and at that time they could see that there was a snake in the helmet,' Davis said, via KATV. 'They verified it was not a copperhead, but it possibly was a cottonmouth or a water snake.'

After being given a new helmet, the player continued practicing after the shock ordeal.

Players were later given a simple message to check their equipment before putting it on to avoid a similar scare as the team hosted a scheduled safety meeting later in the day.

Despite his years working in animal services, Davis was perplexed by the shocking incident.

'I've removed a snake out of a car vent, in the engine, purses, backpacks,' he said. 'In a helmet? Never.

'It was very unreal. You had to kind of be there and take pictures to say this was real.'

Cottonmouth snakes seek shelter in dark, protected spaces, and on this occasion it had to be flooded out of the padding to be safely captured.

The situation would have been much more serious had the player been bitten, with Davis warning: 'The cottonmouth, in my opinion, is probably the second most venomous snake here in Arkansas. I would say the rattlesnake is probably the number one.'

Sports.title: Inter Milan step up pursuit of Spurs star Djed Spence as Italian giants offer £25m for England defender
Sports.content:
Inter Milan step up pursuit of Spurs star Djed Spence as Italian giants offer £25m for England defender

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Inter Milan are continuing their pursuit of Tottenham full back Djed Spence.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the Italian side first made contact in June and are trying to work out a compromise fee for the England international.

Inter are offering £25million, only £5m more than the original package given to Middlesbrough when Tottenham signed Spence back in 2022. Spurs were originally looking for closer to £36m.

Spence, who started four games for England at the World Cup, including the semi-final against Argentina, has fallen further down the pecking order at Spurs after the arrival of Andy Robertson from Liverpool.

He signed a new four-year contract in north London at the start of last season but is believed to be keen on joining the Italian champions, with Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro expected to be Roberto De Zerbi’s preferred full backs this season.

One big plus for Spence though is he is able to play on either side, with many of his Spurs and England minutes coming at left back despite naturally being right-sided.

Inter Milan are willing to pay £25million to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham this summer

He could yet stay in north London but would not be first choice and may be keen for more minutes after his stock rose at the World Cup.

Tottenham, meanwhile, could be as keen to cash in when his value is potentially at its highest.

Sports.title: Tottenham could hand Arsenal major transfer boost after opening Folarin Balogun talks
Sports.content:
Tottenham could hand Arsenal major transfer boost after opening Folarin Balogun talks

Tottenham have spent big in the summer transfer window to overhaul their squad and they don't appear to be done yet after setting their sights on a former Arsenal star

View 2 Images Folarin Balogun (Image: Valery Hache/AFP)

Tottenham are in negotiations with Monaco over a deal which would bring the former Arsenal striker, Folarin Balogun, back to the Premier League.

‌



Balogun came through the Arsenal academy after joining the club as an eight-year old but made just a handful of senior appearances for the club, instead enjoying success out on loan in France with Reims. The striker scored 22 goals for the Ligue 1 outfit in the 2022-23 campaign to attract transfer interest from clubs elsewhere in Europe.

‌



With Balogun's stock high, Arsenal sold the 25-year-old to Monaco in a deal worth €40million (£34.3m). Three years on, it seems the United States international could return to the Premier League, and north London.

‌



According to L'Equipe, Tottenham not only hold an interest in Balogun but have already held opened with Monaco to discuss a transfer for the striker.

Real Madrid plot shock Martin Zubimendi transfer as Arsenal left with dilemma READ MORE :

The same report claims that Balogun, who scored three goals for the USMNT at the World Cup this summer, is valued at around €60m (£51.2m) by Monaco. Any move would secure a windfall for Arsenal, who inserted a 17.5 per cent sell-on clause in the deal which took the striker to France.

Balogun unintentionally made headlines this summer when he was controversially shown a red card in the United States' victory over Bosnia & Herzegovina in the World Cup round of 32.

‌



That sending off should have seen him suspended for their round of 16 tie with Belgium, however, Balogun's ban was 'suspended' for one year following an intervention from FIFA. Donald Trump, the United States president, subsequently claimed credit for raising the red card with Gianni Infantino.

View 2 Images Balogun impressed at the World Cup but became a huge talking point after his ban for being sent off was suspended by FIFA

Spurs have spent heavily this summer in a bid to progress under their new manager, Roberto De Zerbi, after narrowly avoiding relegation from the Premier League last season. The club finished 17th for a second consecutive season, though their top-flight status was only preserved on the final day of the season at the expense of West Ham.

Article continues below

Free transfers for Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson and Martin Dubravka have all been completed. Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke have also been signed for significant transfer fees totalling around £237m.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo marries Georgina Rodriguez as football icon shares ring picture
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo marries Georgina Rodriguez as football icon shares ring picture

Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed that he and Georgina Rodriguez are now married in a post on his Instagram account showing their hands complete with wedding rings

View 3 Images Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have confirmed their marriage (Image: Irish Mirror)

Cristiano Ronaldo has shared a social media post confirming he has married Georgina Rodriguez.

‌



The Portuguese superstar shared a picture of two hands wearing gold rings on their wedding fingers following speculation that he and Rodriguez were soon to be married.

‌



It's been reported that the duo, who have been together since 2016, were married in a 'private and intimate' ceremony attended by their five children in Portugal. People claim the wedding took place in Cascais.

‌



Piers Morgan, Ronaldo's friend, was among those to congratulate the pair, tweeting: “Congrats to my friends @Cristiano & Georgina on their wedding today in Portugal! They’re a great couple, and I wish them a long and happy marriage together. Parabéns!”

Ronaldo, 41, met Rodriguez when he was playing for Real Madrid a decade ago. At the time, she was working as a store assistant for Gucci in the Spanish capital. They share five children together: Cristiano Jr, 16 - Ronaldo's son from a previous relationship - Eva Maria and Mateo, 9, Alana, 8 and Bella, 4.

Inside Cristiano Ronaldo's lavish life with Georgina Rodriguez ahead of fairytale wedding READ MORE :

Rodriguez, 32, had announced their engagement last year, sharing a picture of her ring on social media with a message which translated: “Yes, I do. In this and in all my lives.”

‌



Rodriguez, a model, has become a huge figure on social media over the course of their relationship. A documentary about her, titled "I am Georgina", aired on Netflix in 2022 followed by subsequent series in 2023 and 2024.

Ronaldo spent the summer at the World Cup with Portugal but was left heartbroken when Roberto Martinez's side were eliminated in the round of 16 by eventual winners, Spain.

He confirmed during the tournament, during an interview with Morgan, that he and Rodriguez would wed later in the summer.

‌



View 3 Images (Image: cristiano/Instagram)

He said: “I hope to arrive at my wedding with the champion’s trophy. I’m going to marry her because I believe it’s the right time. Not just because she’s the mother of my children — but because she’s the person I love most.”

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star currently plays in the Saudi Pro League for Al-Nassr, who he joined after departing the Red Devils. Rodriguez has also seen him play in Italy for Juventus and was by his side when he made an emotional return to Manchester United back in the summer of 2021.

‌



Following Portugal's loss to Spain, Ronaldo confirmed it would be his final World Cup game as he reaches the final years of his career, saying: “I'm sad to be leaving the World Cup like this.

View 3 Images The couple got engaged last year (Image: Instagram)

“I gave it my all. I did my best. It was my last World Cup, yes, but I'll now have time to reflect and be with my family. I won't be making any rash decisions.

‌



“I don't decide anything in the heat of the moment. Now is not important whether I will continue [to play]. Tomorrow I will get up the same way I got up today: with a clear conscience.

“I played 23 years in the national team and won three titles. Before Cristiano, Portugal had not won anything. The Euros was the most important. For me, 2016 has the same dimension as a World Cup, honestly.”

Sports.title: Real Madrid plot shock Martin Zubimendi transfer as Arsenal left with dilemma
Sports.content:
Real Madrid plot shock Martin Zubimendi transfer as Arsenal left with dilemma

Real Madrid failed with a late attempt to lure Martin Zubimendi to the Bernabeu last summer but could now make another play for the Spaniard's services this month

View 2 Images Martin Zubimendi is again being courted by Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Real Madrid are said to be considering a surprise swoop for Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi - 12 months after failing to hijack the midfield maestro's move to the Premier League champions.

‌



Zubimendi was courted by a whole host of Europe's elite during his time at Real Sociedad with Liverpool going close to signing the 27-year-old back in the summer of 2024. The player had a late change of heart back then and chose to stay in Spain before moving to Arsenal during last summer's transfer window, despite late interest from Real Madrid.

‌



The playmaker featured in all 38 Premier League matches in his maiden season as a Gunner to help the club win their first league title in more than 20 years.

‌



But with Arsenal splashing out £75million on Bruno Guimaraes to further strengthen their midfield options, The Sun claim Real are ready to rekindle their interest in Zubimendi.

Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out READ MORE :

Whether Zubimendi is attainable or not is another matter with Mikel Arteta known to be a huge fan of the midfielder. It is thought, though, that Arsenal will have to sell if they are to give themselves the financial flexibility in the transfer market to 'level up' the team that almost completed the double last year after reaching the Champions League final, as per Arteta's wishes. And that could leave them with some difficult decisions to make in terms of outgoings.

It emerged on Tuesday that another highly-regarded player, Myles Lewis-Skelly, has been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United. It is currently unclear if Arsenal's London rivals will make a move for the 19-year-old Hale End graduate, though United are not expected to.

‌



Real Madrid's need for a midfielder is nothing new and they were previously believed to be the frontrunners to sign Rodri, with the Manchester City star open to a return to Spain this summer.

View 2 Images Real Madrid were favourites to sign Rodri but he now seems to be Barcelona-bound

The 30-year-old has entered the final year of his contract at The Etihad and the former Ballon d'Or winner was viewed as the ideal fit for the midfielder Jose Mourinho wants this summer.

Article continues below

But Real are now said to be behind Barcelona in the race for Rodri's services, even though their arch-rivals have seen an opening bid for the player turned down by City.

Sports.title: Freddie Flintoff's son Rocky, 18, smashes first career century off just 65 balls
Sports.content:
Freddie Flintoff's son Rocky, 18, smashes first career century off just 65 balls

Rocky Flintoff notched up his first career hundred in brutal fashion as Lancashire hammered Somerset in the One Day Cup

View 2 Images Rocky Flintoff scored his first career century (Image: Getty Images)

Freddie Flintoff's 18-year-old son Rocky proved himself a chip off the old block as he bludgeoned a brutal first career century.

‌



Flintoff Jr was in action for Lancashire in the Metro Bank One Day Cup and helped his side seal a place in the knockout stage with an astonishing display of hitting.

‌



Batting first against Somerset, Lancashire had been reduced to 138-3 when Flintoff entered the fray in the 23rd over.

‌



He shared a stand of 214 with Keaton Jennings, who finished with 156 off 127 balls.

Andrew Flintoff releases statement after shock England departure and confirms next job READ MORE :

Flintoff's hundred came off just 65 balls and he scored a total of 123 runs from 76 deliveries before being caught by Archie Vaughan, son of Freddie's former England captain Michael.

Lancashire scored a mammoth 443-6, bowling Somerset out for 269 in reply to set up a home knockout clash against Ben Stokes' Durham.

‌



It comes just three days after Freddie confirmed he was standing down as head coach of England Lions. He will coach Sydney Thunder in Australia's Big Bash League this winter.

Posting on Instagram, Flintoff said; "Unfortunately, I’ve made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions. Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

View 2 Images Rocky proved himself a chip off the old block (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

"I’d like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give everyday.

"In particular Ed Barney who I’ve loved working with and was so lucky to have as a performance director, and obviously Rob [Key] for trusting me with one of the most Important roles in English cricket.

"I can’t wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me. Good luck to whoever takes over you have some big pants to fill."

Sports.title: Man Utd make decision on top transfer target after Myles Lewis-Skelly U-turn
Sports.content:
Man Utd make decision on top transfer target after Myles Lewis-Skelly U-turn

Manchester United are in the market for another central midfielder and also want to add a left-back but do not appear to be considering a move for Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly

View 2 Images Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly could be on the move (Image: (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images))

Manchester United are set to continue their pursuit of Lewis Hall in their search for a new left-back despite once again being offered the chance to sign Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.

‌



The Red Devils have prioritised midfielders in the transfer window this summer, completing deals for Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. It's understood the club would like to add another central midfielder before the deadline, however, there are other areas which still need strengthening ahead of the upcoming Premier League campaign.

‌



United would ideally like to add another left-back who has the potential to become Luke Shaw's long-term successor at Old Trafford.

‌



Hall has been a priority target despite doubts over whether Newcastle, having already sanctioned significant sales for Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, would consider doing a deal.

Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

But United's stance hasn't changed according to The Sun, who claim they have no interest in pursuing a deal for Lewis-Skelly.

The Arsenal midfielder has featured prominently for the Premier League champions at left-back and was previously offered to United via an intermediary back in January. At the time, they were understood to be more receptive to a deal, although they were quoted a price of around £60million for the 19-year-old.

‌



Arsenal have grand ambitions to level up the squad that came within a whisker of a Premier League and Champions League double and player sales will be necessary to facilitate further quality signings. As an academy graduate, any funds raised from selling Lewis-Skelly would equate to pure profit, giving Arsenal greater financial flexibility in the market. Chelsea have also been offered the chance to sign Lewis-Skelly.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall is Manchester United's preferred left-back target (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Hall remains United's priority transfer target and, while Newcastle do not want to lose him, the player is keen on moving to Old Trafford, the report adds.

‌



His desire to pursue a new challenge is likely to represent an early headache for the club's new head coach, Matthias Jaissle, who has replaced Eddie Howe at the helm.

Hall has established himself as one of the top left-back's in the Premier League since joining Newcastle from Chelsea back in 2023. The 21-year-old made 30 appearances in the league for Newcastle last term, scoring one goal.

Sports.title: Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem
Sports.content:
Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem

Martin Zubimendi is being linked with the Arsenal exit door after only one year and the signing of Bruno Guimaraes suggests the Spaniard will be shunted down the pecking order

View 4 Images Arsenal signing of Bruno Guimaraes could have a knock on affect on the squad (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

When someone of Bruno Guimaraes' calibre arrives at Arsenal, amid all the fanfare, there will be someone wondering if their time is up.

‌



The Brazilian has just moved to the Emirates for £75million after making it known that the Gunners were the club for him. This is a player who could play for any team in Europe and he will inevitably make Arsenal better.

‌



But following his arrival, that leaves one player having to go out and as part of the fallout reports have emerged that Arsenal have named their price on Martin Zubimendi. That generally only happens for players who could be on the move.

‌



You don't see any prices being quoted for Declan Rice, because he's one of Arsenal's untouchables, if they ever did make such a list. Zubimendi less so and after only a year at Arsenal the Spaniard could be set for a new role, and one he may not enjoy, if he stays.

It's a huge change for a player who, it was well documented, Mikel Arteta had eyed for several years before eventually luring him to London. This was a player who dominated England in the Euro 2024 final, making replacing Rodri look a simple task.

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

But elite clubs only go looking for players in areas where they think they can improve. You hear no noise around Arsenal landing a top class centre-half, because in William Saliba and Gabriel, they have what they need. You hear no noise around Manchester City signing a top tier No.9, because they have Erling Haaland.

‌



Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes showed that they feel they can upgrade in that position. Rice is their talisman but alongside him there's been plenty of contenders. Mikel Merino is one, albeit very versatile, Zubimendi another. Myles Lewis-Skelly may have ambitions to play in that role.

If Zubimendi is to shift from a player who was guaranteed to start to one who isn't, then perhaps the warning signs were there. This is a player who started 34 of 38 games last season - but was benched for three of the final four.

View 4 Images Martin Zubimendi increasingly found himself on the bench towards the end of the season

‌



The Spaniard's minutes were cut and he endured the embarrassment of being subbed on, and then off, by Arteta. That came in the vital win over West Ham with Zubimendi coming on in the 28th minute for the injured Ben White. But his afternoon lasted less than 40 minutes and he was hauled off in the 67th minute for Kai Havertz.

"It is never easy to do that to a player, especially someone with Martin’s quality," Arteta admitted after the game.

Weeks later and Lewis-Skelly, who had been snubbed for much of the season, was picked to play in the Champions League final against PSG. Zubimendi started on the bench, and that's where he would remain for the evening.

‌



Managers can talk all they want about the value and the importance of a player, but what really tells is whether they call upon them come crunch time. With the title in the balance and a European Cup on the line, Zubimendi found himself overlooked.

View 4 Images The Spaniard did claim the Premier League title in his first campaign with Arsenal

When Zubimendi signed from Real Sociedad the club's sporting director, Andrea Berta, claimed: "Martin was a key target for us and we all know that he is a perfect fit for our squad with the high quality he has."

‌



That fit does not look so perfect now following Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes. Arteta has a squad that is the envy of most of Europe, but he'll find that having so many options creates as many problems as solutions it solves.

Arsenal have effectively played with two holding midfielders and a 10, previously Martin Odegaard. The Norwegian too is a man under pressure for his spot. Going on the fact that Rice is the pillar and Guimaraes, the second most expensive player in Arsenal history, will start - where does that leave Zubimendi?

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta has some difficult decisions regarding the make-up of his midfield

‌



A possibility exists that Arsenal play with more of a flat three in midfield. But where does that leave Odegaard. Or Eberechi Eze, who played centrally last season, or Kai Havertz or eventually Max Dowman?

Arsenal were pipped on penalties by PSG last season as their European Cup dreams were ended in heartbreaking fashion. On that night in Budapest, for all their battling spirit and defensive quality, it was clear that the Gunners had levels to go in the final third to match PSG.

This summer has been about closing that gap. Guimaraes is the type of player who helps them play through the lines. Their pursuit of Vinicius Junior was well publicised.

‌



Arsenal are firmly back among Europe's elite, capping an impressive rise under Arteta's leadership, but if there's one conundrum they're yet to face during the assembly of their stunning squad, it is who to back. In recent years no major player has wanted out, but with so many top class operators now available some will inevitably end up being cannon fodder in the club's grand plan.

Zubimendi may be one of the early lessons.
