Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Which of Antonelli’s rivals is his biggest threat for the championship this year? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s strong position in the lead of the championship standings at the summer break is remarkable enough already for a driver in his second season in Formula 1.

But what makes his position all the more impressive is that, arguably, no single driver has yet emerged as his clear rival. Antonelli has won six of the 11 rounds so far, more than the rest put together, and only his team mate George Russell has taken multiple wins.

Despite that, Russell is not Antonelli’s closest rival in the standings: Lewis Hamilton is leading a resurgent Ferrari. Plus, the final round before the summer break saw McLaren claim their first victory of the season. Three of the last five grands prix were won by teams other than Mercedes – could Antonelli biggest threat come from one of them?

Lewis Hamilton

50 points behind

The possibility of Hamilton fighting for the championship against the driver who took the Mercedes seat he vacated last year is a compelling narrative. But is it a likely outcome? Hamilton is Antonelli’s closest rival in the points but has missed opportunities due to penalties in recent races.

George Russell

59 points behind

Russell should be Antonelli’s closest rival for the championship but various factors have left him well behind including unreliability (not that Antonelli has been immune), some misfortune and his risky first-lap lunge at Spa. He’s also on course to incur a power unit change penalty before his team mate. Still, Russell should have the equipment and the experience to put Antonelli under pressure.

Charles Leclerc

81 points behind

Hamilton may be closer to Antonelli in the standings but Charles Leclerc has arguably looked more competitive. Providing he avoids a repeat of the dip he fell into around Spain and Monaco, he could emerge as Antonelli’s biggest threat.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Lando Norris

91 points behind

Like Mercedes, unreliability has dogged McLaren this year. They often haven’t been quick enough either, though Norris has now won both a grand prix and a sprint race. The MCL40’s Hungaroring upgrade clearly paid off, and may prove enough to bring the McLarens into regular contention. The reigning world champion is a long way behind, though.

Max Verstappen

110 points behind

If last year demonstrated anything, it is unwise to write off Max Verstappen if he is not mathematically out of contention. Having been 104 points off the lead with 249 remaining, he eventually lost by the narrowest margin in F1 history (relatively). But lying 110 points behind in a car which hasn’t won a grand prix yet may be too much even for him.

Oscar Piastri

127 points behind

Oscar Piastri has proved a close match on pace for his team mate as usual but he’s even further behind in the standings. He went into the final round of last season with a shot at the championship but that doesn’t look likely to happen this year.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Isack Hadjar

151 points behind

Isack Hadjar has impressed with the quality of his performances alongside Verstappen and may yet recover the points he dropped after losing his podium finish in Monaco. But his points deficit to Antonelli is surely too large and the Red Bull not competitive enough yet for him to be a realistic title contender.

I say

Hamilton may be closest in the points but Russell surely has the better combination of opportunity and equipment at the moment. If he can stop the rot in the second half of the season I would back him to put Antonelli under pressure for the title.

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Wants Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn Winner After Rolly
Sports.content:
“Ryan Garcia, the winner, Conor Benn, Ryan Garcia, that’s what’s going straight right there,” Teofimo Sr. said to Fight Hub TV. “And then if Liam Paro is still around or whoever else it is, man, we’re just going to try to take over the weight division at 147, become undisputed again.”

The trainer made his interest in the Garcia-Benn winner clear earlier in the interview.

“That’s a good fight. And I think that we’ll take the winner out of that,” he said. “Especially, whoever wins, it’ll be a great fight. Either it’s Ryan, or it’s Conor Benn. And we’re ready to do it, man.”

That plan depends first on Teofimo beating Romero, which isn’t guaranteed after his one-sided loss to Shakur Stevenson in January. Moving to welterweight gives Lopez a chance to leave that performance behind while immediately fighting for another world title.

His father believes the additional seven pounds will make Teofimo faster and more effective rather than slowing him down.

“I think he should be able to do everything in less than two years, become undisputed,” Lopez Sr. said. “All these fighters are going to be slower than him, and he’s a really smart fighter in there.”

Senior also identified his son’s mental state as the biggest danger to those plans.

“All I know is this is the time where we got to be focused, and my son got to be in his best mental mind ever,” Lopez Sr said. “That’s the only thing that could mess up my son. Everything is mental with him.”

Teofimo has already named Devin Haney, Garcia and Liam Paro among the champions and contenders he wants at welterweight. His father’s version puts the Garcia-Benn winner at the front of the line after Romero.

If Lopez beats Rolly, Garcia and Benn will settle their own business three weeks later.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Admits Money Could Move Joshua-Fury To New York
Sports.content:
“Everybody wants to do the fight in New York apart from Anthony Joshua and me. We’re under a huge amount of pressure,” Hearn said to the Punch podcast. “We’re being told by Turki Alashikh and those guys, look, Netflix particularly, you know, they really want to do the fight in the US.”

Hearn acknowledged the commercial argument for taking Joshua and Fury to America while stressing that it was not the deal Joshua originally accepted.

“I don’t agree with their arguments, but I’m not paying the money. Do you know what I mean? But we wouldn’t have signed the contract if the fight was in America,” said Hearn.

This stance places Joshua’s team in a strong position. Organizers who believe New York generates substantially more revenue can compensate Joshua for giving up the UK location.

Hearn has made it clear that organizers cannot simply announce the switch and expect Joshua to go along with it.

“If they announce that fight without an agreement in place to change the venue, there will be no fight,” Hearn said. “And we ain’t bluffing.”

Hearn’s later comments show this dispute is not an absolute refusal to fight in America. His strategy aims to make changing the location so expensive that keeping the event in Britain becomes the easier option.

“If you want to do it in America, you got to pay us all this money to change because we’re not really bothered about the money. We want it in England.”

Hearn then revealed where the negotiation can ultimately lead.

“We want to make it so much money they just go, ‘Oh, do you know what? Let’s just do it in England.’ That’s our dream scenario. But they might pay the money, and then we got no choice.”

The issue becomes where the breaking point sits. Joshua can demand a substantial premium because his approval is required. Pushing too far, however, risks eliminating the financial advantage organizers see in New York.

Moving the fight away from Britain would also give Joshua an explanation to UK fans. Hearn can argue they fought to keep the event at home, accepting New York only after receiving an offer too lucrative to turn down.

The harder Hearn pushes now, the easier that explanation becomes later.

New York may be the preferred location for the event’s financial backers, yet Joshua’s side controls the cost of the agreement. The remaining question is how badly they want his signature.

Sports.title: Can Kaye Scott Pull Off The Massive Upset Against Claressa Shields?
Sports.content:
A product of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, Kaye Scott had a decorated 15-year amateur career on the Australian national team. Scott made her pro debut in November 2023 as she outpointed Connie Chan.

In the second fight of her pro career, Kaye Scott defeated Desley Robinson via majority decision. Nine months later, Scott and Robinson would participate in a high-stakes rematch.

Much like the first fight, Kaye Scott came out very aggressively, as she pressed forward and worked off the jab. It was a very competitive, action-packed bout, but in the end, Desley Robinson defeated Scott and won the vacant IBF middleweight world title.

One year later, Kaye Scott would receive another chance to fight for a world title. This time she took advantage of the opportunity as she beat Olivia Curry via majority decision and won the WBC and vacant WBA titles.

Now the 42-year-old Kaye Scott (5-1-1) is set to face the biggest challenge of her professional career. On the night of August 15th, Scott will be defending her unified title against a woman who is a 19-time world champion.

Kaye Scott is a pressure fighter who’s most effective in the mid-range. Her opponent, Claressa Shields, is a technical boxer who has all the tools. Shields has the high IQ, footwork, elite handspeed, and excellent punch placement.

Realistically speaking, most fight fans feel Scott is overmatched, and it should be a short night of work for Shields. However, there are two distinct reasons why the defending champion has a chance to pull off the upset of the year.

The first reason is the fact that Scott is familiar with Shields because she is a former sparring partner. The second reason is due to the weight cut. In her last ring appearance, Shields fought at 173.6 pounds.

In the upcoming unified middleweight world title fight, Claressa Shields has to drop down to 160. Shields has been competing at heavyweight for the past two years, and the question is, will the weight cut affect her power and stamina?

Kaye Scott hasn’t been doing much talking, but in a recent IG post, the defending WBC, WBA middleweight world champion displayed confidence.

“Locked in for August 15th. No noise. No distractions. Stay in my lane, and bring the heat.”

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Facing August 20 WBO Deadline For Callum Smith Defense
Sports.content:
Olivieri stated that the extension through August 20 fits the WBO policy of maintaining one world champion per division while eliminating interim belts.

The order puts pressure on Bivol, who holds the WBO title along with the IBF and IBO belts. Callum holds the WBO interim title and has been waiting for his shot at the full championship.

Both fighters work with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom, which should simplify negotiations compared to promotional rivalries.

Bivol returned from elbow surgery on May 30, defeating Michael Eifert by a 12-round wide unanimous decision in Ekaterinburg, Russia. All three judges scored the fight 120-107.

Smith earned his spot by defeating Joshua Buatsi by unanimous decision in February 2025. That victory gave the former super middleweight champion the WBO interim light heavyweight belt and positioned him for Bivol.

Bivol has a bigger financial option elsewhere. A third fight with Artur Beterbiev offers a far larger purse after they split their first two meetings, leaving the Smith mandatory competing with a much more lucrative fight. That leaves Bivol with nine days to decide how he handles Smith’s challenge.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Roasts BoMac Over Conor Benn Pick
Sports.content:
“Ryan is burnt. He hasn’t been the same since his first fight with Tank. He got popped. He never got back into his type,” McIntyre said to Brian Custer on his channel. “I’ve seen Benn firsthand. Man, he’s going to hurt that dude.”

The Ring amplified the knockout pick on X earlier today, drawing a response from Ryan.

“All he needs to worry about is to stop eating all them f*****g chips and taking care of his body and temple. Cause his Brain ain’t working for shit,” Garcia posted.

McIntyre left “popped” undefined, though fans familiar with Ryan’s positive Ostarine tests after his April 2024 fight against Devin Haney may connect the comment to that episode.

The Haney performance complicates the claim of a post-Tank decline. Ryan dropped Haney three times, winning a 12-round majority decision before the result was changed to a no-contest over the positive tests.

His ring return after serving the suspension offered a stronger argument for McIntyre. Garcia hit the canvas in round two against Rolly Romero in May 2025 and struggled to produce sustained offense in a unanimous decision loss.

That performance gave BoMac more ammunition for his criticism. Garcia chose personal insults rather than answering it.

Sports.title: Hearn: Devin Haney Wants Purse Without Promotional Risk
Sports.content:
“The reality is a lot of these fighters have this sort of grand illusion that they really can run their own promotional company and take over,” Hearn told the Punch Podcast. “They love to have a promotional company, and they love their logo on the ring mat and on the poster, but I’ve worked with these guys before, Devin Haney included, and when it comes down to it, they don’t really want to take any responsibility or financial risk in a show.”

Hearn gave an example involving Haney, claiming he offered a true co-promotional partnership that was quickly turned down.

“I’ve said to Devin before, you know, if you want, we’ll go 50/50 on the show. Oh, no, no, no. I said, but if it don’t work, are you going to pay half? No. Just what’s my purse?”

A true 50-50 arrangement would require sharing the financial downside if an event failed to generate enough revenue.

“You want David Diamante to go, ‘In association with Devin Haney Promotions,’” Hearn continued.

While Haney now enjoys greater control over his career decisions, Hearn maintains that independent fighters still depend on established promoters to execute major events. He pointed to Rolando Romero’s fight against Teofimo Lopez as a PBC operation, despite the fighters maintaining their own business banners.

“These guys don’t have the infrastructure and the ability to run high-level operations and shows,” Hearn said.

While maintaining a promotional entity gives Haney leverage at the negotiating table, Hearn’s point remains simple: putting your logo on a poster is vastly different from putting your own money on the line.

Sports.title: Guido Vianello Added To Thin Itauma-Hrgovic PPV
Sports.content:
The 14-3-1 contender is coming off a fifth-round knockout of Alexis Barriere last October. His recent opposition includes Richard Torrez Jr., Arslanbek Makhmudov and Efe Ajagba.

An eighth-round stoppage of Makhmudov in August 2024 is the best result on his record, coming four months after a close split decision loss to Ajagba. Torrez later defeated him by unanimous decision last April.

That experience gives the PPV another recognizable heavyweight on a card built around an intriguing but still unproven 21-year-old headliner.

Itauma is taking a major step up against 34-year-old Hrgovic for the vacant IBF heavyweight title. Hrgovic remains one of the division’s established contenders, but the punishment he has absorbed in recent fights has begun to show. Itauma is being given the opportunity to capitalize against a warhorse who may no longer be at his best.

Sam Noakes against 38-year-old former WBO lightweight champion Denys Berinchyk is the other recognizable supporting fight. Cruiserweight prospect Aloys Youmbi faces 40-year-old Mike Perez, while Constantin Ursu meets Ben Vaughan for the British and Commonwealth welterweight titles.

Beyond those bouts, the card relies largely on prospects and domestic-level fighters.

David Adeleye had previously been linked with Vianello before leaving Queensberry Promotions. With Vianello now confirmed for August 29, the quality of the opponent Queensberry finds for him becomes important on a PPV card that needs another meaningful fight.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Insists He Wants Devin Haney Fight, Hears Nothing
Sports.content:
“Haney is ducking me,” Paro told Fox Sports Australia. “I’ve said I’m good to fight by the end of October, and we ain’t heard a thing.”

Paro also rejected the idea that his financial demands caused negotiations to stall.

“I’ll fight him next, no worries. You know I’ll fight anyone. And I’ve proved that my whole career. I’ll fight him in his backyard or mine.”

The former IBF champion may have more to offer Haney commercially than Catterall. Paro brings name recognition and interest from the Australian market. Despite his loss to Richardson Hitchins, he remains a rugged southpaw with enough power and physical strength to make Haney work.

Catterall involves a different type of difficulty. He is a defensive southpaw who moves, potshots, pulls away when opponents close distance, and frequently ties up. That could produce a difficult tactical contest for Haney without necessarily generating the same financial upside as facing Paro.

Catterall’s willingness to step in still gives Haney an important bargaining chip. His manager, Sam Jones, says they have accepted the proposed date and location while accusing Paro of wanting too much money.

Haney also received some unwelcome news from Ryan Garcia this week. Garcia placed Teofimo Lopez, Rolando Romero, and Shakur Stevenson among the opponents he wants after facing Conor Benn on September 12.

“I’m not in a rush to make that fight happen,” Ryan told The Ring about facing Haney again. “They have to sit with that loss.”

That leaves Haney needing someone to fight. Paro may think the silence means Haney is avoiding him, but it may simply be Team Haney waiting to see which welterweight gives them the better deal.

Ghana News.title: South Africa dump site collapse kills 14 suspected illegal miners
Ghana News.content:
South African police have launched an investigation after 14 suspected illegal miners died when a mine dump site collapsed on them on Monday night.

Eight others were injured and "an unknown number... may still be trapped underground", police said in a statement.

The site was being legally operated by a mining company and it is unclear how the miners, most of whom are believed to be from neighbouring Lesotho, gained access.

Illegal mining is rife in South Africa as miners, known in South Africa as "zama zamas" ("those who try their luck" in Zulu), try to eke out a living by digging in abandoned shafts or dump sites.

Regional police chief Lt-Gen Arthur Adams, who visited the scene on Tuesday morning, said that the dump site was being used to mine platinum and other metals by a local company.

He told local broadcaster Newzroom Afrika that the "walls of the dumping site... caved in on them [the zama zamas]".

Adams said that three of the injured miners have since been released from hospital and have been detained by police.

He confirmed that all the zama zamas are undocumented foreign nationals and will also face illegal mining and trespassing charges.

Adams said the search continues for any miners who may still be trapped under the rubble.

"As it stands, the excavation operations have ceased," he said.

Injuries and deaths of illegal miners are not uncommon in South Africa, especially at abandoned mine shafts.

In January last year, 78 bodies were recovered from a disused shaft in Stilfontein, south-west of Johannesburg,

The miners had been stuck there following a nationwide police operation to end illicit mining at disused sites that had closed, as the industry – once the backbone of the country's economy – was shrinking.

It is no longer profitable for mining multinationals to operate in many places, but the promise of still finding gold deposits proves was a magnet for many desperate people particularly undocumented migrants.

Ghana News.title: Thailand suspends new gun permits after mass shooting
Ghana News.content:
Mourners pray for the 12-year-old who died after being shot at the school outside Bangkok

Thailand's government will immediately stop issuing gun permits after a shooting incident last week in which a 14-year-old killed eight people and himself.

Existing gun owners are already banned from carrying their weapons in public.

The South East Asian country has one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in the region, with around 10.3 million firearms in civilian possession, and high levels of gun crime.

In response to the recent shooting, the prime minister has promised to pass tough new gun control laws with severe penalties, suspending new permits in the meantime.

Last Friday, a pupil at Debsirin Nonthaburi School outside Bangkok shot his grandparents using a handgun owned by his grandfather, before opening fire at teachers and students at school, authorities say.

Both grandparents, five staff members at the school and one 12-year-old girl died.

Police believe the shooter may have taught himself to use a gun via social media.

They say there is evidence that the boy watched violent content online, and that he showed a strong interest in learning how to handle guns.

His consumption of this content as well as anxiety over studies and family issues might have also fuelled his actions, they add.

Officials paid their respects to the victims on Tuesday at a Nonthaburi temple

Until further notice, no new permits to purchase or own guns will be issued. Existing purchase permits will not be renewed but it is unclear what will happen to existing gun ownership permits.

Permits to carry guns were suspended in late 2023 - owners must keep their weapons at home or at a shooting range.

The government is also considering measures to persuade the owners of an estimated four million unlicensed guns to hand them over in the wake of the school shooting.

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has said the announced measures will remain in place as the government works to pass new gun control laws, with stronger controls and significantly harsher penalties.

Gun control advocates have called for mental health assessments as part of the permit process, and for permits to be periodically re-evaluated.

Anutin has said stricter ammunition controls are in his sights, while the education minister has proposed screening at the entrance of schools to stop students from bringing in weapons.

Ghana News.title: France bans unsolicited telemarketing calls
Ghana News.content:
France has banned unsolicited telemarketing phone calls, in what a consumer group is hailing as a "small revolution" for the sales industry.

From Tuesday, unsolicited calls are prohibited for businesses in all sectors - but there are some exceptions.

Calls will only be permitted if they relate to a contract a person has already entered into or the company has obtained prior consent to be contacted for marketing.

"It cannot be stressed enough that peace and quiet is a right, and it is time to stop exposing consumers to unwanted solicitations," consumer advocacy group Que Choisir Ensemble said in a statement.

"This observation also holds true online and on the street, which are saturated with demands to consume," group president Marie-Amandine Stévenin added.

She said the group had long been advocating "for an end to the automatic assumption that someone in their home or private life is a potential customer."

"This is a victory for consumers, the vast majority of whom do not want to receive sales calls," she said.

But the law change has riled some business groups, and officials in Morocco, where the call centre sector is heavily reliant on the French market.

One government minister estimated the telemarketing restrictions could lead to the loss of up to 50,000 jobs, according to a report in Moroccan newspaper Le Matin.

The head of France's direct-selling trade association, the Fédération de la Vente Directe (FVD), also criticised the reforms for adding what he said were administrative burdens for businesses.

"You'll have to obtain written consent from your customer, and you'll also have to keep proof of that consent," Frédéric Billon said in comments reported by the New York Times.

According to a 2025 parliamentary report, 97% of people are annoyed by telemarketing calls, with the authors wryly noting it is "one of those rare issues that unites people in France".

The same report found 72% of French people reported being contacted on their mobile phones at least once a week, while 38% said they were called once a day.

Germany, Austria and Italy are among the European countries that impose significant restrictions on telemarketing calls, often referred to as cold calls.

In the UK, most telemarketing calls are legal provided the recipient has not objected to the call and their number is not on a statutory list of people or businesses who do not want to receive calls.

Ghana News.title: Anne Hathaway pokes fun at ‘fake baby bump’ theories
Ghana News.content:
Anne Hathaway has poked fun at those who suggested her baby bump didn't look real after a recent film premiere, telling them she had "fake hair, real bump".

The US actress turned heads in an outfit that showed off her bare bump at the launch of her new film, The End of Oak Street, in Los Angeles on Sunday.

It sparked a flurry of comments on social media from people saying "Why does it look fake?" and "Oh come on. That is not real."

But others cameto her defence, with one writing: "A lot of people in these comments have never seen a pregnant belly on someone who has abs."

Another questioned: "Can women exist, damn," while someone else posted: "People always commenting about women is insane."

Hathaway, 43, announced in June that she is expecting her third child with husband Adam Shulman.

Celebrities are often judged on their choice of red carpet wear, but Hathaway's outfit at the premiere for The End of Oak Street has attracted particular attention.

Her bump was partially exposed in the custom Atelier Prabal Gurung crop top, which the designer described as a "sculptural high-low halter top with a cascading train". Hathaway paired the top with low-rise La Ligne jeans and red Aquazzura stilettos.

Hathaway stars with Ewan McGregor in the new film

"Fake hair, real bump," the actress wrote on Instagram with a video of her getting ready and attending the premiere.

"Enjoy The @endofoakstreet Block Party chaos with me as my outfit literally melts in the heat!!"

As well as raising unfounded doubts about the bump, some people criticised the star's attire on social media, calling it "ridiculous", "tacky" and "bizarre".

But others praised her. Charlotte Cripps wrote in the Independent: "It might be an outfit that her social media critics wouldn't be seen dead in, but it's a clear message of body positivity, strength, and gender equality – and it's her unique expression of the next chapter of her life."

An op ed in Vogue stated: "What the rest of us need to realise is that a woman's baby bump is none of our business (can't believe this still needs saying).

"What if, instead, we celebrated the fact that a woman's body is doing something amazing, rather than telling her that she looks shameful, fake, "over the top" or "awful and a bit weird"? Now that really would be radical."

The Telegraph's Rebecca Cope said: "Though drawing criticism from some, the look is just the latest example of a celebrity literally letting it all hang out."

Hathaway's appearance on Sunday also led to a surge in interest in her "coconut water" nails look.

Anne Hathaway's recent red carpet looks

The star has been in the spotlight throughout the summer, promoting The Odyssey at its premiere in London on 6 July (below).

She also donned red carpet maternity wear at The Odyssey's US premiere in New York on 14 July.

Ghana News.title: The Office actress Lucy Davis says she has ‘incurable’ cancer
Ghana News.content:
Lucy Davis, who played Dawn Tinsley in the original UK version of The Office, has revealed she has "incurable" breast cancer.

Davis, the daughter of comedian Jasper Carrott, appeared frequently as the sympathetic and witty office receptionist in the groundbreaking mockumentary, from 2001 to 2003.

A post from the 53-year-old actress on Instagram on Tuesday said: "I wanted to share something with you all that I've kept to myself for a while but for various reasons would like to share now.

"A year-and-a-half ago I was diagnosed with stage 4 breast cancer, which has metastasised [spread] to my bones. Specifically to my spine, right hip and my ribs. The cancer is incurable, and too late for chemo."

Davis played Etta Candy in 2017's Wonder Woman film

She added: "The initial lump that I felt, wasn't a 'lump' as such; rather a kind of hard spot. Really tiny. I almost didn't bother getting it checked. So I guess I'm saying don't ignore anything – get everything checked out.

"As of now, I'm trying to live out whatever might be left of my life in as fun a way as I possibly can. I always like to find the teachable moments in anything negative that happens. And cancer has not disappointed in that regard; there's a lot I have learned from it, and I'm grateful for that."

She continued: "I'm not scared of whatever comes next. I'm at peace with it. I'll see my [late dog] Gracie sooner than expected, and for me, leaving my physical body just means going home. Any and all grieving is for my family; it's far harder for them than for me."

'Cancer asks a lot from us'

Birmingham-born Davis played receptionist Dawn, who was also the love interest of Tim Canterbury, played by Martin Freeman in Ricky Gervais's classic TV sitcom - which last month celebrated its 25th anniversary.

After The Office, Davis went on to feature as Dianne in 2004 comedy-horror film Shaun of the Dead and Etta Candy in 2017's Wonder Woman, as well as Hilda Spellman in Netflix series The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina.

More recently, she played Eva in the Disney Channel's action-comedy series The Villains of Valley View.

In her Instagram post - which was accompanied by a video of her reading a poem while ringing a bell in hospital - she went on to say she intended to keep up her work supporting animal rights, which is "so important to me".

She went on: "I still would like to keep working. I'm perfectly able to do so, and acting is one of the biggest joys in my life.

"For those of you on a similar journey to mine, I do wish you well. Cancer asks a lot from us, physically and mentally. And we all get to do it however we choose."

Symptoms of breast cancer

According to Cancer Research UK, stage four breast cancer is a cancer that starts in the breast tissue but spreads to another part of the body, making it incurable. Treatment can control the cancer for some years, however.

The main symptoms of breast cancer in women may include a lump or swelling in your breast, chest or armpit, the NHS website says.

Symptoms can also include a change in the skin of your breast such as dimpling or redness, a change in size or shape of one or both breasts, and/or nipple discharge (if you are not pregnant or breastfeeding), which may have blood in it.

Other symptoms may include a change in the shape or look of the nipple, such as it turning inwards or a rash on it.

Ghana News.title: Pogba expected to have Monaco contract terminated
Ghana News.content:
Paul Pogba is expected to leave Monaco amid talks over a possible contract termination.

The former World Cup winner joined the Ligue 1 side last summer after he was permitted to return to professional football after a doping suspension.

Pogba signed a two-year deal, which was due to run until the end of the forthcoming season.

But a source has told the BBC discussions over an early exit are under way and are expected to be concluded soon.

Monaco have not yet commented on the situation.

Pogba's first season at Monaco was disrupted by injury, but there was hope this season would see the France international play regularly.

But a change in manager, after Filipe Luis replaced Sebastien Pocognoli, could see Monaco head in a different direction in central midfield.

Pogba was provisionally banned from football for four years after a positive test for dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in February 2024, following a doping test in August 2023.

Pogba maintained it was a mistake and that he was given a supplement without knowing it contained a banned substance.

The France international, a 2018 World Cup winner, was permitted to return to football in March 2025 following the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision to reduce his ban to 18 months.

Ghana News.title: Doku ‘not against’ journalist who criticised him at World Cup
Ghana News.content:
Jeremy Doku says he is "not against" the journalist who criticised his plan to leave the Belgium camp during the World Cup to attend the birth of his first child.

Doku's wife Shireen was due to give birth during the second week of July and he told Reuters, before the start of the tournament he intended to leave the camp to be at the birth even if his side were still in contention.

But it brought fierce criticism from L'Equipe channel presenter France Pierron, who labelled a father "completely useless" at the time of their child's birth.

L'Equipe later apologised and said Pierron's comments were "very far removed" from its values. The presenter also apologised but was taken off air until the end of the season of her show.

Doku eventually missed Belgium's 0-0 draw against Iran in the group stage to fly back to the UK for the birth of his son, Praise.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, external, Doku said he understood why some people questioned the timing of events.

"There was a lot of noise, of course," the Manchester City winger said.

"I can understand why people felt like maybe this was orchestrated because it was too perfect.

"I also saw the journalist speak about me and the situation and all the people getting at her. But I just wanted to use this video as well to really... pray over her.

"I don't want to come at her in a way that most people did. I don't want people to be too harsh on her. We don't know what she has experienced. It's her opinion.

"She got fired and all these things. I never want this for a person. I'm not against her. I'm not angry at her or anything. She just said her opinion."

Doku played 86 minutes of Belgium's opening 1-1 draw with Egypt in Group G of the World Cup before missing their next game, with his absence explained as illness.

A Belgium statement later said, that the 24-year-old travelled to London to be with his wife "with the approval of and accompanied by one of our team doctors".

Ghana News.title: Obuasi court remands 2 teachers over alleged attack on SHS headmaster
Ghana News.content:
The Obuasi Circuit Court has remanded two teachers of Obuasi Senior High Technical School into police custody for one week over allegations that they incited students to attack the school’s headmaster.

Kwasi Brefo, 41, and Joseph Appiah Arthur, 34, appeared before the court for the first time on Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

They have been charged with two counts of abetment under the Criminal and Other Offences Act, 1960.

The court has ordered the two teachers to reappear on August 17, 2026.

The prosecution told the court that the suspects aided and abetted students to cause unlawful damage to property belonging to the school.

They are also accused of instigating students to attack the headmaster, Abdulai Zakaria, on August 4.

Obuasi District Commander, Superintendent Mahama Iddrisu, had earlier told JoyNews that the two suspects were among three teachers arrested following a complaint from the headmaster.

Meanwhile, police are awaiting an autopsy and DNA examination on a male foetus exhumed from a location close to one of the school’s dormitories.

Superintendent Iddrisu said the foetus, which was discovered on August 5, is being kept at the morgue of the Obuasi Government Hospital.

The headmaster, Abdulai Iddrisu, who sustained machete injuries during the incident, has since been discharged from the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Colombia scrambles to find survivors after deadly earthquake
World.content:
Cali, Colombia – A day after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake shook western Colombia, rescue teams are frantically fighting through the rubble of collapsed buildings to find survivors and recover bodies.

The powerful quake has caused at least 254 deaths nationwide, most of them concentrated in the cities of Pereira and Cali, according to government figures.

“For me, the earthquake felt eternal,” recalled Luis Saenz, a 22-year-old journalism student from Cali.

Saenz was at home enjoying his morning coffee when the quake struck at 7:34am (12:34 GMT) on Monday. He remembers his cat darting under the bed, then chaos as his family fled into the street.

Some 5,000 homes suffered damage, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, while dozens of buildings – many of them residential – collapsed entirely.

In Cali, Colombia’s third-largest city, at least 95 people died, and 45 structures have fully or partially collapsed, according to local government statistics.

“I never thought I would see my city like this,” resident Maria Isabel Cumbal said between sobs, as she watched rescue efforts unfold at the Vanessa Building in the south of the city.

The seven-storey residential apartment block was reduced to wreckage in Monday's earthquake.

Rescuers now wield hammers, shovels and heavy machinery in an attempt to pierce through thick slabs of concrete and rescue the estimated 20 people trapped underneath.

On and around the collapsed residence, hundreds of volunteers help to clear the rubble by forming a human chain to pass buckets from atop the mound of debris down to dump trucks.

Every so often, a rescuer will hold up a fist to call for silence, so that emergency responders can listen for signs of life.
