· For those who care to know, the future is important for, right now, Osun State – to be fair, like a lot of states – is socioeconomically wounded, and the task of finding its bearing is daunting. Like every other subnational, our dear state faces a demographic nightmare: there are simply too many young people to take care of, educate and prepare for a future of hope. The state therefore does not need violence.

·

· Osun needs a visionary – a thinker-leader, gentle as a dove but wise as a serpent, not an autocrat drunk on power or privilege – with a plan to tackle the very troubling tasks ahead. For him, authority will be about service in love, and leadership as the sincere desire and commitment to seek the good of those entrusted to his care. For example, the state has to redefine the structure and texture of its education system so that pupils entering primary school in the next school year are prepared, some seventeen or so years down the road, to be competitive in a fast-changing international economy. This should begin with computer literacy, as is already the case in California and the Scandinavian countries, and perhaps China.

·

· Again, a very critical issue here is to re-examine the cautionary note sounded by The Economist magazine that Africa is weighed down by an over-abundance of uncapitalized, stagnant micro-enterprises. Rather than an indictment, this rigorous analytical thinking must become the catalyst for Osun’s new economic policy, reshaping the wider Nigerian narrative as well.

·

· I have argued repeatedly that no subnational can create hundreds of thousands of jobs without upscaling hundreds, eventually, thousands of its small businesses. For Osun, I hold firmly to this position. Coincidentally, this is the sort of framework developed in California starting from the 1950s under Governor Edmund G. “Pat” Brown, and it worked. Today, if it were an independent country, California, with its $4 trillion GDP, would be the world’s fourth-largest economy. This model should be studied in-depth, with the possibility of adaptation to Osun State.

·

· The sentiment for slimming down and recalibrating the shape and size of the machinery of the government is perfectly understood. Nevertheless, there are exceptions to prove the rule. Therefore, it is advisable that the new government has a Commissioner for Small Businesses who will serve as a coordinator of the upscale businesses in the state. Properly handled, it should be the most important portfolio, apart from that of the governor and the Commissioner for Finance, in the next four to ten years.

·

· Such a proposition will lead into gently formalizing large segments of the informal sector which will lead to modernized and better capitalized sustainable economic activity. It must be the number one priority, and they should also work with the South West Development Commission (SWDC).

·

· The state should set up a N1 billion annual investment fund, seeking equity investments from private companies in Nigeria, sovereign wealth funds abroad, agencies such as the World Bank’s private sector arm, the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the African Finance Corporation (AFC), the Development Finance Corporation of the Netherlands (FMO), and similar bodies like that. The new government must go for broke in this area. The ripple effects will cut across all sectors, making the modernisation of agriculture feasible. This will transform subsistence agriculture into commercial agriculture, thereby achieving the objective of turning Osun into an export-oriented economy with all of its attendant benefits. The same goes for health, information technology, tourism, the hospitality sector and every other area.

·

· The health sector must also be revamped to produce healthy minds in healthy bodies. This means that the fiscal framework must be adjusted to retain and attract medical professionals in the state. This is not going to be easy at all, for no state in Nigeria appears to have developed an appetite for paying attention to the massive increases in remuneration and conditions of service carried out recently by the British government the now-departed British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer. The award is certainly going to entice medical professionals from developing countries, including Nigeria. The incoming state government must therefore develop a counteractive strategy to retain medical professionals in the state, otherwise, a looming catastrophe in the health service sector is in the waiting.

·

· That’s not all! Any serious economic blueprint must incorporate telemedicine to bridge the rural-urban divide. This in effect is the future even in the developed world. Mechanisms should be established to link Osun medical doctors abroad to work with their local counterparts via digital health platforms. To revamp education, health, agriculture and other areas concurrently, the incoming government must anchor its economic policy firmly on production.

·

· It is not only disappointing but also disconcerting that, in the course of the present electioneering campaigns in Osun, we have not heard even a perfunctory attempt to examine why the Action Group, led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo, placed free education at the heart of its socioeconomic development paradigm. With federation allocations and internally generated revenue swelling, uncomfortable questions must be asked: Why is every contending camp fleeing from our ideological history and why should a serious administration abandon the sick to predatory healthcare costs? For God’s sake, who feeds the schoolchild if the government washes its hands? To put it bluntly, who did this to us that we have so completely amputated our politics from Awolowo’s progressive hue and reduced governance to a sterile scramble for power?

·

· ​The fear of insecurity also introduces a subtle tension on the road to August 15. Nigerians can only ask the security agencies to step up their game, particularly by deploying intelligence frameworks to preempt clear plans to disrupt the democratic process. There is little to gain from superficial peace pacts and appealing to rapacious disruptors hell-bent on decapitating the process. The security services have had months of notice, backed by a history of volatile events in the state, ensuring they are fully prepared. The key flashpoints – as everyone already knows – lie in logistics, particularly the back-and-forth movement of electoral materials. We trust that preventive mechanisms are fully in place, given the sufficient warnings issued.

·

· The electorate must be reassured of their safety and protection because legitimacy derives its oxygen from high turnout at the polls. This is why organized democracies make apathy unattractive and guard fiercely against voter suppression. Unfortunately, such institutional safeguards remain a heavy luxury in Nigeria, a country constrained by resources in critical areas. It is costly enough already that ballot papers have to be reprinted because of a court judgment reinstating a previously omitted political party. This is going to be financially demanding, but it has to be done. Obedience to court judgments is the lifeblood of a democracy.

·

· It is for this reason that so much hinges on this election. It is an opportunity to interrogate a daunting future strategically and with the utmost seriousness, as that future is almost here. Civil society and traditional rulers too have a vital role to play, because democracy thrives on the preservation of traditional cultural norms, sensible behaviour, and electoral vigilance. Intensive public enlightenment should be carried out using every imaginable medium. While low turnout may not legally invalidate an election under constitutional law, it severely traumatizes the electorate and delegitimizes the resulting government.

· ijebujesa@yahoo.co.uk.

World.title: Eastern Cape couple treat 6-year-old daughter to magical snowfall [video]
World.content:
On 10 August, Eddie and Tamara Murray, a couple living in the Eastern Cape, happily braved the cold weather to treat their 6-year-old daughter to a memorable snowfall experience.

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) had previously issued a level 6 warning that snowfall disruptions were expected in multiple municipalities within the Eastern Cape, affecting several routes and mountain passes.

Fast forward to Tuesday, 11 August, most of those passes have since reopened as conditions have eased.



THE MURRAY FAMILY EMBRACES SNOWFALL EXPERIENCE IN THE EASTERN CAPE

Sidima Mfeku from SABC News reported live from Penhoek Pass, where families parked their cars by the roadside to enjoy the snowfall.

Among them was the Murray family, who took the opportunity to have some fun in the snow while celebrating their daughter’s sixth birthday.

Eddie, the father of the young girl, shared his thoughts on experiencing snow.

“Every year we are lucky to have snow. We bring the kids all the time to come and play. That’s something that you experience maybe once in your lifetime, but we’re lucky to stay around here,” he said.

His wife, Tamara Murray, also expressed her thoughts about the snow.

“We also come from the Eastern Cape (Craddock), and we’ve never seen snow before. So being around the area that snows is genuinely something that is amazing,” she said.



Tamara said the following about her daughter experiencing the snow: “So this will be so memorable for her taking it when she goes and gets bigger.”

SAFETY REMAINED A PRIORITY FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT

According to the SABC, safety was a priority for the provincial Department of Transport, with law enforcement implementing measures to protect the public.

The cold weather conditions in the province also forced motorists to change routes when approaching the Kimber Bridge.

World.title: Orlando Pirates predicted XI vs AmaZulu
World.content:
Orlando Pirates will be looking for a stronger showing when they travel to face AmaZulu in the Betway Premiership this week.

The fixture marks the Buccaneers’ first trip outside Soweto this campaign and the first of back-to-back away games this week.

They will face an AmaZulu side playing the second of three consecutive home matches, with league football now their immediate priority following an early cup exit.



The match also marks the return of Betway Premiership action to King’s Park, with the two sides meeting at the historic venue for the first time in more than five years.

Orlando Pirates look to dominate AmaZulu

Pirates have also strengthened their attacking options with the recent arrival of Norwegian striker Sebastian Pedersen, who could make his debut against Usuthu.

With Evidence Makgopa sidelined for several months, Pirates are currently left with Yanela Mbuthuma and Boitumelo Radiopane as their recognised strikers. Pedersen could therefore be handed an opportunity to lead the line and showcase what he can offer.



A victory would move the Buccaneers to the top of the table, provided they better their rivals’ goal difference.

In recent years, Orlando Pirates have had the better of AmaZulu and unbeaten in 11 against against Arthur Zwane’s side. An attacking team might be too much for Usuthu to handle but with captain Nkosinathi Sibisi missing, the home team might fancy their chances.

Midfielders: Thalente Mbatha, Patrick Maswanganyi, Kabelo Kgositsile, Oswin Appollis

World.title: Mamelodi Sundowns shock TS Galaxy in 5-goal thriller
World.content:
Brayan Leon opened the scoring for Sundowns from the penalty spot. Victor Letsoalo repsonded with a brace to put Galaxy 2-1 ahead.

Substitute Sphelele Mkhulise then turned the game around. He scored in the 88th minute before completing his brace in stoppage time to seal a dramatic Sundowns victory.

Below is how it all happended…



The referee blows the final whistle. It ends TS Galaxy 2-3 Sundowns at the Mbombela Stadium.

90+3′ ⚽️ Goal! Mkhulise gets his second. A cool tap in from the six yard box after briliant play from Matthews and Mudau. TS Galaxy 2-3 Sundowns!

88′ ⚽️ Goal! Mkhulise knocks the equaliser after a scramble in the box. TS Galaxy 2-2 Sundowns!

77′ ⚽️ Goal! Letsoalo gets the second goal for the home side. A brilliant header from a Mvelase freekick. TS Galaxy 2-1 Sundowns!

69′ ⚽️ Tape makes a strong save on the near post to deny a stinging Leon shot.

66′ ⚽️ Mailula is caught offside. The score remains TS Galaxy 1-1 Sundowns!



58′ ⚽️ What a brilliant block by Khoza. Mvelase thought he had scored for TS Galaxy! His shot blocked four yards from goal!

56′ ⚽️ Tape makes a wonderful save to deny Van Wyk.

46′ ⚽️ We’re back live at the Mbombela Stadium. The score is still TS Galaxy 1-1 Sundowns!

SECOND HALF: TS GALAXY 1-1 MAMELODI SUNDOWNS

45′ ⚽️ Referee blows the whistle for half time. TS Galaxy 1-1 Sundowns!

36′ ⚽️ Goal! Letsoalo equalises with a briliant finish inside the box on the near post. TS Galaxy 1-1 Sundowns!

26′ ⚽️Yellow card! Madua is booked for a hand on Mahlambi’s face.

17′⚽️ Sundowns win a dangerous freekick outside the box

11′ ⚽️ Sundowns remaining in full control.

7′ ⚽️ Goal! Brayan Leon scores from the penalty spot after Matthews was fouled by Zindoga in the box. TS Galaxy 0-1 Sundowns!

1′ ⚽️ Kick off. We’re underway at the Mbombela Stadium!

TS Galaxy will host Sundowns at Mbombela Stadium, kick off is at 19:30.

TS Galaxy starting line up: Tape, Motaung, Zulu, Mncwango, Kokora, Nkosi, Mvelase, Mahlambi, Zindoga, Letsoalo, George.

Substitutes: Madela, Mahlangu, Silva, Fisher, Maake, Mbunjane, Rantoa, Ngwenya, Zulu.

Mamelodi Sundowns starting line up: Williams, Mudau, Johannes, Khoza, Basadien, Gomolemo Kekana, Allende, Santos, Matthews, van Wyk, Leon.

Substitutes: Goss, Mvala, Modiba, Mdunyelwa, Mkhulise, Zwane, Mokoena, Mailula, Rayners.

The Rockets started their campaign with a 2-2 draw against Siwelele, while Kabo Yellow are coming off a 3-2 victory over Polokwane City in the MTN8 last weekend.

TS GALAXY UNDER BERNARD PARKER

TS Galaxy have undergone major changes ahead of the 2026/27 campaign. The Rockets brought in Bernard Parker as their new coach as they look to build a competitive side for the new season.

They also added 14 new players to their squad during a major overhaul. However, TS Galaxy have reason to feel confident ahead of the meeting with Sundowns.

The Rockets are unbeaten in their last four home matches against the Brazilians. That run includes a memorable 3-2 victory in May 2026 and a Nedbank Cup triumph earlier this year.

Playing at Mbombela Stadium could therefore give TS Galaxy another boost against the reigning champions.

MAMELODI SUNDOWNS BEGIN TITLE DEFENCE

Sundowns enter the match after an entertaining 3-2 win over Polokwane City in the MTN8.

They are preparing to reclaim the Betway Premiership title after Orlando Pirates clinched it last season. Coach Miguel Cardoso will want his team to build momentum quickly despite facing a difficult away trip.

Sundowns no longer have Lucas Ribeiro or Peter Shalulile, who both departed the club. That leaves Cardoso with a reshaped attacking unit as Sundowns target another league title.

If you are buying tickets from a lottery outlet, they close at 20:40 on draw days.



HOW TO PLAY THE DAILY LOTTO

The Daily Lotto costs R3 per board. Players match five numbers from a pool of 36, either self-selected or via Quick Pick.

The Daily Lotto will pay out its estimated jackpot every evening – even if no one correctly matches all five numbers drawn.

WHERE TO BUY YOUR TICKETS

World.title: All Blacks blank toothless Sharks
World.content:
Ruben Love produced a near-perfect goal-kicking display as the All Blacks clinched an emphatic 54-0 against the Sharks at Kings Park in Durban on Tuesday night.

While nowhere as clinical as they would’ve liked, the All Blacks produced a more well-rounded display against the men from Durban four nights after their error-strewn tour opener against the Stormers in Cape Town.

Irrespective of the type of performances to date, the All Blacks are unbeaten in their two opening games of the Castle Double Malt Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry and could very well head into the first Test against the Springboks on 22 August on a three-game winning streak if they get the job done over the Bulls at Loftus this coming weekend.



Because the Sharks didn’t provide much of a challenge, there wasn’t much to gauge the All Blacks on. However, from an individual perspective, there were statement performances from Love, Fehi Fineanganofo and Jordie Barrett. And while Barrett is a sure bet for a start in the Test series, Love and Fineanganofo enhanced their chances of selection for the clashes against the Springboks.

FIRST HALF RECAP

One of the big storylines in the lead-up to this encounter was the Sharks’ selection of Ma’a Nonu, one of the game’s most revered sons, against the All Blacks, the team he represented 103 times in the Test arena across 12 trophy-laden years.

And even before kick-off, this most unpredictable Nonu-All Blacks reunion produced as the now 44-year-old answered New Zealand’s haka with a lone haka of his own.

However, that sideshow would prove to be about the only challenge/resistance be the Sharks for the remainder of the night. From kick-off, it was the all the Kiwis. It took them a while before they scored, but touchdowns by Fehi Fineanganofo and Damian McKenzie put them 14 points up at the break.

SECOND HALF RECAP

It was one-way traffic in the second half as the floodgates opened. The visitors ran in six more tries – by Caleb Clarke, Fineanganofo, Barrett, Kyle Preston, Timoci Tavatavanawai, Sam Darry – to round off a resounding victory.

Coupled with his two first half conversions, Love knocked five more two-pointers from all sides of the park to finish the game as the top-point scorer with seven from eight kicks at goal.



There weren’t many, if any, highlights to speak of for the Sharks, but they would have been happy when they clinched a scrum penalty against the powerful All Blacks pack in the 67th minute. In the end, though, the scoreline is a true reflection of the one-sided nature of the game.

ALL BLACKS SCORERS

Tries: Fehi Fineanganofo (2), Damian McKenzie, Caleb Clarke, Jordie Barrett, Kyle Preston, Timoci Tavatavanawai, Sam Darry. Conversions: Ruben Love (7).

World.title: The number of unemployed people has nearly doubled in 18 years
World.content:
More than one-third of South Africa’s working population is unemployed.

The recent 0.9% decline in employment could be blamed on global events that have made doing business challenging.

This may have fueled the problem. But it isn’t the cause.



South Africa is in an unemployment crisis, regardless of how you choose to slice it.

The most worrying figure is that unemployment has nearly doubled since 2008.

The number of unemployed people increased by 94% in 18 years

If you’re counting the numbers quarterly, these subtle declines seem par for the course.

Zoom out and take a look at the bigger picture: South Africa is deep in an unemployment crisis.

According to data from Statistics South Africa (Stats SA), 4 371 000 people were unemployed in 2008. As of the second quarter of 2026, 8 481 000 people are unemployed.

This is a 94% increase. It’s also only 261 000 people away from being double the 2008 figure.



Employment has increased by 15.9% in 18 years.

In the first quarter of 2008, amid a global recession, 14 438 000 people were employed.

At the end of the second quarter of 2026, only 16 739 000 people were employed.

Contrast that with the working-age population growth.

In 18 years, South Africa’s working population has increased by 31%.

Young People have Given Up

Buried in the data are the Not in Employment, Education or Training (NEET) figures.

It shows that young people, aged 15 to 24, have given up on education and employment.

When data began in the third quarter of 2012, 31.4% of those in this age group weren’t studying or working.

As of the first quarter of 2026, 37.6% of those in this age group weren’t employed or studying — the highest in recorded history.

Can South Africa’s Economy Absorb the Unemployed?

According to Stats SA, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew 0.5% in the first quarter of 2026.

The sixth consecutive quarter of growth.

Last year it grew 1.1%.

In 2021, it grew 4.9% after a 6.4% contraction in 2020.

The economy is, for all intents and purposes, stagnant.

If you use the measurement that for every 1% of GDP growth, roughly 100 000 jobs are created, South Africa’s economy would need to grow by 5% every year for the next 9 years to absorb the current unemployed population.

To absorb future job seekers coming onto the market, this growth would need to be higher. Significantly higher.

World.title: Springboks vs All Blacks | Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry: All the RESULTS
World.content:
The All Blacks are set to revive one of rugby's greatest traditions when they embark on an unprecedented eight-match tour of South Africa and the United States. Image: SA Rugby website

The All Blacks are set to revive one of rugby’s greatest traditions when they embark on an unprecedented eight-match tour of South Africa and the United States, rekindling a format that has been absent from the international game for three decades.

Dubbed “Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry”, the 2026 tour will see New Zealand take on South Africa’s four United Rugby Championship franchises before contesting a four-Test Freedom Cup series against the Springboks.

The tour marks the first return to the traditional touring format between the two nations since the launch of the Tri-Nations in 1996.



Rugby’s classic tours return

Following an agreement between the South African Rugby Union (SARU) and New Zealand Rugby (NZR), the two rugby powerhouses have brought back the extended bilateral tours that helped shape the sport’s rich history.

Instead of meeting only during the Rugby Championship, the All Blacks will spend more than a month on South African soil, recreating the touring experience that produced some of rugby’s most memorable contests.

As part of the new international calendar, the Rugby Championship will become a biennial competition from 2027.



Provincial giants await

Before taking on the world champion Springboks, New Zealand will test themselves against each of South Africa’s four United Rugby Championship franchises.

The tour opened on Friday, 7 August against the Stormers in Cape Town before clashes with the Sharks in Durban, the Bulls in Pretoria and the Lions in Johannesburg.

The fixtures offer South Africa’s top franchises a rare opportunity to face the All Blacks, while giving the visitors valuable match practice ahead of the Test series.



Freedom Cup expanded to four Tests

The highlight of the tour will be a historic four-match Freedom Cup series between rugby’s two most successful nations.

The first three Tests will be played in South Africa before the series concludes in Baltimore, where the Springboks and All Blacks will meet in the United States for the first time.

The expanded series is expected to provide one of the toughest examinations either side has faced in the professional era.



Women’s rugby joins the occasion

The tour will also celebrate the growth of the women’s game, with the Springbok Women taking on the reigning world champion Black Ferns in a curtain-raiser before the third Test at FNB Stadium on 5 September.

A rivalry renewed

Few rivalries in world sport carry the history and prestige of clashes between the Springboks and the All Blacks.

With more than a century of fierce competition behind them, the revival of traditional tours promises to reconnect rugby with one of its most iconic customs, giving supporters weeks of elite rugby while providing both nations with an ideal platform to build towards the next Rugby World Cup.

World.title: 'Starved of opportunity' - Economist as SA's unemployment deepens
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Economists have dubbed South Africa’s employment rate a crisis.

According to Xhanti Payi, the reality of this crisis can be seen in socio-economic outcomes, from crime to violence on the rise.

“People are really feeling quite starved of opportunity, and they're outside that moment,” he said.

Payi’s remarks come after the recent announcement of the unemployment rate, which has jumped to a four-year high.

It rose to 33.6% in the second quarter of the year, from 32.7% in the first.

READ | SA unemployment rate climbs to 33.6%

South Africa's unemployment rate has been above 30% for five years, and it's among the highest in the world.

Payi said when one tracks the number of people who are coming into the job market and are ready to work, and the number of people who are actually working, those numbers are diverging.

He said this is a major problem because that divergence means not only is the job market failing to accommodate the number of people who are coming in or are available for work, but it is also actively losing jobs.

“That's actually something that's of serious worry. It's even more sad for young people who can't even look forward to a job,” Payi said.

Statistics show that 19,000 jobs were lost on balance, while more than 300,000 people entered the workforce, either from school or because they had re-entered the job market.

This pushed up the unemployment rate by nearly a percentage point.

The jobs crisis looks even worse according to the expanded definition of unemployment, which includes people who have simply given up looking for work.

It soars above 43.5%.

READ | Foreign nationals hold just 3.4% of SA formal jobs, Wits study finds

The data points to an economy that is still struggling to generate enough jobs, especially in the formal sector.

Women are also bearing the brunt, Payi noted.

“Over the last 10 years, I think the statistics office has really highlighted this in quite a stark way. We have actually moved now to 50% more women, and now almost 60% more women are actually unemployed. If we just look back 10 years ago, which is something of a crisis, given that we keep celebrating all of these opportunities.

World.title: 'Paying for room with no window' - Student grievance spark protest
World.content:
FORT HARE - The University of Fort Hare has suspended in-person classes at its Alice campus in the Eastern Cape.

This comes after protests broke out on Tuesday morning as students expressed their unhappiness over unresolved residence issues dating back to 2025.

They have also raised concerns about the premises’ infrastructure and what they describe as inadequate security measures.

Last year, unknown perpetrators torched multiple buildings as demonstrations erupted over governance issues and the SRC elections.

READ | UFH protests | Committee believes violent protests were avoidable

Similar scenes were witnessed this time around, with reports of arson and road closures.

SRC representative Sinovuyo Ngqwangi says the situation could have been avoided if management had been willing to listen to their grievances.

She claims they are often met with “arrogance” from management, which results in their concerns not being heard.

“Blocking the road and trying to burn things was to first get their attention. So once we got their attention, the stakeholders were able to come to us after that. “If it were not for that, I doubt if they would have come down to us and signed the memorandum of demands,” she said.

She says while the university has indicated that their grievances will be addressed by Friday, students have vowed to remain on the ground until then.

“We received a lot of calls from parents who are indeed worried. But I wish they could see the conditions we live under while they pay huge amounts for residence. “They are paying over R58 000 for a room that does not have a light, heater or even a window... When parents, see students protest just know they are fighting for our rights.

In a statement issued earlier in the day, the University confirmed that teaching and learning would continue online until further notice.

It also thanked the staff and students for their cooperation amid what it called a 'temporary arrangement'.

World.title: Ma’a Nonu performs Haka against All Blacks
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - All Blacks legend Ma’a Nonu found himself on the opposite side of the Haka as his new club, the Sharks, took on New Zealand in Durban.



The second Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry warm-up fixture is underway at a wet Kings Park Stadium.



A rare and emotional moment dominated the build-up, with Nonu joining the Sharks after recently signing with the Durban side before performing the Haka against his former team.



The 44-year-old is a two-time Rugby World Cup winner, helping New Zealand lift the Webb Ellis Cup in 2011 and 2015.



Nonu was named on the replacement bench for the Sharks, as he prepared to face the All Blacks for the first time in the colours of his new club.

World.title: Snow sparks Eastern Cape tourism boom
World.content:
GQEBERHA - While heavy snow has disrupted several R58 mountain passes and forced motorists to drive with extreme caution, many are finding joy in the moment.

The heavy snow has also sparked a major tourism boom by drawing crowds eager to witness the rare winter landscape.

Disaster management teams are on high alert as freezing temperatures, disruptive snow and heavy rain sweep across parts of the country.

READ | Disaster teams on high alert as snow, heavy rain sweep across SA

Warnings for disruptive snow are in place over some parts of the Eastern Cape and the Free State.

In KwaZulu-Natal, travellers using the N3 highway have been warned to drive carefully as snow hits the province.

eNCA reporter Ronald Masinda was in Barkly Pass this morning and filed this report.

World.title: NUM rejects Eskom restructuring plan
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) has rejected Eskom's restructuring plans, warning they could lead to privatisation and higher electricity costs.

According to NUM President Phillip Vilakazi, at the centre of their concerns is that workers and the public were not adequately consulted.

"What we are saying is the National Union of Mine Workers, our best interest is to have a consultative process that gives us the details of the intention of such a program...

"If you look at the principle of our own country, we are made to believe that a democratic government is a government of the people, by the people, for the people. Therefore, consultation is primary," he said.

Vilakazi said they will not allow what he calls the "privatisation of a state-owned entity that does not benefit people.

READ | Gold Fields' South Deep Mine workers score five-year wage deal

As such, he insists that the focus should be on affordable power and protecting jobs.

World.title: ‘We Don’t Want Bloodshed’ | Davido appeals to Trump over Nigerian state election
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Nigerian singer David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, has called on US President Donald Trump to pay attention to concerns ahead of the 15 August Osun State governorship election.

The call comes amid reports of violence and tensions ahead of the poll.

In a social media post on Tuesday, the singer raised concerns about possible violence, intimidation and disruption of the democratic process.

READ | Tyla drops Lagos show as South Africa, Nigeria row over immigration

He called on the US and the international community to urge “relevant authorities to ensure that every voter is protected and every vote is respected”.

World.title: Parliament disputes Fadiel Adams' faulty laptop claims at Madlanga Commission
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Parliament has disputed Fadiel Adams' claim that laptop problems delayed his responses to the Madlanga Commission.

The National Coloured Congress leader, who took the stand at the commission on Tuesday, said his faulty device had caused him to miss critical emails.

He said he had instead relied on phone calls and colleagues for updates about his work.

READ | 'Take the commission seriously' | Madlanga reprimands Fadiel Adams

But Parliament says its Information and Communications Technology (ICT) records show no evidence of persistent malfunction or repeated repairs.

It says the logged issues were mainly password, login and Wi-Fi problems.

Parliament also says Adams had access to other devices to maintain his work.

World.title: Gachagua bombshell
World.content:
Democracy for Citizen Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua when he read out President Ruto’s four-year score card during a media briefing at the party’s offices in Nairobi on August 11, 2026. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has accused President William Ruto of going against the very promises he made to Kenyans as he sought office.

Instead, Gachagua claimed the President had presided over human rights violations, corruption, wastage of public resources and the weaponisation of State agencies, the very vices he vowed to fight against.

World.title: You have failed Kenyans, Gachagua tells Ruto
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for Citizen Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua when he read out President Ruto’s four-year score card during a media briefing at the party’s offices in Nairobi on August 11, 2026. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused President William Ruto of failing Kenyans and abandoning his campaign promises.

Gachagua who was speaking at the DCP headquarters accused the president of eroding democratic gains of multipartyism and swallowing opposition parties.

“Four years later, Mr. William Ruto has betrayed the trust bestowed on him by the people of Kenya, betrayed the fruits and foundation of our Nation that have been built by previous administrations under the various development blue prints such as Vision 2030,” he said.

Gachagua was addressing the press on the score card of the Kenya Kwanza administration for the four years it has been in leadership.

According to the opposition figure, President Ruto had promised to uphold the rule of law, build a secure, just and democratic Kenyan founded on the constitution but he had abandoned all of the promises.

He added that there were promises of professionalising the National Police Service, safeguarding human rights, protecting Kenyans and strengthening the administration of justice while ensuring security agencies are accountable to the constitution.

Gachagua alleged that the Kenya Kwanza administration had allowed goonism and drug abuse to thrive adding that the country had also become a bedrock of extrajudicial killings and an abductors playground.

He said that during campaigns they had promised to amend and operationalise the National Coroners Service Act of 2017 to establish the Coroner General’s office to remove the burden of probing deaths from the regular police channels and Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI).

Gachagua said that proposed amendments were aimed at removing potential conflict of interest and ensuring transparency in handling unexplained deaths, enforced disappearances or fatalities caused by the police.

“Four years later, this promise has not been fulfilled.”

He accused the government of overseeing the arrest and rendition of government critics from Turkey, Uganda, Tanzania and South Sudan adding that officials attached to a construction company from China were deported when they protested the awarding of a contract to rivals.

“Kenyans are not safe, our children are not safe, investors are not safe and foreigners are not safe. Foreigners are not safe, Investors are not safe, no one in Kenya is safe.”

He accused the President of limiting the freedom of the press through sponsored disinformation campaigns and also citing the attempted abduction of Standard Group’s Associated Editor Alex Kiprotich in Nakuru on June 26, 2026.

According to Gachagua the government had failed to fight corruption despite promising to do so adding that it had entrenched graft as a way of life in Kenya.

World.title: Wamboka: Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang'i should back Sifuna
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kabuchai Mp Majimbo kalasinga and his counterpart Jack Wamboka during a press briefing on Monday. [Juliet Omelo, Standard]

The political battle for the 2027 presidency has intensified, with leaders allied to the Linda Mwananchi movement urging opposition figures Kalonzo Musyoka, Rigathi Gachagua and Fred Matiang’i to abandon their presidential ambitions and back Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna.

Bumula MP Jack Wamboka made the call after a three-day political tour of Western Kenya by the Linda mwananchi brigade, saying the region had demonstrated growing grassroots support for Sifuna.

Wamboka said the tour was a major success, with close to 22 rallies held in three days. He added that the crowds reflected growing enthusiasm for Sifuna, particularly among young people, women, political aspirants and ordinary voters.

“We respect you, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i. We know you have what it takes but in 2027, we ask you to stand with Sifuna,” Wamboka said.

He said the reception in Western Kenya showed that Sifuna’s campaign was gaining national attention.

The first time MP said Sifuna had focused on issues affecting Western Kenya, particularly the collapse of industries and the struggling sugar sector. He pointed to Mumias and Nzoia sugar factories, saying their decline had left farmers and workers suffering.

Wamboka accused National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula of failing to deliver development promises made to Bungoma residents citing unfinished roads and the stalled Bungoma stadium, saying several projects lacked adequate funding despite repeated commitments to voters during the campaigns.

He also questioned Wetang’ula’s political record, citing past controversies and accusing the Speaker of failing to live up to his promises adding that voters should judge leaders by what they deliver, not by speeches alone.

Kabuchai MP Majimbo Kalasinga said the tour had proved that Sifuna’s bid was gaining grassroots support.

“Edwin Sifuna is going for president, nothing else,” he said.

He said supporters contributed small amounts to the campaign, arguing that the movement was being funded by ordinary Kenyans rather than wealthy political backers. He said crowds turned up voluntarily.

Kalasinga also announced that Linda Mwananchi would hold a rally in Homa Bay on August 16 despite local warnings. He said Sifuna had a right to campaign anywhere in Kenya.

He called for peaceful competition and warned against attempts to block the rally or restrict political activity in the region emphasising that Kenya is for everyone, constitutionally, peacefully and equally.

They two vowed to fight for the Linda Mwananchi name.

The Wamboka-Kalasinga push adds momentum to Sifuna’s campaign and pressures opposition leaders to unite before the 2027 election.

World.title: Kindiki defends government's development agenda in Mt Kenya
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki and Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on August 10, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has reiterated the government’s commitment to ensure equitable development.

Prof Kindiki said that President William Ruto’s government has initiated many development projects in Mt Kenya to transform livelihoods.

“Am advising the people against being deceived to leave the government to join the opposition where nothing is being provided,” he said.

The Deputy President said the road projects which had stalled have since been revived after the government released Sh176 billion owed to contractors to ensure completion of 6,000km.

He spoke at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on Sunday, where he was the chief guest during celebrations to mark 100 years since the establishment of Gaichanjiru Mission Hospital managed by the Catholic Diocese of Murang'a.

Kindiki, who was accompanied by Cabinet Secretaries Alice Wahome (Lands) and Rebecca Miano (Tourism), said that the government has impacted the region with affordable houses estimated at 180,000 units, modern markets and student hostels that have created employment for hundreds of skilled and unskilled persons.

He said the church has a history of partnering with the government in matters concerning development and empowerment of the less fortunate in the community.

“In Murang’a the government has ensured all the projects that KeRRA under Eng Antony Mwaura was working on are completed to give the locals value for money,” said the DP.

During the event, the President gave Sh10 million for procurement of equipment for the health facility, where more than Sh20 million was raised.

Ruto also gave Sh 50 million and directed the Housing Department to facilitate construction of the hospital's ICU, HDU, theatre and laboratory

Kindiki lauded efforts by Wahome that have seen Murang’a County benefit from Sh27 billion programmes from her ministry.

“Murang’a through her efforts has 27 modern markets, Affordable Housing Programme units, and student hostels, programmes that have engaged hundreds of persons,” he said.

World.title: Charlene Ruto's Koito lights up Kilgoris
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Ruto, is engaged to Tanzanian entrepreneur Isaiah Yunge.

The drums rolled, traditional songs filled the air and dancers swayed in colourful rhythm as Kilgoris was transformed into a spectacular theatre of love, culture, wealth and political power.

At the expansive Intonna Heritage Farm in Naserian Village, President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Chelagat Ruto, took a major traditional step towards marriage as the First Family hosted her Koito ak Chaik—a colourful Kalenjin engagement and farewell ceremony.

For hours, the skies above Kilgoris were punctuated by helicopters ferrying distinguished guests to the President’s family property, while luxury vehicles streamed through the gates carrying politicians, government officials, business personalities, relatives and friends.

On the ground, the mood was unmistakably festive. Traditional songs echoed across the expansive farm as dancers moved to the rhythm, colourful attire transformed the venue into a sea of elegance and culture, and guests embraced the joy of a ceremony that combined an ancient African tradition with the unmistakable grandeur of Kenya’s First Family.

It was romance wrapped in tradition—and tradition presented on a spectacular scale.

The guest list read almost like a roll call of Kenya’s political establishment. Leaving the Narok delegation was Governor Patrick Ole Ntutu, who joined Kilgoris MP Julius Sunkuli and former Narok Governor Samuel Tunai in celebrating the First Family on the special occasion.

The ceremony also brought together elected leaders from across Narok County, creating an impressive gathering of the county’s political establishment at the heart of Trans Mara.

From governors and Senators to MPs, the event brought together leaders from across the country. Top government officials and senior executives too came dressed for the ceremony

The fashion became part of the spectacle. Brown, maroon and other earthy tones dominated the scene, blending effortlessly with the traditional African setting. It was a celebration in which political leaders seemed determined to make an entrance as memorable as the occasion itself.

But beyond the political faces and the luxury was the heartbeat of the ceremony—culture. Traditional songs rang across the farm. Dancers moved with energy and precision, their performances adding colour and rhythm to a celebration centred on family and love.

The atmosphere shifted between moments of emotion and bursts of exuberance as relatives, friends and guests celebrated Charlene’s transition into a new stage of life.

The contrast was striking. Modern wealth arrived by helicopter, while ancient traditions were celebrated through song and dance. Luxury vehicles lined up outside as cultural performers entertained guests inside. Political heavyweights mingled with family elders.

Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

And amid the glamour, the central message remained simple: Charlene and her fiancé, Isaiah Yunge, had brought together not just two families but two countries.

Yunge is a Tanzanian technology entrepreneur and digital innovation enthusiast associated with Goodsam Technologies and is a co-founder of Smart Kaya LLC, a smart-home technology venture.

He has been recognised among Forbes Africa’s 30 Under 30 and received the Queen’s Young Leaders Award in 2018. His interest in technology reportedly began at an early age. At 17, he was selected as a UNICEF Africa Youth Ambassador and participated in international advocacy around children's rights.

He later pursued training in sustainable business models through the Swedish Institute, studied Leading Change at Cambridge University and became an alumnus of the Harvard Ministerial Leadership Program.

For all its glamour, the heart of the celebration remained the centuries-old tradition of Koito. Among the Kalenjin, it is a significant engagement ceremony through which the families of the bride and groom formally meet, bless the relationship, exchange gifts and discuss dowry arrangements.

It is a moment when families begin the process of becoming one. The Chaik aspect gives the occasion an emotional dimension, symbolising the farewell of a daughter as she prepares to leave her parental home and begin a new chapter with her husband. Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

For Charlene, the symbolism was profound. Surrounded by her parents, family, friends and some of the country’s most powerful political figures, she was celebrated not simply as the President’s daughter, but as a daughter taking a traditional step towards marriage.

The songs, dances and blessings gave the occasion an emotional warmth that stood in contrast to the scale of the event.

Yet there was no escaping the extraordinary display of wealth surrounding the celebration. Helicopters arriving overhead. Luxury vehicles streaming through the gates. High-ranking government officials and elected leaders arriving in motorcades. Elegant outfits and carefully coordinated colours.

It was a spectacle that demonstrated the resources, networks and influence available to one of Kenya’s most powerful families. The ceremony was therefore more than a social event.

For Charlene, however, beyond the helicopters, politicians, fashion and cameras was the quiet meaning of the day.

A daughter was being prepared to leave one home and begin another. Two families were being brought together.

Love was at the centre. Culture provided the rhythm. Wealth supplied the grandeur. And political power provided the spectacle.

For one unforgettable Saturday, Charlene Ruto’s Koito turned Kilgoris into a glittering stage where romance, tradition, influence and prosperity met under the Narok sky.

World.title: Police join protest victims' Sh25.75m reparations payout
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prof. Makau Mutua, Chairperson of the Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations. [File,Standard]

A protest reparations panel has approved compensation for 49 police officers, awarding them Sh25.75 million alongside payments to civilians who suffered human rights violations.

The Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations approved seven claims involving severe injuries, 37 for moderate injuries and five for minor injuries, according to an update issued Friday, August 7.

"In acknowledgement of the dedication by our uniformed officers to protecting the public, the Panel has resolved to grant appropriate compensation for the human rights violations they sustained during the period in question," the panel said.

The inclusion of police officers adds a new dimension to a compensation programme created against the backdrop of protests in which police conduct has faced scrutiny.

During protests between June 17 and July 7, 2025, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) recorded 65 deaths, 342 civilian injuries and 171 injuries to police officers.

IPOA said most of the deaths were linked mainly to police actions during crowd-control operations.

The compensation programme grew out of the National Dialogue Committee (NADCO) process, which sought to address political and governance tensions in Kenya.

The government later set aside Sh2 billion for victims of human rights violations linked to protests and other demonstrations between 2017 and 2025.

The panel reported that it has processed 680 claims and disbursed Sh896.1 million in compensation.

The panel listed three phases of payments as Sh448.7 million in the initial phase, Sh225.4 million in the second phase and Sh247.95 million in the third phase.

The latest phase covered 175 civilian victims and included 50 fatalities, 46 severe injuries, 49 moderate injuries, 21 minor injuries and nine economic-loss claims.

The panel reported total payments of Sh222 million for the phase.

However, 472 claims submitted through IPOA and KNCHR remain outstanding because applicants have not provided enough supporting documents.

The panel is working with IPOA regional offices to locate affected victims and their beneficiaries and obtain the documents required to process the claims.

The backlog includes 594 of the 600 economic-loss claims received by the panel. Only four have been processed and compensated.

The panel has also received nine claims under the sexual offences category. Eight have been processed and compensated while one remains pending.

Claims involving enforced disappearances remain under review because the panel says the cases require investigation and verification before they can be approved, referred for further investigation or declared ineligible.

The panel has also reclassified three claims from minor to severe after reviewing medical reports and additional submissions.

It approved above-scale compensation for five victims whose injuries it described as permanent and life-altering and said it would recommend that President Ruto include them in a government-funded lifetime medical scheme.

World.title: EACC arrests Kitui County Chief Officer over Sh17.48m procurement fraud
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors arrested by EACC. [Joh Muia, Standard]

The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) has arrested Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors over alleged conflict of interest and procurement irregularities involving Sh17.48 million contracts.

In a statement on Thursday, EACC CEO Abdi Mohamud said investigations found that Kivoto, who served in the Departments of Agriculture & Fisheries and Irrigation, allegedly traded with the county through five proxy companies: Shanel Construction Ltd, ECO Stone Ltd, AZ Links Ltd, DTK Construction Ltd, and 4-Walls Ltd.

The companies were paid a total of Sh14.1 million by the county between the 2018/2019 and 2024/2025 financial years.

EACC further established that three of the directors, Josephine Mwikali Wambua of Shanel Construction, Makoma Wambua of AZ Links and Emmanuel Wambua of ECO Stone are relatives of Kivoto. There were also financial transactions between Kivoto and directors of DTK Construction and 4-Walls.

Following investigations, the file was forwarded to the DPP, who approved charges against nine suspects, including conflict of interest, abuse of office, money laundering, and corrupt procurement.

Those arrested are Gladys Mami Kivoto, Josephine Mwikali Wambua Director, Shanel Construction, Roselyne Kyambi Kilonzi Director, Shanel Construction, Mary Mueni Mbiti Director, DTK Construction & 4-Walls, Jonathan Kivondo Kieti Director, DTK Construction and Onesmus Munyao Nzioka Director, ECO Stone.

EACC directed Makoma Wambua of ECO Stone, Emmanuel Wambua of AZ Links, and Stella Nthenya Kioko of AZ Links who are reportedly in hiding to present themselves at the EACC Lower Eastern Regional Office in Machakos or the nearest EACC office for processing.

The suspects are expected to be arraigned at the Kitui Law Courts.

World.title: High Court orders striking nurses back to work
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Uasin Gishu County nurses strike over delayed payments and unfulfilled Collective Bargaining Agreement [Wycliff Kipsang, Standard]

Nurses across the 47 counties have been ordered to report back to work immediately or face legal action from the counties.

Justice Monica Mbaru of the Employment and Labour Court in Mombasa issued orders temporarily stopping the nationwide nurse strike that commenced on July 29, 2026, and ordered the Kenya National Union of Nurses and Midwives (KNUNM) to direct its members back to work.

Justice Mbaru said on Wednesday that any nurse absent from work without proper and lawful cause shall face disciplinary action.

This is after Mombasa County Government and its Public Service Board successfully enjoined the 46 county governments to make the order national.

“In the interim, the KNUNM (respondent) is hereby restrained from undertaking any industrial action relating to the strike notices dated July 21 and July 29 and shall direct all its members to resume duty forthwith and unconditionally to allow the court to address the claim herein on a priority basis,” said Justice Mbaru.

The judge ordered all county labour officers in the 47 counties to record attendance of nurses who report to work and compile a report in court on September 22, 2026.

“Any member of the KNUNM who will be noted by the County Labour Officer as absent from duty without lawful cause shall allow the counties to issue necessary notice to show cause why disciplinary action should not be taken,” said Justice Mbaru.

In their petition certified urgent, Mombasa County claimed that the nurses strike has crippled services in public hospitals across all the 47 counties, thereby placing patients facing emergency and inpatient care at risk.

In Mombasa County, the nurses strike paralysed medical services at all medical facilities, including Coast General Hospital, Port Reitz Hospital, Likoni District Hospital and Shimo La Tewa GK Prison Hospital.

Mombasa County, through its Counsel Murtaza Tajbhai, said that the strike had turned from a labour disagreement to a matter of immense public interest.

Tajbhai said that the nurses’ union proceeded with the said strike despite the Mombasa Public Service Board inviting the KNUNM officials for talks to avert the said strike.

The union had raised concerns over the 2025-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), implementation of the 2017 Return to Work Formula and pension terms for Universal Health Coverage staff care guidelines for nurses and the reinstatement of 46 nurses dismissed in Kisii County.

However, in their petition, Mombasa County said that the said grievances could not be addressed by each county individually.

Mombasa County Service Board Chief Executive Officer Fadhil Maamum told the court in his affidavit that most of the demands required consultation with national institutions like the Salaries and Remuneration Commission, while others cannot be implemented immediately given their significant financial implications.

He said that nurses under Mombasa County have no salary arrears and had met some of the union’s demands through negotiations.

Maamum said that while the nurses’ grievances can be resolved, the patients do not have the luxury of time.

“Nurses are designated essential service providers under the Labour Relations Act and the industrial action was unlawful because the statutory dispute resolution mechanism had not been exhausted," said Maamum.

He said the court's intervention will allow for negotiations and safeguard the constitutional right to healthcare.

However, the Union said that the strike was after failed action by the counties to meet their agreed grievances despite continued negotiations.

The nurses said they will not be reporting to work unless guided by the union.

World.title: Trump tries new line of attack on Democrats, calling them ‘jihadists’
World.content:
President Donald Trump said Monday that “jihadists” are being elected “all over the place” — trying a new, incendiary line of attack against Democrats with the midterm election just three months away.

“Well, the one thing is, we have jihadists being elected all over the place,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, without specifying who he was talking about or offering evidence of his claims.

“We have this whether it’s communism, jihadism,” Trump added.

The president has frequently cast Democrats and democratic socialists as communists, looking to portray the party as increasingly extreme headed into November — even though portrayals of even the party’s most liberal candidates as communists are far from reality.

But calling them “jihadists” is a new escalation, which Trump acknowledged in his remarks Monday, recounting that a “friend of mine called up,” and told him, “’You know, really, you should use the word jihadist because that’s what’s happening.’” The president’s escalating rhetoric comes amid broad lines of attack from others in the GOP seeking to paint Muslim candidates as anti-American.

Trump said that, “as an example,” some of the candidates he termed “jihadist” are coming from countries like Somalia. The president has repeatedly criticized Rep. Ilhan Omar, a Minnesota Democrat who was born in Somalia, came to the United States as a child and is now a naturalized citizen. Trump has previously advocated for sending Omar and another Muslim congresswoman “back from where they came.”

He’s also unleashed increasingly provocative rhetoric against Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, saying at a campaign event in Las Vegas last week that he’s “full of sh*t” and is a “hater of Jews and hater of Israel,” without offering evidence. El-Sayed, who is Muslim, has been critical of the Israeli government.

On Monday, Trump posted on Truth Social an image of El-Sayed with Sen. Elizabeth Warren in a Native American headdress, with the caption, “Pocahontas and ‘Abdul’ want to take your stuff, and Crash the Economy!!!” And over the weekend, Trump shared an image of himself and first lady Melania Trump alongside a photo of El-Sayed and his wife, Sarah Jukaku, who wears a hijab. The caption read: “Two very different America’s.”

In an interview on CNN’s Sate of the Union with Jake Tapper, El-Sayed agreed that the two images offered differing visions of America.

“Yeah, he’s right. One in which your overlords are two people who don’t like each other but joint in the interest of making billions of dollars off of you. Or, two people who genuinely love each other, enjoyed some pancakes together, want to come together to build the kind of America where they can raise a family and know that that family is going to have the good thing,” El-Sayed said. “So, yes, you got two different visions of America.”

And it’s not just Trump engaging in that sort of rhetoric. Shortly after El-Sayed won the Democratic nomination last week, national Republicans repeatedly started referring to him by his full name: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed.

Previously, Trump has accused Democrats of being taken over by “godless Communists” who pose an existential threat to the country. And while the democratic socialist movement appears set to push the Democratic Party further to the left, the tenets of socialism — much less democratic socialism — are still far removed from the communist ideology that Trump has loudly, and inaccurately, portrayed as a rising threat.

This story has been updated with additional details.

World.title: Former Syrian President Assad sentenced to death in absentia
World.content:
AP —

A Syrian court sentenced ousted Syrian President Bashar al-Assad along with his younger brother to death in absentia on Tuesday for crimes against humanity and war crimes during Syria’s 14-year conflict that left about half a million people dead.

The sentences at the Fourth Criminal Court in Damascus are the first against Assad or members of his inner circle since the Assad family’s five decades in power came to an end 20 months ago.

“Bashar Assad used state agencies to commit war crimes and crimes against humanity,” said judge Fakhareddine al-Aryan during a court session that was aired live on state TV.

Also sentenced to death in the same case was Assad’s maternal cousin Atef Najib, who was convicted of overseeing a crackdown in the southern province of Daraa that led to the uprising and later the civil war.

Atef Najib appears in court in Syria on Tuesday. Syrian Ministry of Justice

Amid tight security, Najib stood inside a cage wearing a prisoner’s uniform as the judge read the sentence. A crowd of people gathered outside the courthouse in central Damascus to hear the verdict.

Assad and his brother Maher fled to Russia after the government’s fall in December 2024 and received political asylum. Syria’s new rulers have asked Russia to hand the Assads over.

Najib, who was sanctioned by the U.S. Department of the Treasury in April 2011, was later detained and is one of the highest-ranking officials to be put on trial.

Najib is a former Syrian army brigadier general who was head of the Political Security Branch in southern Syria’s Daraa province under Assad in 2011.

During his tenure, more than a dozen teenagers who scrawled anti-government graffiti on a school wall in Daraa were arrested and tortured. The case became a catalyst for mass protests against the repressive policies of Assad’s security forces.

The protests were met by a brutal government crackdown and spiraled into a 14-year civil war that ended with Assad’s ouster in a lightning rebel offensive.

Maher Assad was a former commander of the Syrian military’s 4th Armored Division – which Syrian opposition activists have accused of killings, torture, extortion and drug trafficking, in addition to running its own detention centers.

World.title: Trump loves data centers. Americans hate them
World.content:
If there’s a true populist issue built for this moment in time, it might be opposition to AI data centers. Lawmakers and candidates from both parties across states are increasingly positioning themselves as critics of data center proliferation.

And recent primary results suggest it’s a pretty potent issue.

There is, however, one big exception to the growing political stampede away from data centers: President Donald Trump and his administration officials, who are bear-hugging them.

It’s merely the latest political head-scratcher from the president, given the growing volume of polls showing just how much Americans hate data centers and overwhelmingly don’t seem to want them in their communities.

Trump’s defenses of data centers have grown substantially in recent weeks. He’s not only pitched them as vital to competing with China on artificial intelligence, but as win-wins for the US communities that welcome them.

Trump loves data centers

Back in March, the administration debuted an initiative called the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, which aimed to get developers to voluntarily promise that data center construction wouldn’t raise people’s energy bills.

But even at the time, Trump downplayed the need for his executive action. He suggested data centers weren’t really raising energy bills in the first place.

“They need some PR help, because people think that if a data center goes in there, electricity prices are going to go up,” Trump said.

Last month, he sharply criticized Democratic New York Gov. Kathy Hochul for signing an executive order halting the construction of new data centers. Trump on social media called them “big, strong, bold, and Money Machines” and “Cash Cows, with Lower Taxes and Record Setting Jobs.”

Last week, he told Fox News that “any community that turns down AI is making a big mistake,” claiming data centers would reduce taxes and make property values go up.

He called it “a tremendous thing” and even seemed to marvel at how anybody could oppose them.

“It’s almost like there’s a campaign against, you know, data centers,” the president said.

And then in an interview with Punchbowl News later in the week, he took aim at GOP-controlled Texas, which moved to more strongly regulate data center construction.

Trump said data centers could be “bigger than oil.”

“I don’t think they’re unsightly,” he added. “I mean, I’m looking at some of these data centers — the most incredible buildings I’ve ever seen. They go for two-and-a-half, three miles.”

But the American people really don’t like them

Virtually everything Trump is saying is at odds with where the American people are.

Americans opposed the construction of new data centers 45 percent-16 percent in a Reuters-Ipsos poll in June.

And the margins grew significantly when it came to building them in their communities. The margin against grew to 59 percent-10 percent when the data centers were within 10 miles of the person’s home. Gallup in March showed 7 in 10 Americans opposed building data centers “in your area.”

The passion is clearly on the side of the critics.

Only between 3 percent and 7 percent strongly supported the construction of data centers in their areas in the above polls, while between 44 percent to 48 percent strongly opposed them.

While 61 percent of Americans said data centers were necessary in the Reuters poll, 77 percent wanted them to be built in remote areas away from communities.

The Sabey Data Centers Seattle Data Center campus in Tukwila, Washington, US, on Saturday, July 11, 2026. David Ryder/Bloomberg/Getty Images

Despite Trump’s claims that data centers are economic boons and potentially “bigger than oil,” just 50 percent of Americans think they create jobs and are good for the economy. And only 1 in 6 feel that way strongly, saying that describes data centers “very” or “extremely” well.

Despite Trump’s claim that data centers aren’t or wouldn’t make electricity more expensive, 77 percent said they were doing just that in Reuters/Ipsos polling earlier in June, while two-thirds said the same in a March Pew Research Center poll.

And finally, all told, Americans said by a whopping 71 percent-29 percent margin that the costs of data centers outweighed the benefits, according a Marquette Law School poll in May.

Most notably: All of these polls suggest it’s a remarkably bipartisan aversion. Republicans are somewhat more likely to see the benefits of data centers and welcome them in their communities, but they’re strongly against them, too.

The bipartisan campaigns against and efforts to rein in data centers

That bipartisanship has made itself clear in how the issue has been addressed across the country — and not just in New York and Texas. Bills banning data center construction have been proposed in 15 states, spanning from deep red to deep blue.

The issue also featured prominently in both parties’ gubernatorial primaries in Kansas last week, with critics winning both primaries. (The Democrat who won, state Sen. Cindy Holscher, disowned a previous vote in favor of data center construction and strongly backed a moratorium.) Both parties’ gubernatorial nominees in Ohio also back a moratorium.

Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and House candidate William Lawrence played up the issue on their way to primary victories in Michigan last week. And Democratic Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong looks to do the same Tuesday after making the issue her calling card.

They’ve all seemed to sense the rare issue that truly galvanizes — both because it directly impacts Americans in their communities and, they worry, is exacerbating their already increasing costs.

But Trump seems to be making a different calculation.

World.title: Trump says the US has “mine swept the entire” Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
President Donald Trump said Monday that the United States has swept the Strait of Hormuz for mines and claimed the US Navy has full control of the vital waterway.

“It’s open now. Look, the only one that has control of the Strait of Hormuz right now is the United States Navy,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

“They will, on occasion, drop a mine, and we find the mine,” the president added. “You know, we’ve mine swept the entire strait, as you probably maybe heard, maybe you didn’t hear.”

He added that the United States controls the strait “100%.”

Earlier Monday, Trump applied a new condition to talks with Iran, saying he would require compensation from the country for past misdeeds after Tehran said US compensation was required to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said an agreement with Oman to manage the strait would not be enough to reopen the waterway unless the United States meets the list of conditions.

World.title: Egypt, US discuss investment opportunities, desalination cooperation
World.content:
Housing Minister Randa al-Menshawy and US Chargé d’Affaires Robert Silverman discussed on Monday, August 10, 2026, ways to expand bilateral cooperation in housing, urban development and infrastructure.

The talks focused on investment opportunities in Egypt’s new cities and potential cooperation in seawater desalination, including the use of advanced technologies and expertise in the sector.

al-Menshawy said Egypt’s expanding urban development projects offer opportunities for partnerships with US companies and international institutions, helping attract investment and transfer modern technologies.

Silverman expressed interest in expanding cooperation with the Housing Ministry and US companies, citing Egypt’s growing investment opportunities and major urban development projects.

The two sides agreed to maintain coordination and communication in the coming period to explore new areas of joint cooperation.

World.title: FM reaffirms Egypt’s full solidarity with Lebanon to preserve its sovereignty
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty reaffirmed Egypt’s full solidarity with Lebanon to preserve its sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and national institutions.

Abdelatty made the remarks on Monday, Aug 10, 2026, in a phone call with Lebanese Foreign Minister and Emigrants Youssef Rajji, during which they discussed ways to strengthen bilateral ties, as well as developments in Lebanon and the region.

Abdelatty said Egypt highly values its historical and fraternal ties with Lebanon, while stressing his country’s keenness to work with the Lebanese side to promote bilateral relations and advance cooperation across various fields.

The two ministers also tackled the latest round of negotiations between Lebanon and Israel, held in Rome earlier this month, and exchanged views on the outcome of the talks, with a view to creating conditions conducive to completing Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanese territory.

Abdelatty underlined the importance of maintaining the negotiating track and building on progress made during the latest round to achieve tangible results that respect Lebanon’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

He also called for the full and non-selective implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701, urging Israel to halt all military attacks on Lebanon and withdraw completely from Lebanese territory in a move that would strengthen Lebanon’s security and stability and prevent renewed cycles of escalation in the region.

Abdelatty also reaffirmed Egypt’s full support for the Lebanese government and its efforts to strengthen state sovereignty and extend its authority across the country, as well as for state institutions, particularly the Lebanese army, to enable it to fulfil its national responsibilities in maintaining security and stability.

The top Egyptian diplomat emphasized that Lebanese state institutions should remain the framework for managing the country’s affairs and safeguarding its stability.

For his part, Rajji expressed appreciation for Egypt’s steadfast support for Lebanon, praising Cairo’s continued backing of the Lebanese state and its institutions.

Rajji also affirmed Lebanon’s keenness to maintain coordination and consultations with Egypt on issues of common concern.

World.title: Egypt, Japan discuss expanding education projects
World.content:
Minister of Education and Technical Education Mohamed Abdel Latif on Monday, August 10, 2026, met with Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) First Vice President Yuko Mitsui, as they discussed developments in Egypt-Japan cooperation in education and ways to expand existing projects.

The talks took place during Abdel Latif’s visit to Japan and covered the expansion of Egyptian-Japanese schools, teacher training and prospects for extending Japanese educational practices to mainstream schools.

Abdel Latif said the number of Egyptian-Japanese schools will rise to 102 in September, up from 69 last year and 52 two years ago.

Mitsui praised the Education Ministry’s efforts to increase the number of Egyptian-Japanese schools, while maintaining the quality of education. She also underlined the importance of continuing the approach to maximize the benefits of the Japanese model.

The two sides also tackled a cooperation program with Hiroshima University to train and develop teachers, which is scheduled to begin in September.

Abdel Latif said the program will provide comprehensive training based on the Japanese education system, combining theoretical, practical and research components to enhance teachers’ skills.

The program will be held in person in Egypt, with Hiroshima University professors delivering 10 courses covering academic, practical and research aspects, the minister said.

Mitsui expressed interest in the program, highlighting its importance in strengthening teachers’ capabilities and drawing on Japanese expertise in training and developing educational staff.

The talks also addressed expanding cooperation beyond Egyptian-Japanese schools to include mainstream public schools, allowing Japanese educational practices to be adapted to the Egyptian context.

The two sides explored the possibility of benefiting from Egypt’s experience with the Japanese education model as a successful example of international educational cooperation and transferring the experience to Arab and African countries.

JICA vice president said that Japan viewed the Egyptian-Japanese experience as an outstanding example of educational cooperation outside Japan and expressed her country’s desire to further develop it and expand its benefits.

The talks also covered Japanese supervision of Egyptian-Japanese schools. The number of Japanese supervisors is expected to reach 39 by September, with the supervisors overseeing academic and administrative aspects and transferring Japanese expertise to Egyptian staff.

The two sides stressed the importance of maintaining coordination and cooperation in the coming period to strengthen the strategic education partnership between Egypt and Japan, support efforts to develop the education system and broaden the use of Japanese expertise in the region and Africa.

World.title: PM reaffirms gov’t commitment to developing stock market performance
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reaffirmed the government’s commitment to developing the performance of the stock exchange, enhancing its stability and protecting investors across non-banking financial sectors.

Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting he held on Monday, August 10, 2026, to review a number of proposals aimed at improving the performance of the Egyptian Exchange, as well as the progress it has made in recent months.

The meeting was attended by Investment and Foreign Trade Minister Mohamed Farid Saleh, Financial Regulatory Authority Chairman Islam Azzam and Egyptian Exchange Chairman Omar Radwan.

The Premier welcomed positive developments on the Egyptian Exchange, particularly a rise in average daily trading value to LE15 billion (US $304 million) and market capitalization exceeding four trillion LE.

Farid presented recent performance indicators for the securities market and outlined measures under consideration to improve the exchange, particularly government offerings and incentives to encourage private-sector companies to list.

The meeting also tackled preparations for government offerings, including efforts to ready companies for trading and prepare major entities, both state-owned and private, to take advantage of new tax incentives for listings and trading on the Egyptian Exchange.

It also reviewed proposed legislative amendments to Law No. 95 of 1992 and its executive regulations, as well as efforts to highlight tax advantages and incentives linked to securities trading.

The meeting reviewed plans to transform the Egyptian Exchange into a joint-stock company, with the possibility of eventually listing it, while also reviewing upgrades to its trading and market-surveillance technology infrastructure.

The attendees further explored new mechanisms for short selling, derivatives and market makers, as well as measures encouraging private insurance funds to invest required portions of their assets in shares and equity investment funds listed on the Egyptian Exchange.

The meeting stressed the need to remove obstacles to establishing new private insurance funds serving a broad segment of investors.

World.title: Liberia: Supreme Court Suspends Criminal Court “C” Proceedings Amid Jury-Tampering Legal Challenge
World.content:
MONROVIA — The Supreme Court of Liberia has intervened in the ongoing legal controversy surrounding the corruption trial of former Finance and Development Planning Minister Samuel D. Tweah Jr. and several former government officials, ordering a temporary suspension of proceedings before Criminal Court “C” pending a hearing on a petition for a writ of prohibition.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

The directive from the Supreme Court places a hold on further proceedings in the challenged matter before Criminal Court “C,” where Assigned Circuit Judge Ousman F. Feika has been presiding over proceedings connected to the disputed jury verdict in the high-profile corruption case.

The intervention was communicated through an official notice dated August 3, 2026, from the Office of the Clerk of the Supreme Court. The communication summons Judge Feika to appear before Associate Justice Yussif D. Kaba, who is currently presiding in Chambers, for a conference on Wednesday, August 12, at 3:00 p.m.

Justice Kaba, pending the scheduled conference, has directed that all further proceedings and actions in the matter identified in the petition be stayed. The order effectively prevents Criminal Court “C” from taking additional action on the contested proceedings until the Supreme Court reviews the legal issues raised by the petition.

The Supreme Court’s decision introduces a new judicial dimension to an already complicated case that has attracted considerable public attention because of allegations of jury misconduct and possible interference with the deliberations of jurors. The controversy emerged following the conclusion of the corruption trial involving Tweah and four other former officials of the former government.
