World.title: The Green Heart of Zagreb: Exploring the Croatian Capital’s Parks
World.content:
August the 10th, 2026 – Zagreb is one of the most heavily forested EU capitals, and the green heart of Zagreb acts as the lungs of the urban side’s beating heart.

Zagreb, much like Croatia as a whole, is very widely praised for its cafe culture, but you don’t need to be sitting in a busy city street to enjoy that coffee. Less celebrated, but equally defining, is just how green the city feels. Parks, gardens, lakes and densely forested hills weave through and around the capital, giving it (as touched on above) one of the highest concentrations of green space among EU cities.

For visitors, this means you can move from a museum, restaurant or old square to a lush, green meadow or park in mere minutes. Croatia is full of natural beauty, but when it comes to cities, these spaces are not an afterthought or somewhere forgotten by builders, they’re an absolutely central to the city’s identity and daily life.

The Green Horseshoe: Nature Woven into the City Centre

Sanjin Kastelan/TZGZ

Turning the clock back to the late 19th century, celebrated urban planner Milan Lenuci designed a U-shaped sequence of parks and squares that still frames the Lower Town (Donji grad). Known locally as Lenuci’s Green Horseshoe (or, if you want to get even more local: Zelena potkova), it connects promenades, blooming flower beds, monuments and grand public buildings into a continuous green corridor stretching for roughly 1.2 miles.

Zrinjevac is arguably the most atmospheric part of all. Just a short walk from the hustle and bustle of Ban Jelačić Square, an oasis awaits. It features towering mature plane trees, flower beds, fountains and a distinctive cast-iron music pavilion. During the summer, the pavilion hosts open-air concerts and free dance evenings; locals and visitors gather for waltz, swing or salsa under the trees. The scorching Croatian summer heat is calmed by the trees and thick plant life. The sequence continues near Strossmayer Square and King Tomislav Square, all the way to the main railway station (Glavni kolodvor), with statues, shaded walkways and seasonal colour. During the much cooler winter, Tomislav Square transforms into a ice rink; while swapping out its winter attire to serve as an open stage for classical concerts in summer.

Julien Duval/TZGZ

These central parks reward unhurried wandering. They are places to sit with a coffee, watch the city pass by, or simply appreciate how thoughtfully nature was integrated into Zagreb’s 19th-century expansion.

zagreb’s botanical garden

Marko Vrdoljak/TZGZ

At the southwestern end of the Green Horseshoe sits the Zagreb Botanical Garden (Botanički vrt). It was formally established back in 1889 by Professor Antun Heinz of the University of Zagreb, and opened to the public in 1891. Spanning about five hectares, it is both a scientific institution and a public garden of real charm.

The layout mixes English landscape style, long, winding paths, irregular plantings and a substantial arboretum with a more formal French-style parterre of flower beds. Collections include native Croatian flora, alpine and Mediterranean plants, aquatic species, conifers, and exotic trees and shrubs from all around the world. Estimates of the plant holdings range from several thousand to over 10,000 taxa, including many protected and endemic species. Small lakes with bridges, a rock garden and historic glasshouses (including a house for the giant Amazonian water lily Victoria amazonica) add to the allure.

Boska i Kreso/TZGZ

The garden is compact enough to explore in an hour or two yet rich enough to reward slower visits. It’s open seasonally (typically from April to early November, with limited winter opening in particularly calm, good weather) and charges a modest entrance fee. Located a short walk from the main train station, it is one of the easiest major green spaces to reach.

the legendary (and gorgeous) park maksimir

Julien Duval/TZGZ

East of the city centre lies Maksimir, the city’s largest, most famous, and most beloved park of all. Founded on the initiative of Bishop Maksimilijan Vrhovac and opened to the public back in 1794, it was the first large public park in all of southeastern Europe at the time. Spanning roughly 316 hectares (about 780 acres or so), it is comparable in scale to some of the grand European landscape parks and remains a protected monument of garden architecture and cultural heritage.

Originally conceived with baroque elements and later reshaped in the English Romantic style under Bishop Juraj Haulik, Maksimir combines broad meadows, mature oak and hornbeam woodland, five artificial lakes, streams, pavilions and long tree-lined avenues. Historic structures like the Swiss House, the Echo Pavilion and lookout points still stand. Wildlife of all kinds absolutely thrives here, with the park a well known habitat for birds, including rarer species.

Julien Duval/TZGZ

Within the park sits Zagreb Zoo, one of the oldest in the region (opened 1925), home to lions and all kinds of other animals you (thankfully) wouldn’t bump into in a cafe.

Families come for the playgrounds and lakeside walks; runners and walkers use the extensive paths; picnickers claim the grass on weekends. Trams (lines 4, 7, 11 and 12 among others) make it straightforward to reach. Maksimir feels both historic and lived-in. It’s a genuine city park that has adapted to changing fashions while retaining its charming, grand 18th- and 19th-century character.

the city of lakes – meet bundek and jarun

Julien Duval/TZGZ

South of the centre, the winding Sava River corridor offers a different kind of green space with a distinctly more recreational and watery character.

Bundek Park in Novi Zagreb sits between the Liberty (Most slobode) and Youth (Most mladosti) bridges. It centres on two expansive lakes surrounded by walking and cycling paths, meadows, playgrounds, sports courts and barbecue areas. Significantly renovated back during the mid-2000s, it has become a beloved for families, picnics and summer swimming (with lifeguards on the larger lake during the hotter season). An open-air stage hosts events, including the Pop Up by the Lake festival. Its proximity to the city centre (a short bus ride from the main station) and relaxed atmosphere make it especially popular with locals.

Julien Duval/TZGZ

Jarun sits further west and is often called Zagreb’s very own “sea”. This large artificial lake is ringed by paths popular with cyclists, runners and more. Islands, beaches, cafes, outdoor gym equipment and sports facilities give it a lively, active character. During the summer, it is a major venue for outdoor living; it also hosts the INmusic festival. Trams 5 and 17 serve the area. Where Bundek feels more intimate and family-oriented, Jarun offers scale and a truly energetic feel. Together, the two lakes give Zagreb something very few inland capitals possess: genuine waterside recreation within easy reach of the busy urban core.

bear mountain – medvednica has always had zagreb’s back (quite literally)

Julien Duval/TZGZ

Just north of Zagreb rises Medvednica, a densely forested mountain and protected nature park that functions as the city’s great outdoor backyard. Its highest peak, Sljeme, stands at 1,033 metres. The park is home to dozens of marked hiking trails of varying difficulty, mountain lodges serving traditional food, the medieval fortress of Medvedgrad, the Veternica cave, and viewpoints that look back over the entire city.

Miroslav Zadravec/TZGZ

Popular routes include the gradual Leustek trail and the steeper Bikčević trail toward the summit or lodges such as Puntijarka. Medvedgrad itself is a rewarding shorter destination, combining history with panoramic views. In winter the upper reaches attract skiers and sledgers; year-round the forest offers cool shade and clean air. Public transport (tram to Mihaljevac followed by bus, or the Sljeme cable car) and road access make it straightforward for visitors without a car. Few European capitals can claim a proper mountain nature park so close to the centre. For many Zagreb residents, “going to Sljeme” remains a ritual escape.

Though named after the populations of brown bears that once called it home (in Croatia, bear is medvjed), you won’t find them there now. As Zagreb expanded and grew, the bears retreated to more remote areas. If you do want to see them – head to Lika!

honestly, you can’t even name them all…

Julien Duval/TZGZ

Beyond these major sites, Zagreb is sprinkled with additional green spaces. Ribnjak Park near the cathedral offers a more intimate central oasis. Tuškanac and Cmrok on the northern slopes provide wooded walks and, in winter, popular sledging slopes. Mirogoj Cemetery, designed by Herman Bollé, is as much a landscaped park and open-air architectural gallery as a burial ground, with arcades, monuments and mature trees.

Julien Duval/TZGZ

Most city parks are free to enter, but the Botanical Garden and Zagreb Zoo charge modest fees. Public transport (trams and buses) reaches nearly all the major sites efficiently; walking and cycling are excellent options for the central Green Horseshoe and the lakeside paths. Spring brings blossom and milder temperatures; summer is ideal for the lakes and shaded trails; autumn colours are spectacular in Maksimir and on Medvednica; winter has its own quiet beauty, especially after snow has fallen.

zagreb gets hot, but it would be far hotter without these green spaces

Julien Duval/TZGZ

The above photo likely doesn’t stir up mental images of sunscreen and t-shirts, but we won’t sugarcoat it – Croatia is extremely hot in summer. Zagreb, far from the sea breeze, can become absolutely stifling. This is where the functionality of these green spaces come to the fore. Zagreb’s green network is not merely decorative. It cools the city down, supports biodiversity, provides everyday recreation for residents and offers visitors an immediate sense of the city’s character.

Sanjin Kastelan/TZGZ

You can step out of a cafe on the main square and be under the protective shade of tall plane trees within minutes, or leave the centre and be hiking forest trails and bumping into deer an hour later. That accessibility is rare and worth experiencing deliberately when in Zagreb. Everyone can become sick of the sound, pace and stress of the city, but you can’t always escape it as easily as you can here.

Whether you prefer the grandeur and elegance of Zrinjevac, Maksimir’s sprawling trails and numerous lakes, the energy of Bundek and Jarun, Medvednica or anywhere else, Zagreb’s green spaces should enjoy much more attention than they get.

World.title: Big Changes Coming for Drivers in Croatia in Autumn
World.content:
August the 10th, 2026 – Big changes are on the horizon for drivers in Croatia this autumn, more specifically as of October the 1st.

The beginning of the roll out of this change has in fact already begun. As of the 1st of July this year, drivers in Croatia are no longer able to use their previous top up SMART cards. However, they’ve still been able to spend the existing balance on them and will be able to continue doing so until the end of September.

After October the 1st, the SMART card will cease to function entirely as a means of payment on the motorways managed by HAC (Croatian Motorways), as reported by Poslovni.

an overhaul of a system used for years

For drivers in Croatia who still have a remaining amount on the card, there are two possibilities available to them. Those who wish to continue using electronic toll collection can transfer the money from their SMART prepaid account to an ENC prepaid account. In the process of doing that, they can exchange their SMART card for an ENC device at Croatian Motorways sales offices.

The second option is intended for those who do not wish to switch to ENC. They can request the closure of the SMART prepaid account and a refund of the available money. The request can be sent to HAC by e-mail or submitted in person at one of their sales offices.

Some drivers have been using the SMART system for years, especially on the motorways previously managed by Autocesta Rijeka – Zagreb, so it’s fairly understandable that some cards are still sitting in cars. Precisely these users should pay attention to the deadline, because after 30 September they will no longer be able to spend the remaining balance in the usual way.

massive changes are afoot for the toll collection system

The change comes at a time of major interventions in the Croatian toll collection system and increasing reliance on electronic payment. For the SMART card user themselves, however, the most important question is much simpler – whether there is still money on the account and what to do with it before the card ceases to be valid.

That is why it is not a bad idea to check the balance already now, especially if you use the SMART card only occasionally. Until the 1st of October, it can still be used for payment, but topping up is no longer possible. After that date the options remain transferring the funds to ENC or getting a monetary refund.

World.title: Iraq auto sales drop 28.6% in H1 2026 amid broad economic slowdown
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — New vehicle sales in Iraq dropped 28.6% year-on-year during the first half of 2026, totaling 59,264 units sold through official dealerships, according to a report by automotive data provider Focus2move released on Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

The downturn marks a sharp contraction following years of strong expansion between 2021 and 2024, when annual sales peaked at 158,076 units. Market analysts attribute the drop to liquidity constraints, delayed public sector payrolls, and broader macroeconomic uncertainty across the country.

Key Brand Performance & Market Share Breakdown

Kia Motors: Maintained the market leadership spot with a 28% market share, despite a 27.8% decline in total sales volume.

Toyota: Ranked second with a 22% market share, recording a 24% drop in deliveries.

Nissan: Held third place, with sales falling 13.3%.

MG: Placed fourth with an 8.9% market share, seeing sales decline 31.6%.

Jetour: Advanced to fifth place with an 8.4% market share, bucking the industry trend with a 29.2% sales increase.

Great Wall Motor (GWM): Achieved positive growth, with sales rising 6.9%.

Hyundai: Experienced the steepest contraction among major global manufacturers, with sales plummeting 69.7%.

The electric vehicle (EV) segment experienced a severe downturn during H1 2026, with sales falling 72% to represent just 1% of total automotive market share. Chinese automaker BYD led the EV niche with a 48.3% market share, followed closely by Toyota at 43.4%.

While official figures reflect authorized dealership transactions, auto market observers note that Iraq’s grey market and used car showrooms suffered even heavier losses. Used car dealership owners estimate that sales volumes dropped between 40% and 50% compared to the same period in 2025, driven by reduced consumer spending power and tighter household budgets.

World.title: Parliamentary committee: Iraq holds 109T IQD reserves, salaries secured for 10 months
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Parliamentary Finance Committee announced on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, that the nation’s cash reserves stand at 109 trillion Iraqi Dinars (approximately $83 billion), ensuring that public sector salaries and pensions are fully secured for at least 10 months despite regional financial pressures.

Committee member Mansour Al-Baiji stated to official state media that senior lawmakers met on Monday with Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi, Minister of Finance Faleh Al-Sari, and Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) Governor Nizar Nasir Hussein to evaluate the state’s liquidity and fiscal stability.

Key Financial Indicators & Statements

Treasury Cash Reserves: Central Bank Governor Nizar Nasir Hussein confirmed 109 trillion IQD (~$83 billion) in liquid cash reserves inside the treasury.

Public Payroll Security: The available cash reserves alone are sufficient to cover state employee and pensioner salaries for 10 consecutive months, supplemented by gold bullion holdings and non-oil revenues.

Government Alignment: High-level executive coordination continues between Prime Minister Al-Zaidi, the Ministry of Finance, and the CBI to navigate liquidity bottlenecks caused by recent oil export disruptions.

The announcement aims to reassure public sector workers following recent salary disbursement delays caused by severe crude export drops and liquidity constraints linked to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Al-Baiji emphasized that ongoing understandings between the Finance Committee, the Ministry of Finance, and the Central Bank have established proactive fiscal measures to maintain state liquidity, protect gold reserves, and stabilize the national currency.

World.title: Suspected militia drone strike destroys $400M Taji tank ammo reserves
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi security and intelligence authorities are conducting a high-level investigation into an early August explosion at Taji Camp north of Baghdad, suspecting a targeted drone strike rather than a heat-induced fire as initially reported, according to an investigation by Asharq Al-Awsat on Monday, August 10, 2026.

Military sources confirmed that heat-signature camera feeds captured an unidentified drone arriving from south of Baghdad before the ammunition depot detonated. The strike severely degraded the primary munition reserves of the Iraqi Army’s premier 9th Armored Division, destroying vital 120mm shells for U.S.-made M1A1 Abrams tanks and armored personnel carriers.

Key Investigation Metrics & Financial Impact

Disputed Official Cause: Ministry of Defense originally reported a August 2 fire caused by summer temperatures; intelligence sources now cite a precision drone strike launched from south of Baghdad.

Massive Ammo Losses: The depot contained approximately 50,000 tank and armored vehicle shells, representing the bulk of the 9th Armored Division’s heavy munitions inventory.

Severe Financial Toll: With standard 120mm tank rounds valued between $5,000 and $10,000 per unit, total material losses are estimated at $250 million to $500 million.

Zero Depot Inventory: Senior military officers revealed that the 9th Division’s strategic reserve of tank shells has been effectively reduced to zero, leaving only the immediate rounds pre-loaded inside operational tanks.

Emergency Procurement Request: Iraq has placed an urgent defense procurement order with foreign suppliers to immediately replenish its depleted tank and armored vehicle ammunition stocks.

Security analysts view the Taji strike as part of a preemptive effort by hardline armed factions to neutralize the Iraqi Armed Forces’ heavy armored advantage ahead of Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s September 30 deadline for non-state groups to hand over weaponry or integrate into state forces.

Addressing drone activity during a press conference on Monday, Interior Ministry Spokesperson Major General Muqdad Miri warned: “Any unauthorized drone operation will be treated strictly as an act of terrorism. All weaponry within the country must submit unconditionally to the authority of the state.”

With the 9th Armored Division actively redeploying units to secure the upcoming Arba’een pilgrimage, the loss of its central ammunition depot presents a major operational challenge for the Ministry of Defense as federal authorities attempt to maintain military superiority over rogue armed groups.

World.title: UNFPA Advisor clarifies Iraq population growth
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Claims of explosive population growth in Iraq are vastly exaggerated, according to Mahdi Al-Alak, Senior Advisor to the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA). Speaking to official state media on Monday, August 10, 2026, Al-Alak pointed to official census figures demonstrating a steady decline in national demographic growth rates over the past two decades.

Al-Alak highlighted a dramatic shift in family sizes, noting that while an average Iraqi woman gave birth to 6 to 7 children during the 1980s, recent national census data shows the fertility rate has dropped by more than half to 3 births per woman.

Key Demographic Findings

Declining Annual Growth: Iraq’s current annual population growth rate stands at 2.51%, down from over 3% recorded two decades ago.

Sharp Drop in Fertility: Average births per woman have dropped from 6–7 children in the 1980s to 3 births today, according to the latest census data.

Global Benchmark Comparison: While Iraq’s 2.51% growth rate remains higher than the global average of 1.1%, the internal trajectory shows a clear long-term deceleration.

UNFPA Assessment: Claims of an unmanageable demographic explosion misrepresent actual census trends and structural social shifts.

The slowing population growth rate reflects changing economic realities, urbanization, higher educational attainment among women, and shifting social norms regarding family planning across Iraqi governorates.

While a 2.51% growth rate continues to place demands on public infrastructure, housing, and job creation, UNFPA officials stress that the long-term trend indicates a stabilizing demographic profile rather than an uncontrolled population surge.

World.title: Trump says would be ‘terrible mistake’ to oust embattled Infantino
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said on Monday it would be “a terrible mistake” to replace Gianni Infantino, the embattled FIFA president who tried, and failed, to sell off part of the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino came under renewed fire in an open letter signed by three confederations — Europe’s UEFA, North and Central America’s CONCACAF and Asia’s AFC — accusing the world football boss of breaking trust “through deception”.

But Trump backed Infantino, who awarded the US president a “FIFA Peace Prize” at the World Cup draw ceremony last year.

“FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino,” Trump posted on Truth Social.

Trump called Infantino “fantastic” and said he “presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented”.

“If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!” added Trump, who attended the World Cup final with Infantino last month.

Trump’s backing of Infantino is at odds with US Soccer, who joined the voices lining up against the FIFA president.

Infantino launched, and then withdrew in the face of scathing criticism, a plan to bring private investment into FIFA competitions, including World Cups.

FIFA hit back on Saturday at efforts “to undermine” football’s governing body and Infantino.

However, Monday’s joint letter from UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC retorted: “Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

– UEFA boycott threat –

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is viewed as a potential challenger to Infantino, who will be up for re-election for a fourth and final term at the FIFA Congress in March, 2027. Candidates have to be declared by November 18.

Infantino had looked certain to be unopposed for a fourth term after overseeing a successful World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada until his plans were revealed.

The 56-year-old Swiss, who has been in situ for 10 years, has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive.

Individual member associations, not confederations, vote in the FIFA election,

Infantino has received support from CONCACAF’s Mexico and two AFC members — Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar, where he has a house.

– ‘Shabby, backroom deal’ –

UEFA’s threat to boycott World Cups if the private investment plan went ahead proved pivotal in Infantino withdrawing his sell-off plan.

UEFA had called it “a shabby, opaque, backroom deal” and lashed out at Infantino again on Monday for a “failure of judgment”.

After the furore, Infantino received “full support” of senior FIFA directors in an emergency meeting in Morocco last week, but the three confederations said that was meaningless.

The recent meeting, where “a select number of members of the FIFA Management Committee” were present, they said, “represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment”.

“It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him.”

Infantino had been basking in the afterglow of the largest ever World Cup involving 48 teams until his plans divided the sport.

“The growth over the past decade has been real. But that progress was never the work of one individual,” declared the letter.

“It was the product of FIFA, the Confederations, the Member Associations, and the thousands of people who dedicate their lives to the game.

“The expanded tournaments… were shared achievements, agreed together, delivered together.”

Under Infantino’s leadership “there is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness”, they said.

“That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve.

“Football’s strength has always been its unity.”

World.title: Russian barrage on Ukraine kills 9, wounds dozens
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian attacks across Ukraine killed at least nine people overnight and wounded dozens, authorities said Tuesday, after Kyiv warned that Moscow had received more ballistic missiles from North Korea.

Russia has stepped up ballistic missile strikes on Ukrainian cities in recent weeks, with Ukraine responding with strikes deep inside Russian territory.

The overnight attacks spanned Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk, regional authorities said.

Russia’s defence ministry said its forces “delivered a group strike with high-precision ground-based weapons, hitting military-industrial enterprises and transport-logistics centres in the cities of Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia”.

In Zaporizhzhia, Ivan Fedorov, head of the regional military administration, said Russian forces launched a “massive” attack using missiles and guided aerial bombs.

“Six people were killed and 19 others wounded,” Fedorov wrote on Telegram, updating an earlier toll of five dead.

In the eastern Dnipropetrovsk region, Russian drone and artillery strikes on five districts killed three people and wounded five others, regional military administration head Oleksandr Ganzha said on Telegram.

In Kyiv, AFP journalists heard a series of explosions shortly after midnight after authorities issued a missile alert.

Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on social media that the capital was “under ballistic missile attack”.

Ukraine’s emergency service said a warehouse caught fire and one person was wounded.

President Volodymyr Zelensky had said earlier that Russia was preparing to deploy more North Korean troops and had received new ballistic missiles from Pyongyang.

Only certain air defence systems, including US Patriots, are capable of intercepting ballistic missiles.

A shortage of PAC-3 interceptors has worsened since the war launched by the United States and Israel against Iran in February.

At the same time, Ukraine has been increasing its strikes against Russian cities far from the border.

World.title: Oil prices rise further as hopes for Hormuz deal fade
World.content:
Hong Kong – Oil prices extended hefty gains Tuesday as hopes for a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz fade, fanning fresh inflation fears and ramping up bets on at least one US interest rate hike this year.

Crude has surged around 10 percent over the past week, with the United States and Iran appearing no closer to a deal on the crucial waterway despite upbeat comments from the White House earlier in the month.

In the latest blow, Donald Trump said Monday he would seek conflict compensation from Iran as part of any peace negotiations, citing attacks and killings stretching back decades allegedly backed or perpetrated by Tehran.

The US president’s announcement was a direct response to Tehran’s demand for US war reparations as a precondition to any resolution of the crisis.

Trump’s remarks came a day after he said he was “low-keying” his approach to the conflict, suggesting he was prepared to let economic pressure mount in place of further military strikes.

However, the latest back and forth risks putting a quick agreement further out of reach, and on Monday both main crude contracts jumped around five percent. They extended the gains on Tuesday.

“In the absence of any positive headlines on negotiations to reopen the strait, pressure on oil prices has been upward,” wrote Jason Wong at BNZ.

And Stephen Innes, global strategist at Quintex Intel, said: “In effect, both sides are trying to weaponise the oil barrel without firing another shot. Washington is trying to choke Iran’s ability to get its crude out, while Tehran is squeezing the artery through which everybody else’s crude gets through.

“It is quite the game of chicken.”

The prospect of oil prices remaining elevated for the time being has revived concerns over inflation and boosted the chances of interest rate increases.

While a surprise loss of more than 20,000 jobs in the US economy last month eased fears of a Federal Reserve hike, a spike in price pressures could force the bank’s hand.

Cleveland Fed boss Beth Hammack told Yahoo Finance on Monday: “I would say in general, one 25-basis-point move probably doesn’t do a whole lot for the economy.

“So it’s probably some number of (movements). But I don’t want to prejudge what that number is going to be.”

The US-Iran deadlock and rising crude costs comes as traders await the release of consumer price data on Wednesday, which could play a key role in guiding the Fed on its next move.

Asian equities were mixed following a tepid day on Wall Street.

Shanghai, Wellington, Taipei and Manila all edged down but there were gains in Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore and Seoul.

Tokyo was closed for a holiday.

World.title: One year after Putin-Trump summit, ‘spirit of Anchorage’ dissipated
World.content:
Moscow – In the year since Donald Trump hosted Vladimir Putin on US soil for a summit designed to broker an end to Russia’s offensive on Ukraine, the diplomatic initiative has fizzled out and the conflict has escalated.

For months, Russian officials talked up the “spirit of Anchorage” — a supposed climate of detente, renewed dialogue with Washington and a framework for finding a way out of the deadliest European conflict since World War II.

Now there are few traces of that atmosphere. US mediation efforts are at a standstill, both Russia and Ukraine are ramping up attacks and more civilians are being killed than at any point since the first months of the war.

– ‘Ending the war’-

On August 15, 2025, Trump broke with the West’s policy of isolating Putin, rolling out the red carpet as the Kremlin chief stepped off his plane at the Elmendorf-Richardson air base in Alaska.

It remains unclear what was decided or discussed behind closed doors.

Russia has always maintained some kind of understanding on a peace deal was struck — “a compromise proposal”, as Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov called it.

Washington has rebuffed any talk of a deal being reached.

“There was a proposal in Alaska, but there was no agreement. If there had been an agreement, we would have had an end of the war,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in June.

Moscow had hoped the summit would lay the foundations for a “lasting peace” by addressing what it calls the “root causes” of the conflict, said political analyst Sergei Markov — designated a “foreign agent” but still close to the Russian authorities.

For years — including right before launching its offensive in February 2022 — Russia has called for a new overarching security deal with the United States over Europe, NATO and arms control.

The “compromise” Russia tabled in Alaska, Markov told AFP, was to limit its territorial claims on Ukraine to the eastern Donbas region in exchange for recognition of Russia’s new borders by Washington and the lifting of sanctions.

– Disenchantment –

Those Russian demands were included in a 28-point document drafted by the United States — later cut down to 19 — after separate negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow.

The document was never published officially and never came to fruition.

US-brokered direct talks between Russia and Ukraine in early 2026 broke down, chiefly over the issue of territory.

Ukraine refuses to cede land it still controls and wants an immediate ceasefire along the current front line, with territorial status to be decided during fuller peace talks.

And since late February, Washington’s attention has been consumed by the war on Iran.

Trump has since issued fresh sanctions on Russia and the last remaining nuclear arms control agreement — New Start — has been allowed to lapse.

Having once sensed a window of opportunity to press its demands and been at pains to praise Trump’s efforts, Russia has lately allowed itself to publicly question Washington’s commitment to diplomacy.

“I don’t even want to imagine that Alaska … was conceived to gain time in order to strengthen Ukraine militarily,” Lavrov said in June.

A meeting between Lavrov and Rubio in Manila in July — their first since September 2025 — lasted only around 30 minutes.

“We’ll have to find new suggestions and new ideas” that both “Russia and Ukraine can agree to,” Rubio said after that meeting.

“That’s going to require a lot of work,” he added.

– Escalation –

The two sides’ conditions for peace are irreconcilable.

Russia demands territory alongside political and military concessions that Ukraine rejects as capitulation.

At the same time, both are convinced force can improve their negotiating position.

“The Russian armed forces will continue their mission to liberate the Donbas and Novorossiya in line with the approved plan,” Russia’s army chief Valery Gerasimov told Putin in a televised meeting in early July — referring to land stretching across eastern and southern Ukraine.

Buoyed by European support, Kyiv is banking on its long-range strike campaign to tip Russia’s economy and society over the edge.

Its attacks triggered a nationwide fuel crisis over the summer, and have forced Moscow-installed authorities to put the annexed Crimean peninsula under a local “state of emergency”.

Russia has upped its missile attacks on Kyiv, killing dozens there in recent weeks.

It has also brought Ukrainian exports through the Black Sea to a standstill through a campaign of port and ship strikes.

“The spirit of Anchorage has dissipated,” said Russian political analyst Fyodor Lukyanov — close to the ruling elite — in August.

The result? “Brutal escalation.”

World.content:

. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.

NEW DELHI: More than a year after Supreme Court ruled that residence or domicile cannot be the basis for postgraduate medical admissions under the state quota, parents of NEET-PG aspirants say admission rules still vary across states, leaving students with unequal opportunities despite having taken the same national entrance examination.The concerns stem from SCâs Jan 29, 2025, judgement in Dr Tanvi Behl vs Shrey Goel case, which held that residence-based preference in postgraduate medical admissions is not permissible. The court said admissions should be based on NEET-PG scores while allowing only limited institutional preference, meaning a student may receive preference for having graduated from a particular medical college â and not because he or she is a resident or domicile of a state.The dispute primarily concerns private medical colleges, where admissions are conducted through state counselling. Several states prescribe domicile or other state-specific eligibility conditions. âThe intention of the SC judgement was to replace residence-based preference with institutional preference. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.If these policies are challenged, the courts will decide whether they are consistent with the judgement. The Centre can still review the issue and issue uniform guidelines to states,â a health ministry official said.State counselling brochures for the NEET-PG admission process, reviewed by TOI, indeed show differences in eligibility rules. Gujarat requires additional state-specific eligibility conditions for some candidates who completed MBBS outside the state. Maharashtra allows only certain Maharashtra domicile candidates who studied outside the state to apply, while Karnataka permits candidates from other states to participate in counselling, though without Karnataka reservation benefits.Parents say these differences mean students with the same NEET-PG score may not have equal opportunity to compete for PG seats.In a representation to PMO in July, a parent sought uniform implementation of the SC judgement, a common national counselling portal and biannual NEET-PG examinations, arguing that students continue to face unequal admission opportunities across states. PMO has acknowledged the grievance, but no final decision has been communicated.Parents say the system also increases costs as candidates must register separately for multiple counselling processes, each with its own eligibility rules, timelines and security deposits. In response to one representation, NMC said domicile or residence-based reservation under state quota falls within the statesâ jurisdiction and advised the complainant to approach the state or UT concerned. A similar representation to PMO in 2022 seeking uniform rules was closed after noting the concerns.

World.title: Air India Phuket flight probe: Marijuana’s legal availability adds to worries of airlines
World.content:
Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The legal availability of marijuana for either medicinal or recreational use in places like Thailand and Amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. The reason: Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult. The only way to deter their consumption by flight crew members, say officials across multiple airlines, is to increase random dope testing, as there substances usually remain present in the body for much longer than alcohol.The concern across airlines globally to check this stems from the fact that operating a flight âunder the influence of any psychoactive substance might render (licensed personnel like pilots) unable to safely and properly exerciseâ perform their duty, as per the International Civil Aviation Organisation.Possibly the most infamous case of this was a US carrierâs off-duty pilot travelling on the jump seat (extra seat behind pilots) in the flight deck trying to shut down the engines. This off-duty pilot had reportedly taken psychedelic mushrooms two days before the incident and hadnât slept in 48 hours. âThis is a challenge globally. Often the tests are not conclusive if taking some medicine leads to detection of psychoactive substances.However, recent consumption of drugs does show up in tests,â said officials.DGCA rules on âprocedure for examination of the aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substancesâ says: âIn case the confirmatory test is found positive, the medical in charge of the organisation shall consult a medical review officer to determine if the result was due to a legitimate therapeutic treatment or some other innocuous source (for example pain relief medication containing codeine may trigger a positive result for opiates).âAirlines try to create awareness and encourage employees to anonymously report addiction so that the same can be addressed. But mostly people avoid reporting the same, so this virtually remains a non-starter, said many officials. Officials running operations across airlines say the focus in India is primarily on self-reporting and de-addiction.âBut given the easy availability of psychoactive substances, we need to make the consequences a bit tougher and act as deterrent. We have to increase random testing, thatâs the only way out,â said an official. Under DGCA rules, all scheduled commercial airlines and air navigation service providers need to test at least 10% of their flight crew members and air traffic controllers every year.

World.title: Benchmark hospital room cost against 3-star hotel tariff: Panel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A patientâs hospital room in a private hospital could soon cost no more than a room in a nearby three-star hotel if a key recommendation of the parliamentary standing committee on health and family welfare is accepted.

In an effort to rein in soaring medical bills, the panel has proposed linking room rents in private hospitals in major metropolitan cities to the average tariff charged by three-star hotels nearby.

The recommendation is part of the committeeâs report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare facilities in public and private sector, which says the absence of a transparent mechanism for fixing room charges has led to wide variations in bills.

It recommended benchmarking room rents to nearby three-star hotels, while allowing hospitals to levy separate charges for resident doctors, nursing care, consumables, meals and laundry.

Beyond room rents, the panel, headed by SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, proposed standardised package rates for common medical and surgical procedures.

Citing the 80th National Sample Survey (Jan-Dec 2025), the panel said average cost of hospitalisation was Rs 6,631 in govt hospitals compared with Rs 50,508 in private hospitals. For childbirth alone, the average out-of-pocket expenditure was Rs 37,630 in private hospitals against Rs 2,299 in govt facilities.





Hospital administrators, however, questioned the comparison. âHotel room tariffs should not be the yardstick for hospital room rents because medical infra, staffing and support services are different,â said Dr Vinoy Kumar Upadhyay, CMD of Hope Hospital in Greater Noida.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Noting the sharp difference in treatment costs, the panel said reducing out-of-pocket expenditure should be a key priority. It called for a legal mechanism to standardise and cap charges for essential treatments and routine procedures in private hospitals, mandatory disclosure of treatment costs before admission, and a fast-track grievance redressal mechanism for complaints related to billing.

Beyond room rents, the panel, headed by SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, proposed standardised package rates for common medical and surgical procedures. It also recommended advance cost estimates for complex treatments, financial navigators to guide patients on treatment costs and insurance, and âContinuum of Careâ packages covering screening, treatment and palliative care under a single capped payment. It urged the Centre to raise public health spending to 2.5% of GDP, strengthen govt hospitals, expand affordable medicines, and ensure stricter implementation of the Clinical Establishments Act.

World.title: Assessing implications of Mecca defence pact: India
World.content:
Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, accompanied by their ministers of Foreign Affairs and Defence, pose after signing a joint defence agreement in Mecca.

NEW DELHI: India continues to examine the implications of the Saudi-Pakistan-Turkiye security pact for its own security as well as regional peace and stability, said ministry of external affairs. The ministry also stressed that India remains fully committed to safeguarding its national interests and will take all necessary measures in this regard.The Mecca joint defence agreement may be designed to address West Asia dynamics but it has also led to concerns in India about possible long-term diplomatic and security challenges that it might pose for the country vis-a-vis its relations with Pakistan.The primary concern for now of course is what the pact might mean for its policy of zero tolerance against cross-border terrorism and of setting a strategic deterrence against Pakistan's support for the same, amid the likelihood of an augmentation of Pakistani military capabilities through the agreement."As far as this agreement is concerned, we are examining its implications both from the perspective of India's national security and considerations of regional peace and stability,"said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. TNN

World.title: MoPSW clears ₹335-crore flyover project at Vizag Port
World.content:
The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) has approved a ₹334.89 crore internal flyover at Visakhapatnam Port Authority to improve cargo evacuation, reduce traffic congestion and streamline movement within the port premises.

The project, approved by Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal, was appraised by the Delegated Investment Board (DIB) chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

On the occasion, Sarbananda Sonowal said: “This project will remove a critical bottleneck at Visakhapatnam Port, enabling faster cargo movement and improve overall operational efficiency. We are committed to building modern, seamless and globally competitive port infrastructure under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.”

The proposed 3.584-km elevated corridor, connecting Convent Junction with the Dock Area, will separate road and rail traffic within the port. The project is aimed at addressing delays at nine major railway level crossings, which currently see about 18 gate closures a day due to high train exchange volumes.

The frequent closures contribute to congestion, longer vehicle waiting times, higher fuel consumption and increased vehicle operating costs, affecting the efficiency of cargo evacuation. By providing an elevated road corridor, the project will enable smoother movement of vehicles and cargo while reducing conflicts between road and rail traffic. The project will include associated civil and electrical works, utility shifting, safety installations and five years of maintenance. Construction will be planned to minimise disruption to ongoing port operations, particularly in critical dock areas.

The project is scheduled for completion within 30 months of commencement.

World.title: When five DMK men were killed in a police firing at the Marina 25 years ago
World.content:
On July 29, 2001, a month after former Chief Minister and DMK president M Karunanidhi was arrested at midnight by police, who forcibly entered his Oliver Road house (since sold) in Chennai, the DMK general council passed a resolution to take out a rally on August 12, to condemn the police atrocities during the operation.

On the appointed day, the rally commenced at Little Mount in Saidapet. It was to proceed via Cathedral Road to Kamaraj Salai and end on the sands of the Marina beach where Karunanidhi was to address a meeting at the Seerani Arangam (since demolished).

Trouble began quite early in the evening. The cadres raised slogans critical of then Chief Minister Jayalalithaa and Chennai Police Commissioner K Muthukaruppan. As the rally wound its way, it turned violent near the DGP’s Office. Police resorted to a lathicharge. Journalists were also physically attacked by the men in khaki and their camera equipment broken.

Also Read | How Tamil Nadu witnessed the dramatic arrest and release of Karunanidhi and Stalin in 2001

Soon there was a clash and arson. “Four police vehicles, a bus, a jeep and two motorcycles, were set ablaze by DMK cadres. Five journalists, including The Hindu photographer, Mr. M. Moorthy, eight policemen, and about 15 DMK volunteers were admitted to hospital,” according to a report from The Hindu Archives.

The police opened fire at the crowd killing five DMK cadres [In all, six people had died.] The Marina front resembled a war zone. Karunanidhi, sensing the situation was getting out of hand, wound up his address and appealed to the cadres to leave safely.

Andhra Pradesh Governor C Ranagarajan, who was holding additional charge as Tamil Nadu Governor, flew down from Hyderabad the following day. Karunanidhi met him at Raj Bhavan (now Lok Bhavan) and submitted a memorandum saying the State had been witnessing “a reign of terror” for the past three months and on Sunday “all forms of force conceivable to human kind were unleashed” on DMK men and the media. “We had already informed Your Excellency of the diabolic design of the ruling AIADMK to disturb our rally and unleash violence on our cadre on August 11,” he said in a three-page memorandum.

A day after the firing, video footage emerged which showed a clash had taken place between the DMK cadres and some inhabitants of Ayodhyakuppan near the Marina. Some men wearing headgear and holding sickles were seen targetting the DMK cadre and video also showed scenes of the arson.

Karunanidhi told journalists the party had evidence to show streetlights went off near the DGP’s office and, taking advantage of the “darkness”, the police opened fire, aside from resorting to a lathicharge and firing tear-gas shells. “AIADMK rowdy elements” from Ayodhyakuppam went on the rampage, attacking the DMK men with knives and sickles, he charged. “All the DMK men in hospital had sustained stab injuries,” he said, asserting DMK men would not have attacked one another and it was only the handiwork of enemies.

The police firing and attack on journalists had triggered widespread political outrage. Jayalalithaa constituted a one-man Commission of Inquiry headed by Justice Bhaktavatsalam, a retired Madras High Court judge, to probe the incidents.

A year later, the Commission gave the police a clean chit saying the firing was justified. “The use of force by the police on the procession (on August 12) was the minimum required and justified,” the Commission said, in its report tabled in the Assembly.

According to the Commission, a section of the processionists, while passing through Dr. Radhakrishnan Salai, between 7 and 7.15 p.m., tried to “forcibly enter into the DGP’s office complex and committed arson, setting fire to a vehicle parked inside. As it could have set the DGP’s office complex itself afire, the police used water-cannons to disperse the mob.”

An archival report, citing the Commission’s report said, the police then burst tear-gas shells. The enraged mob started entering the DGP office complex and caused bleeding injuries to police personnel with aruval and casuarina sticks. Almost simultaneously, four members of the procession scaled the northern compound of the office and set fire to three two-wheelers parked inside. Eight persons who attacked the police and set fire to police vehicles were apprehended.

“Observing that their colleagues were being apprehended by the police personnel, the rest of the members of the unlawful assembly were greatly enraged” and, shouting that the DGP office should be set on fire, they surged towards the complex. The Commission’s report said, as the police lathicharge could not contain the mob, constable Sivakumar, after giving necessary warnings, opened, in all, seven rounds of fire, killing two processionists—Solai Perumal Murugesan and Selva Ramesh Kumar—and injuring another person (at that spot).

Also Read | When emotions overwhelmed Karunanidhi

The violent mob, on nearing Vivekanandar Illam, attempted to snatch a pistol from the Assistant Commissioner, Balasubramaniam, and attacked the Deputy Commissioner, Varadaraju. “Therefore, to scare away the violent mob, Mr. Varadaraju fired one round from his pistol. As the crowd became more violent, another Assistant Commissioner, D Kumar, ordered firing in which four persons were injured,” it said.

As for the violence near Ayodhyakuppam – behind which Karunanidhi had alleged a conspiracy by the ruling AIADMK – the Commission said when the processionists proceeded towards Seerani Arangam on the Marina, some of them threw stones, causing bleeding injuries to spectators from Ayodhyakuppam. “In order to retaliate”, at about 9 p.m., after the meeting was over, some of the Ayodhyakuppam people attacked the processionists, causing injuries to some of them, including A.P. Rangasamy, who died. “The death of Rangasamy is not the result of police action.” His body was found near the G.U. Pope statue.

At the same time, the Commission, dismissed the police’s claim that the DMK rally was taken out only to “create a law and order problem” for the AIADMK government so that the Centre might invoke Article 356 to dismiss it. “This argument is highly imaginary. After the Supreme Court verdict in the Bommai case, it is not easy for the Centre to invoke its powers under Article 356 as it likes,” the Commission said.

DMK MLA from Saidapet V Perumal, who was also general secretary of the party’s Labour Progressive Federation, had complained of giddiness during the rally. He was taken to the MLA Hostel where he fell in the bathroom. He died at a hospital later. The DMK men claimed he had complained of giddiness soon after he had witnessed the “police attack” on the rally and suffered a heart attack due to shock.

World.title: Gen Alpha students storm DM office in Hamirpur, Uttar Pradesh, over road construction
World.content:
Generation Alpha school children and residents from Chandupur in Hamirpur district, Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) marched with national flags to the district Collectorate, staging an uproar and a demonstration to demand the construction of a long-overdue road leading to their school.

The video of the protest went viral leading to an uproar on social media. The students numbered over 200 along with at least 50 parents who participated in the protest were from villages and hamlets of Chandupur gram panchayat located in the Kurara block of Hamirpur district. They raised concerns regarding the poor condition of the road leading to their school, which becomes nearly impassable during the monsoon season.

Speaking to media, students and their parents said that the local population had to rely on an unpaved road.

“In times of heavy rainfall, this route transforms into a muddy path, complicating access for students traveling to school and for residents needing to transport ill individuals to medical facilities. Additionally, an alternative route previously utilized by the community has been closed off by the Forest Department, further restricting their access to the area,” said a parent accompanying the students.

This protest marks not the first effort by the students to highlight this issue. They claimed earlier local authorities placed soil on the road as a temporary fix, after lot of efforts. “However, with the onset of rain, the road reverted to a muddy state once more,” added a student.

As the children reached the premises of the Collectorate, carrying the Tricolour and banners, local officials and police personnel reached the spot to prevent the situation from escalating. Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Abhishek Kumar and Circle Officer Yashpal Singh reached the location with police personnel and attempted to stop the students from proceeding towards the DM’s office. However, the students continued towards the office, after deliberations with officials the protestors were pacified. The Hindu attempted to speak with the District Megistrate (DM) Hamirpur, but failed to get a response.

World.title: ED arrests Bijnoriya in Nexa Evergreen money laundering case
World.content:
The Jaipur zonal office of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested an accused, Subhash Chandra Bijnoriya, in connection with a money laundering investigation related to the alleged fraud case against Nexa Evergreen, in which ₹2,676 crore were collected from a large number of investors.

Mr. Bijnoriya, one of the principal architects and operators of Nexa Evergreen Group, has been accused of carrying out fraudulent operations along with another partner in the firm. The two accused allegedly floated and operated a web of companies and proprietorship concerns in the names of associates and investors for layering and routing the proceeds of crime.

The ED arrested Mr. Bijnoriya under Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, on Monday (August 10, 2026) and produced him in a PMLA special court here, which remanded him to the custody of the financial investigation agency till August 13.

The ED launched investigation in the case on the basis of multiple first information reports and chargesheets filed by Rajasthan Police against Nexa Evergreen Group. An ED spokesperson said here that the accused had lured investors by claiming that the funds would be invested in land development and plotting projects at Dholera Smart City in Gujarat.

“Investors were induced on the promise of assured weekly returns of 3% for 60 weeks or allotment of plots, while additional commissions and rewards, including laptops, motorcycles and cars, were offered for enrolling new investors under a multi-level referral scheme,” the ED spokesperson said.

The entities floated as part of the alleged fraud and their bank accounts were systematically used for collection of investors’ funds, inter-account transfers, payment of returns to earlier investors in the nature of a Ponzi scheme, and acquisition of immovable properties, according to the ED. All of this was done while concealing the true source and ownership of funds.

The ED’s Jaipur zonal office had earlier conducted searched under Section 17 of the PMLA in June 2025 at 25 locations in Jaipur, Sikar, Jhunjhunu and Ahmedabad, which resulted in the seizure of cash amounting to Rs.2.04 crore along with various incriminating records and digital devices.

An amount of ₹15 crore lying in the bank accounts and crypto accounts linked with various Nexa Group entities and associates were also frozen, according to the ED.

World.title: Congress will corner Haryana government over rising crime, tax burden in Assembly session
World.content:
Former Haryana Chief Minister and the Leader of Opposition in Assembly, Congress’s Bhupinder Singh Hooda, on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) said the party would corner the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in the monsoon session of the State Assembly over poor law and order, rising organised crime and tax hikes based on property tax and collector rates in the State.

“We will submit a calling attention motion during the assembly session, to seek answers from the government regarding the breakdown of law and order, rising organized crime and tax hikes based on property tax and collector rates,” said Mr. Hodda, addressing a press conference in Chandigarh.

He said the Congress MLAs will also move motions in the Assembly to raise issues surrounding waterlogging in urban and rural areas due to rains, compensation for farmers, demands of electricity department employees, the privatisation of power services in Gurugram and the grievances of guest teachers, sanitation workers and other staff.

“The Congress would move an ‘adjournment motion’ as well to discuss the alleged scams involving IDFC Bank, AU Small Finance Bank, etc in the session,” he said.

Mr. Hooda accused the BJP government for being insensitive towards farmers. “The government has failed to lift the full stock of urea and other fertilizers allocated to Haryana by the Centre. The Centre had allocated 9.59 lakh metric tonnes of urea to Haryana up to August, yet the government has lifted only 8.14 lakh metric tonnes. Similarly, 2.53 lakh metric tonnes of di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) were allocated, yet the government lifted only 1.15 lakh metric tonnes. This implies the government intends for farmers to face hardship by having to stand in long queues for fertilizer,” he said.

On the issue of Sutlej-Yamuna Link (SYL) canal, the center of a decades-long water-sharing dispute between Punjab and Haryana, Mr. Hooda said, “The incumbent Chief Minister of Haryana remains frequently active in Punjab, yet never raises the matter of the SYL canal while he is there. Ministers from the Centre regularly visit and announce decisions regarding the transfer of water from Haryana to Rajasthan via pipeline, but no one speaks about securing Haryana’s rightful share of water from Punjab.”

Mr. Hooda announced that the Congress party will hold a protest demonstration on August 19 regarding the demand for the regularisation of ‘Haryana Kaushal Rozgar Nigam’ workers and other issues. “During the 2024 assembly elections, the BJP had announced the regularisation of 125,000 ‘Kaushal’ workers to garner their votes. However, even after nearly two years, these contractual employees have not received any law or official notification regarding their regularisation,” he alleged.

World.title: Chandigarh body seeks Vice-Presidents’ help to halt auction of Panjab University heritage furniture in U.S.
World.content:
Chandigarh Administration’s Heritage Items Protection Cell on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) sought urgent intervention from Vice-President and Panjab University (PU) Chancellor C.P. Radhakrishnan to stop the proposed auction of heritage furniture items associated with Panjab University, to be held in the U.S. on August 13.

In a letter to the Vice-President, advocate Ajay Jagga, who is a member of HIPC, has asserted that heritage items belonging to Panjab University had been listed for sale by a Chicago-based auction house, which includes a set of eight dining chairs, described as student residence chairs of PU, with an estimated price of $12,000-$15,000. Besides, there’s a writing chair from PU, with an estimated price of $3,000-$4,000.

“As a premier national institution, Panjab University has a corresponding moral and institutional responsibility to safeguard its own heritage. Therefore, the Panjab University should immediately lodge a formal objection to the proposed auction scheduled for August 13, 2026 in the United States, in which two items belonging to Panjab University are proposed to be auctioned. Such timely intervention may help prevent the alienation of India’s institutional heritage and chances of bringing it back and reaffirm the nation’s commitment to preserving its cultural legacy for future generations,” he wrote in the letter.

Pointing out that it was astonishing to learn who sold Panjab University’s articles in violation of the Constitution of India, and who took them to the U.S. for sale, he said “There is an urgent need to stop this auction or at least put it on hold. Beyond doing our best to reclaim our heritage items, we also need a probe into how, why and by whom the heritage of Panjab University was sold, despite a ban by the Ministry of Home Affairs.”

Mr. Jagga said the representation has been filed in accordance with Article 51A(f) of the Constitution, which calls upon citizens to value and preserve India’s rich cultural heritage, and Article 49, which relates to protection of monuments, places and objects of national importance.

World.title: Maharashtra snake bite deaths: Fadnavis orders cancellation of licence of tribal residential school
World.content:
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) ordered that the licence of the residential tribal school, where three girls died due to snake bite, be cancelled permanently. The administration said that it was in the process of issuing a notice regarding the matter. The CM also said that the official who had inspected the school earlier and had submitted a report, should be placed under suspension.

Maharashtra Tribal Affairs Minister Ashok Uike is learnt to have said in the Cabinet meeting on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) that the government should take strict action against the private organisation which receives government aid to run the residential school for tribal girls.

“The tribal residential schools need to be inspected properly. Instead of looking at only such schools which are on the main roads, the schools in the interior areas too need to be inspected properly. This school had no teacher, no warden. No facilities were provided though this school received government aid,” the CM is learnt to have said during the meeting.

Meanwhile, a 14-year-old girl continued to be critical and remained under treatment. Another girl, 11, is stable, district health officials told The Hindu. Officials said that the snake bit five girls, and not six, as reported earlier in the media. Several girls felt scared and said they had symptoms like stomach ache and vomiting. “They were all admitted and later discharged after found to be stable,” Dr. Pratap Shinde, District Health Officer, Gadchiroli, told The Hindu.

The incident took place in the intervening night between August 9 and August 10. approximately between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m.. At the residential tribal school for girls in Japtalai in Dhanora taluka, some girls were sleeping on the floor in a large hall. The total number of girls in the tribal school is 233.

Political reactions

The Opposition slammed the government and asked that the culprits be booked for culpable homicide. “This is a murder by the system,” NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut asked how the girls could die of a snake bite in Maharashtra. The BJP said that the school was being run by the organisation owned by Congress leader Marotrao Kowase, who was an MLA for three terms and an MP for one term.

World.title: Security stepped up, anti-terror ops launched ahead of Independence Day in J&K
World.content:
Multiple anti-militancy operations were launched in parts of J&K on Tuesday (August 11, 2026), as security was heightened ahead of the Independence Day in the Union Territory (UT).

Officials said an anti-militancy operation was initiated in Poonch’s Mendhar Sector after a security guard spotted suspected movement near an under-construction tunnel, connecting the Pir Panjal valley with Kashmir.

Officials said the security guards opened three to four rounds “as a precautionary measure”. Security forces cordoned off the jungles of Bhata Dhurian and Sangiot after the incident.

In the Chenab valley, security forces launched another anti-terror operation after locals reported movement of terrorists in upper reaches. Officials said locals suspected movement of four terrorists at Ramtund area of Bhaderwah, Doda. Acting on the tip-off, the security forces have launched an operation to trace the hiding terrorists.

In the Kashmir valley, frisking and searches of vehicles and markets were intensified throughout the day. Major markets like Lal Chowk in Srinagar saw security forces conducting searches of hotels and shops, as part of the stepped-up security.

A purported online threat to Pandits has left security forces on tenterhooks. Officials said Kashmiri Pandits working in the Kashmir valley were allowed to go on leave till August 20, in the wake of the online threats by a little-known outfit United Liberation Council. The J&K police were looking into the online threats, apparently emanating from across the border.

Inspector General of Police, Kashmir Zone, V. K. Birdi assessed the security situation in Srinagar and took stock of “multi-layered security arrangements”.

“For the main function on August 15 in Srinagar, all the security arrangements and preparations for the parade are going on. Security arrangements were not confined to the main venue but had been extended across Srinagar city and all districts of the Valley,” said IGP Birdi.

On twin targeted killings by terrorist of a policeman and two non-locals since July 22, IGP Birdi the incidents were being investigated. “It is appropriate to reveal it,” he added.

World.title: Investigators say chemical, DNA reports not ‘conclusive’ enough to determine direction of Mir Raza Ali probe
World.content:
Investigators probing the murder of young business owner Mir Raza Ali on Tuesday received the chemical examiner’s report and one DNA report, but said the findings were not yet “conclusive” enough to determine the direction of the investigation, Dawn has learnt.

Owner of eatery Wafflix, Ali had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

Investigators are also awaiting the findings of other samples and the police surgeon’s final report in light of the laboratory findings.

The DNA report confirmed the identity of the deceased, ruling out theories circulating on social media that someone else might have been killed.

Informed sources told Dawn that the chemical analysis of samples taken during the first post-mortem examination had revealed three key findings. First, it confirmed the presence of gunshot residue on the back of the perforation in the deceased’s shirt, indicating an entry wound. Second, traces of acid were found on his shirt. Third, the chemical examiner’s report detected bupivacaine, an anaesthetic and painkiller, in his blood.

The sources said several samples had been collected during the exhumation of the body, carried out around 12 days after his death on a court’s order following an application by the family.

Meanwhile, the sources said the investigation team formed by Sindh IGP Javed Odho and headed by DIG Crime and Investigation Amir Farooqi had decided to conduct geofencing in areas surrounding the crime scene to detect the possible movements of pedestrians and people travelling in cars or on motorcycles.

The team would also obtain the call data record of the victim’s mobile phone, they said.

Moreover, on the request of the family’s lawyer, Jibran Nasir, two new members — DSP Siraj Lashari of Hyderabad and Karachi South police inspector Mohammed Ali — had been included in the investigation team.

They also said the chemical examiner’s report detected traces of acid on the victim’s shirt, but there were no acid burns on his body. Similarly, the presence of painkillers in his body did not suggest that he had been administered an anaesthetic before being killed.

The sources said investigators were still “confused” about the entry and exit wounds caused by the gunshot, which had generated considerable debate. According to them, the first post-mortem report showed a bullet wound on the chest from the front, while the second report suggested that he had been shot from behind.

They said there was a 38mm wound on the chest, along with burn marks on the shirt, while the wound on the back was 7mm in size and showed no signs of burns on the shirt.

“We are not challenging anything at this stage, but there is still confusion among investigators,” a source familiar with the investigation said.

The sources further added that the victim’s kitchen was located in the same area where his body was found, but it had been closed at the time of his death.

Meanwhile, the secretary of the investigation team and SSP RRF Mohammed Ali Raza, along with other investigators, visited the crime scene. The complainant, the victim’s father Mir Husain, and the family’s lawyer, Jibran Nasir, also joined them.

‘Neither depressed nor deprived’

Speaking to the media, Nasir alleged that the deceased’s only digital footprint, his smartwatch, had remained in the possession of SSP SIU Samiullah Soomro for eight days without any memo, which he said amounted to manipulation of evidence.

“Ali had deleted applications from his phone; his only digital footprint was his smartwatch. However, SSP Soomro kept it with himself for eight days and distributed information extracted from it to the media,” he said. “Isn’t this criminal conduct by SSP Soomro?”

The lawyer alleged that police had taken the smartwatch from the family a couple of days after the killing but had not prepared any memo for it, which he said demonstrated the officers’ lack of sincerity.

Jibran said Ali had remained missing for around 12 hours after he was last seen and had allegedly been subjected to torture during that period before his death.

“After finding acid on his clothes, we fear that he may have been forced to consume acid,” the lawyer said.

“He was neither depressed nor deprived. He was martyred and oppressed,” he said, warning the police and government against treating the death as a suicide.

He criticised the Sindh government for including East SSP Zubair Nazir Sheikh in the initial investigation team, alleging that the Sindh High Court had ordered an inquiry against the officer over a Rs500 million extortion allegation.

“The Sindh government included such people in the investigation team,” he said.

Nasir also alleged that another officer on the initial team, SP Usman Sadozai, had been in Azad Jammu and Kashmir for the past two weeks and had not returned to Karachi. He questioned how the officer had been attending meetings of the investigative committee.

Nasir further criticised the Gulistan-i-Jauhar police for failing to notice the acid and other evidence and initially portraying the death as a suicide.

He alleged that efforts were being made to protect someone he described as “powerful, brutal and oppressive”.

The lawyer alleged that Ali’s killers were professionals who had tried to conceal his identity by pouring acid on his face and thumbs and setting the crime scene on fire.

He said it was possible that Rs300 million had been debited from Ali’s account by someone to portray it as a financial loss and create the impression that he had committed suicide after suffering a heavy loss.

Nasir said he had met the new investigation team along with the deceased’s family and had also visited the crime scene on Tuesday.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs1.70, raises high-speed diesel by Rs1.39
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs1.70 and increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.39 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs325.92 per litre while HSD will cost Rs382.25 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 12.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Man shot dead on Rawalpindi's Mall Road after 'opening fire' on security personnel
World.content:
A man, whom police claimed was affiliated with a “particular political party”, was shot dead by law enforcement officials on Rawalpindi’s Mall Road on Tuesday after he allegedly opened fire on security forces, injuring an official.

“The attacker, Muhammad Hussain, was immediately killed in retaliatory fire,” said a statement by Rawalpindi police.

The police added that evidence and “links have emerged from his mobile phone and other belongings”, adding that further investigation is ongoing.

“Law enforcement agencies remain fully prepared and committed to eliminating all forms of terrorism and incitement to unrest,” police said.

PTV News, quoting security sources, said the alleged assailant was a resident of Khyber district and an “active PTI member”. A PTI flag, bullets and weapons were also allegedly recovered from him, the report added.

In a statement aired on news channels following the incident, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar slammed PTI’s “politics of violence” after state media reported the incident.

Visuals of a red and green cloth, a gun, and bullets allegedly recovered from the alleged attacker were also televised by PTV News and during Tarar’s video statement.

The information minister said there was “no reason for opening fire on security personnel”, later confirming the incident location as Rawalpindi’s Mall Road.

Tarar also slammed the “politics of violence adopted by the PTI” and criticised its members for “coming equipped with weapons”.

The minister referred to the call for a long march to Islamabad, which has been announced by the PTI for September 27. He claimed that it was “on record that they always come armed at all their protests, open fire on security personnel and martyr them”.

“They do not believe in a peaceful protest, and today, the entire nation has witnessed their nefarious aims and objectives,” Tarar asserted, noting that the security personnel were targeted “in public in broad daylight”.

“This is their ideology; they believe in violence and such incidents. The PTI has always done politics of violence, and not a single one of their protests has been peaceful,” Tarar alleged.

Noting that a PTI flag and “other documents” were recovered from the alleged attacker in today’s incident, he claimed that the PTI’s aim was only to “spread anarchy in the country and ruin the law and order”.

The minister stressed that the PTI’s announcement of a long march came right after Pakistan was praised internationally after signing a joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
